News.title: Trump backs down on taxpayer funded ads and now says his PAC will pay for them
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

President Donald Trump announced Monday that his political action committee will take over funding for a series of national television s that had previously been paid for with government funds.

The decision follows growing criticism over the spots, which were financed through a $20 million Department of Homeland Security contract awarded on September 20 to LMD Agency. According to public records first reported by The Washington Sun, the White House Office of Management and Budget had transferred $20 million to Customs and Border Protection for “OBBB Commemorative Events” a day prior.

Data from ad-tracking firm AdImpact shows that more than $10 million in taxpayer money has been spent on the campaign since September, with ads appearing across both cable and broadcast networks bearing the disclaimer “Paid for by the U.S. Government.”

The broadcasts spanned multiple themes, CBS News reported, including one spot featuring Trump stating, “We will defeat communism, socialism and Marxism in America,” over flashing photos of the president, and another recounting the U.S. capture of former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro.

Another made the declaration: “God made Trump.”

open image in gallery Donald Trump criticized opponents who objected to using public funds for the national broadcast campaign, calling the promotional spots ‘a rather standard thing to do’ ( AFP/Getty )

Critics from both parties raised concerns that the campaign violated federal restrictions against using public funds for propaganda or promotional purposes. Observers noted that at least one spot included video clips previously featured in a 2024 Trump campaign .

In a letter last month, a group of Senate Democrats condemned the effort, writing: “This is the sort of government propaganda one might expect in North Korea, not the United States of America, and it is an egregious and illegal misuse of Americans’ hard-earned tax dollars.”

Republicans also voiced concern.

“I don’t think any public official, including President Trump or Kristi Noem or John Kennedy, should spend public money on private ads for themselves,” GOP Senator John Kennedy of Louisiana said on “Face the Nation.”

The White House repeatedly defended the campaign, insisting the spots were public service announcements rather than political promotion.

A White House official stated last month that the spots “are clearly not political,” adding: “The President is not on the ballot and the ads don’t have a call to action.”

open image in gallery Taxpayer-funded ads featuring Trump, military imagery and glowing praise are airing nationwide ahead of the midterms, including one that claims ‘God made Trump’ ( White House )

A White House spokesperson further described the anti-communism ad as “educational and unapologetically patriotic. We should be proud of our country.”

Trump acknowledged the criticism surrounding the campaign Monday on Truth Social.

“The Radical Left is upset with the fact that I am taking Ads, which I consider to be a positive promotion for our Great U.S.A., and paying for them with U.S.A. money,” he wrote. “This is a rather standard thing to do but, rather than doing that, although nothing will make them happy, I have decided to do the Patriotic Ads, among others, and pay for them myself, and with money I raised for MAGA, Inc.”

The move marks a shift from comments made just days prior.

open image in gallery ( AP )

Speaking to reporters in the Oval Office, Trump defended the original funding source, arguing that the broadcasts were intended to promote the nation rather than a candidate, as reported by The New York Times. During those remarks, however, he noted that he would gladly cover the expenses if the arrangement was deemed improper.

Over the weekend, The New York Times reported that Trump had directly instructed his budget director to allocate public funds for the television spots.

The super PAC financing the transition possesses substantial capital to absorb the costs. According to AdImpact, MAGA Inc. entered September with roughly $415 million on hand and, together with two affiliated super PACs, has reserved approximately $194 million for upcoming advertising.

However, diverting super PAC funds to cover the ads uses money Republican strategists had hoped to direct toward key midterm contests, such as the Texas Senate race.

Trump previously said that he is “going to spend whatever amount of money necessary to try and help us.”

News.title: Tories promise to scrap Labour’s mansion tax
News.content:
The Tories have pledged to scrap Labour’s “mansion tax” on homes worth more than £2m.

Andrew Griffith, the shadow chancellor, pledged to abolish the “vindictive levy” in his keynote speech to the Conservative Party conference, warning it would hit people living in “ordinary homes”.

Under the tax, which was announced by Labour last year, properties valued at more than £2m face an extra levy on their council tax from 2028.

The shadow chancellor said: “They pretend it’s a mansion tax, but it will hit people here in Birmingham, in Manchester, and those living in ordinary homes making long commutes to our capital city. For many, it will be simply unaffordable.”

He pledged to follow in the footsteps of Nigel Lawson, Margaret Thatcher’s chancellor, and cut one tax at every Budget if the his party returns to power.

Elsewhere in his speech, Mr Griffith promised to scrap a net zero “grocery tax” which pushes up the cost of the weekly shop and cut the cost of a new build by £50,000.

The shadow chancellor also accused previous Tory leaders of failing to govern as free market conservatives, and said Andy Burnham and John Healey want to take Britain back to a “socialist fever dream of the 1970s”.

News.title: How worried should we be about the Russian plague lab leak?
News.content:
Russian media says 200 people are being quarantined. How likely is it that the disease could now spread?

Experts say the risk from this particular bacterium is low.

It can be treated with antibiotics and – although its possible others have been exposed – it seems unlikely it will spread far. The pneumonic form of the disease is spread by droplets and prolonged direct and close contact is required for the disease to spread.

Brendan Wren, professor of microbial pathogenesis at the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, said the disease was less transmissible than Covid.

“Plague is still endemic in many parts the world, including western parts of the US, so there shouldn’t be too much concern as the transmission of Yersinia pestis between humans is generally poor.”

The incubation period of pneumonic plague is short – just a day in some cases – so if no one else falls in within the next week, the likelihood of sustained transmission is low.

What is plague exactly?

Plague is caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis and is transmitted via rats and other small rodents.

The bubonic form of the disease – known as the Black Death when it spread throughout Europe in the Middle Ages – is characterised by swollen nymph nodes and has a 30 to 60 per cent mortality rate. This is the more common form of plague.

The pneumonic form of the disease is almost always fatal if left untreated. However, antibiotics are effective against it so early diagnosis and treatment is essential. But drug resistant forms of the disease are emerging.

Plague is endemic in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Madagascar, and is also present in some parts of the United States, including Arizona and New Mexico, where according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention there are an average of seven cases a year.

News.title: Extreme heat is increasing risks for pregnant women and babies, experts warn
News.content:
Soaring temperatures are increasing birth complications and defects in newborns, a new report has warned.

The report, which surveyed 1,000 doctors and midwives, found that at least 73 per cent of healthcare workers across Australia, Brazil, Britain, India and Zimbabwe had seen an uptick in heat-related complications in pregnancy and birth.

High temperatures can cause surface-level blood vessels to dilate, which in pregnant women can significantly decrease blood flow to the placenta and reduce oxygen and nutrients reaching the foetus.

This phenomenon can increase the risk of stillbirth, premature births, and low birth weight, the report, released by the Wellcome Trust, said.

Heat can also make it hard for newborn babies, whose bodies are already extremely fragile, to regulate their internal temperatures – which can significantly impact both their ability to breathe properly and feed from their mothers.

Extreme heat can also severely affect the health of a pregnant woman, placing heavy demands on the cardiovascular system and inadvertently increasing the risk of gestational diabetes, dangerously high blood pressure, and pre-eclampsia.

The effects are more severe on women who live in places where temperatures are newly or rapidly increasing, as opposed to women who have always lived in hot climates and whose bodies have acclimatised to the heat over time.

Insufferable heat can also impact women’s access to critical healthcare during pregnancy.

More than a quarter of healthcare workers surveyed by Wellcome said they had seen first-hand how fewer women travel to hospitals and clinics during heat waves, particularly in the developing world where millions access healthcare on foot.

The world experienced its hottest August on record in 2026, when the average global surface air temperature reached 16.96 degrees Celsius – roughly 1.65 degrees above pre-industrial levels.

Britain also saw its hottest summer since records began, with five heatwaves recorded over the course of just 40 days, and temperatures reaching 38 degrees in some parts of the country.

A Wellcome-funded project studying pregnant women in Wales, known as MAGENTA, has found that women in the UK have experienced negative birth outcomes as a result of the persistent heat.

Initial research has linked exposure to elevated temperatures exceeding 25 degrees with higher rates of premature births and stillbirths. A 1-degree increase in heat exposure can boost the chances of a preterm birth by around 5 per cent, the research found.

Climate change has been identified by the World Health Organization (WHO) as the greatest threat to global public health.

Between 2030 and 2050, experts project climate change will cause an additional 250,000 deaths every year.

The deaths will be due mostly to heat stress, malnutrition, and an increase in the prevalence of infectious diseases like malaria, which is spreading into new areas where mosquitoes can now more easily survive and spread disease, according to the WHO.

Dr Madeline Thomson, head of climate impacts and adaptation at Wellcome, said: “Extreme heat, fuelled by climate change, is impacting our way of life and our health - and yet many countries are not prepared. With El Niño pushing temperatures higher, the failure to act is costing lives.

“We already know many of the solutions to protect people - from early warning systems to cooler buildings.

“But the challenge is providing solutions to those who need them most, including pregnant women and newborns, who face serious risks but often receive inadequate information and support.”

News.title: ‘The dogs were eating their bodies’: Thousands of Yemenis flee war across the sea
News.content:
The Houthi militiamen had barely chased the government forces out of Alia Mohammad’s coastal village when the bombing began in a Saudi-backed attempt to recapture it.

Caught in the middle were Ms Mohammad, her family and their neighbours near the town of Dhubab, overlooking the Bab el-Mandeb strait, or ‘Gate of Tears’.

As the roar of planes split the sky over their heads and explosions shook their village, it took little time for them to decide what to do.

Born from generations of fishermen, they resolved to take to the sea and flee their homes in Yemen, to seek refuge across the strait in Djibouti.

More than 4,000 Yemeni refugees have arrived in the coastal Djibouti town of Obock in the past month, fleeing an offensive which has redrawn Yemen’s battle lines and strengthened Tehran’s hand in the Middle East energy crisis.

The offensive last month saw the Iranian-backed Houthi advance around 90 miles along the Red Sea coast in a 48-hour blitz that delivered what analysts have called the most consequential shift in Yemen’s front lines in years.

News.title: This is when to upgrade your tech (and when not to bother)
News.content:
The tech giants’ attempts to persuade people to upgrade to new gadgets every two years are proving less and less effective. According to YouGov polling, Brits are increasingly deciding to stick with the devices they have for longer, and it isn’t altogether surprising.

As well as the inherent wastefulness of the bi-annual upgrade cycle, year-on-year improvements are less dramatic than they used to be, and tech prices are sky-rocketing thanks to the growing needs of AI data centres.

Inevitably, however, there will come a time when you need to bite the bullet and buy a new model. These are the questions to ask yourself to decide whether that should be today, or whether you can kick the can a little further down the road.

How’s the performance?

A good place to start is to evaluate how your device functions day-to-day versus the day you bought it. Tech inevitably slows down over time, but the drop isn’t equal among devices: a five-year-old flagship smartphone may still outperform a budget model from last year.

If it’s still running smoothly enough, and isn’t broken in an unfixable way, then it probably pays to wait until it no longer passes this test. The longer you wait, the more appealing the upgrade choices will be.

The exception to this is if you’re bumping up against storage problems. If there’s no way to add more, and cloud storage isn’t cutting it, then you may need to upgrade early.

News.title: Jibulu emerges as England World Cup bolter in Sale defeat of Saracens
News.content:
Could Nathan Jibulu, the Sale Sharks hooker, emerge as a bolter for England’s World Cup squad? With Steve Borthwick, the England head coach, watching from the stands, the 23-year-old produced the kind of “wrecking-ball” performance in this surprise victory for the North West side that suggested he is on course to do so.

After their tame defeat by Bristol Bears in the opening round, few had predicted that Alex Sanderson’s side had much hope against Saracens, who were looking to back up their impressive win at Welford Road last weekend. But Jibulu’s powerhouse display on either side of the ball typified their stout and physical resistance, backed up by a masterly display by George Ford.

Given the age and injury profile of England hookers Jamie George and Luke Cowan-Dickie, who both missed this contest, and the fact that Theo Dan has yet to make a forceful challenge for the position in the national side, Sanderson is in no doubt that Jibulu has the X factor required to break into Borthwick’s squad this season.

“This is the player that any time you watch him play, he impacts – he takes metres either side of the ball – and we knew that he had that in him,” Sanderson said.

“It shows he’s of international class. He nailed his line-outs, on the back of that he was a wrecking-ball runner causing havoc around the field.

“This is the person that we knew, this is the player that we knew we had in him. It could be the year where he explodes onto the international scene. I hope it is, but it’s early days.

“He’s that quality, he’s that kind of an athlete. You can get away with being fast and skilful in the Prem, but it’s another level again in terms of the power that’s required at international level. And he’s got that ability, he’s immensely strong.”

Borthwick will have left the StoneX Stadium on Sunday evening with a full notebook. Ben Bamber, Sale’s 6ft 9ins lock, has also been attracting his interest and it was Bamber who crossed for the decisive try, Sale’s third, hitting a great line off Ford to finish like an outside centre.

News.title: Brilliant Hamilton storms to podium despite another Ferrari blunder
News.content:
One of the big talking points heading into the weekend has been the cooling vests drivers wear under their overalls (as opposed to the jacket-like ones they wear when they’re out of their cars). Russell told us in our Brits media session on Thursday that Mercedes had decided to forego the vests here, since the technology was not yet refined. The system works by pumping a coolant through thin tubes stitched into the vest.

Drivers have complained that the connecting valve to the pump, which was originally placed on the side of the vest, proved uncomfortable when combined with the high G-forces experienced in an F1 car. On some vests the connector has been moved to find a more comfortable position, but the thick material and tubing have also proved cumbersome under the driver’s fireproof overalls. There are also concerns over the reliability of some systems and the possibility that a failure will mean the vest will have the opposite effect and work as a heat insulator.preferring to spend that money instead on car upgrades. The money to develop the vests comes out of the budget cap.

But Russell added that the FIA should make the tech mandatory and develop it themselves, describing this race as like being in a “sauna”.The Briton’s comments prompted a sarcastic response from Verstappen - who doesn’t wear the vests either, out of choice - who said Russell “shouldn’t make a fuss”.

“I don’t need it,” Verstappen said. “Maybe I suffer a bit less from the heat.. I find a Finnish sauna at 85 degrees a lot hotter... You shouldn’t make a fuss. Yes, it is hot, but that’s part of it. You have to train for that.”

The Dutchman added: “When I was 18, I had a bit more trouble with these conditions. But after that, I started training more in the heat, such as in the sauna and a steam room, so that I can handle the sweating better and the fact that your head gets very hot. Maybe I should take him (Russell) to the sauna a few times.”

These two have history, of course. They’ve sniped at each other for years. In 2024, in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, it reached a peak when Verstappen described Russell as being “two-faced” and said he had lost all respect for him. Russell responded by saying Verstappen was “a bully”. Earlier this year, the Mercedes driver said Verstappen could always retire from the sport and drive sports cars if he didn’t like the regs.

News.title: Rees-Zammit taunts Pollock as Bristol outplay Northampton
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Bristol Bears vs Northampton Saints from the Gallagher Prem, with both teams looking to build on winning starts following the opening weekend of action.

Last season’s champions Northampton kicked off their title defence with an emphatic 59-26 victory over a new-look Newcastle Red Bulls outfit at Franklin’s Gardens.

While Henry Pollock’s new cornrow hairstyle was the centre of attention at kick-off, the limelight was soon stolen by Tommy Freeman and James Pater, who both notched hat-tricks for Phil Dowson’s side.

Of 19-year-old full-back Pater, who starts on the bench today, Dowson said afterwards: “He doesn’t let the occasion get to him. He has an incredible skill set, great speed and ability to manoeuvre away from defenders.”

Bristol, meanwhile, began their season with an impressive 34-24 victory away at Sale Sharks, with Pat Lam’s side ensuring Courtney Lawes’s return to the English game was a disappointing one.

Louis Rees-Zammit was operating in his favoured wing position and got Bristol off to a strong start with two tries in the opening 23 minutes, offering Lam hope of a fruitful campaign from the Welshman.

“When you look at our wingers in the past, they scored a lot of tries and Louis is a world-class finisher,” the Bristol director of rugby said. “You get the ball to him in space and you create the opportunity, there’s a good chance he’ll finish it.”

Northampton will be hoping for a repeat of the meeting between the sides at Franklin Gardens in May when they thumped Bristol 94-33, but they have not won at Ashton Gate since 2021.

Both teams have made a pair of changes following their opening-weekend victories, with England international Ellis Genge among the players to drop out after spraining his wrist against Sale.

Sports.title: Chelsea ace Moises Caicedo fined and hit with eight points for driving £160k supercar without valid licence
Sports.content:
Next

CHELSEA ace Moises Caicedo has been fined and hit with eight points for driving his £160,000 supercar without a valid licence or insurance.

The Ecuadorian, 24, was pulled over in his Audi RSQ8 near the club’s training ground in Cobham, Surrey.



The Premier League star – once Britain’s most expensive footballer – was convicted of driving without a license and no insurance.

Midfielder Caicedo, said to earn £250,000 a week, was fined £1,444 at Crawley magistrates’ court.



He also got eight penalty points for the April 2025 offences, placing him close to a ban.

He joined the Blues from Brighton in 2023 for a then-British record fee of £115million.

He has played just 14 minutes this season owing to injury.

Chelsea FC last year said the issue was a personal matter.

His brush with the law raised questions over whether other foreign footballers may also be driving without the correct documents.

On March 31 last year, he was seen at the wheel of the Audi — which can do 155mph and reach 60mph in 3.8 seconds — leaving Chelsea’s training ground in Cobham, Surrey.



Caicedo, who has 65 international caps, is the youngest of ten siblings and often visits his home town of Santo Domingo in Ecuador where he plays football with locals.

He won the UEFA Conference League and the FIFA Club World Cup in 2025.

PIERS MORGAN has lifted the lid on why Cristiano Ronaldo dramatically quit the Portugal camp after manager Jorge Jesus “pulled a Ten Hag”.

Ronaldo, 41, could never play for his nation again after his dramatic falling out with Jesus, who he also worked with at Al-Nassr.



Jesus reportedly went back on his promises to Ronaldo regarding playing arrangements over the international break before the country’s record appearance- maker and goalscorer returned home.

The former Manchester United ace was left as an unused sub against Norway despite being asked to warm up.



Taking to social media, Ronaldo said he would speak publicly about the events of the rift in “due time”.

SunSport columnist and TalkTV host Morgan was the man Ronaldo turned to for a bombshell interview when he quit Manchester United.

That interview ended up being a massive attack against the club’s stagnation and manager Erik ten Hag, who had relegated Ronaldo to the bench.

And Morgan, 61, now reckons Jesus is doing the same, and lifted the lid on what he understood to have caused the problems between them.

Speaking on his Piers Morgan Uncensored show, he started off by bringing up a quote from Carlo Ancelotti when talking about Luka Modric, where he said you don’t warm up a player of that stature and not bring him on.

Morgan compared it to the current Ronaldo case, saying: “It’s nothing to do with money, fame or any of those things. He was given absolute guarantees about how he would be used.

“The coach apologised to him and repeated that apology to the president and said he would go out and explain this shouldn’t have happened.

“What he does is the opposite and pulls a Ten Hag, he goes out and tries to belittle and embarrass Ronaldo, put him back in his box, say all the players are important to me blah, blah, blah, which also pisses off Ronaldo.”



Morgan continued: “Then he goes to Ronaldo and says, ‘I know we would rest you the second two games but I want you for 30 minutes against Norway, and he goes, ‘Okay, if that’s what you want I’ll do it.’

Sports.title: Luke Littler names shock all-time Man Utd XI and admits he’d rather see them win treble than land another world title
Sports.content:
Next

LUKE LITTLER has named his all-time Manchester United Premier League IX – but there is no room for the current manager.

The Nuke, born and bred in Warrington, has been a loyal United fan all his life.



And in discussion with former United midfielder Paul Scholes on the The Good, The Bad & The Football podcast, the two-time world darts champion put together his Red Devils Dream Team.

The starting line-up was made up of players that the 19-year-old had watched play at Old Trafford in his lifetime.



In goal, he went for Spaniard David de Gea, a mainstay in Manchester for 12 years, but someone who overcame a lot of stick when he first moved to English football.

At full-back, he went for Ecuadorian Antonio Valencia on the right (“very good”) and Frenchman Patrice Evra on the left.

At centreback, Littler said “he’d put Rio (Ferdinand) and (Nemanja) Vidic in there”.

He has always been a huge fan of Marcus Rashford (“I’ve watched Rashford since his first game”) and he would go with the England star on the left-hand side of midfield.

Amad Diallo, the Ivory Coast winger, would be his choice on the right.

Michael Carrick, the boss of United since January, was an accomplished midfielder in his day.

During his time at the club he was the winner of five Premier Leagues, one FA Cup, three League Cups, the Champions League, Europa League and FIFA Club World Cup.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Though Scholes suggested Carrick as a viable option in central midfield, Littler, however, went for Portuguese leader Bruno Fernandes and Frenchman Paul Pogba.

Littler laughed: “There’s got to be someone better than Michael Carrick.”

Up front, he went for obvious choices – Cristiano Ronaldo and Wayne Rooney, two of the finest players to don the famous red shirt.



Scholes – winner of 11 Premier League titles – went for Peter Schmeichel in goal and a defence of Gary Neville (right-back), Denis Irwin (left-back) and Rio Ferdinand and Jaap Stam (centre-backs).

In an old school 4-4-2 formation, Scholes, 51, plumped for a midfield quartet of Ryan Giggs (left), Valencia (right), and then Roy Keane and Carrick in central positions.

In attack, Scholes chose Dutchman Ruud van Nistelrooy and Wayne Rooney.

Scholes argued: “I’m going to leave Cristiano out. Because how long did I play with Cristiano?

“Maybe three or four years. I played with Wayne a lot longer. I’ll bring Cristiano out with 20 minutes to go.



“Imagine somebody saying that now. F***ing hell. What is wrong with you?”

Littler, winner of the past two world darts titles, would happily swap another Sid Waddell Trophy if it meant he was able to watch United win the Treble for a second time.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Just like his dad Anthony did in 1999 when Sir Alex Ferguson’s side, with Scholes in the team, won the Premier League, FA Cup and then Champions League.

Littler, born in January 2027, said: “I think I’d say United won another treble. My dad witnessed the treble, I didn’t.”

Sports.title: Mark Chapman and Kelly Cates’ secret romance leaves Match of the Day colleagues stunned as ‘NO ONE knew it was going on’
Sports.content:
Next

THE romance of Match of the Day hosts Mark Chapman and Kelly Cates has stunned colleagues.

Sources say nobody at the BBC football show seems to have realised the pair were an item before it was revealed in The Sun yesterday.



An insider said: “The ­chatter in the BBC Sport department since their relationship was revealed has been off the charts.

“No one appears to have known they were dating.



“When the news came out, people were talking about it and were flabbergasted as no one knew it was going on.

“Chappers and Kelly have clearly been very professional and have been very discreet about their relationship.



“Their romance has been the best-kept secret in sport.”

Chappers, 52, was spotted shopping yesterday after his relationship with Kelly, 51, was revealed.



Mark, whose annual BBC earnings are about £340,000, got two ravioli ready meals and a microwavable ­spaghetti carbonara from an M&S in Cheshire.

He also talked on his phone while drinking a takeaway coffee.

Chappers and Kelly appeared together on Channel 4’s Celebrity Gogglebox this summer — and their body language was very different to when they were on the programme last year.

In 2025, his arms were folded and her hands were clasped down by her side as they awkwardly watched footage of an animal being castrated.



This year the pair were on the same sofa but were sat much closer, and there was no awkward arm-folding or hand-clasping.

They seemed far more relaxed.

Chappers grew close to Kelly after his three-year relationship with estate agent Clere Collier ended in April.

Kelly is understood to have been single since 2021 when she separated from TV ­producer Tom Cates after 14 years of marriage.



Those close to Chappers say he did not date Kelly and Clere at the same time.

Chappers, Kelly and Gabby Logan take it in turns to present Match of the Day.

The trio took over from Gary Lineker last year.

Sports.title: Phil Foden trapped in Man City maelstrom after guilty verdict amid miserable 34-game drought and England exile
Sports.content:
Next

PHIL FODEN looked like a player in a world of pain BEFORE the Manchester City verdict was handed down.

Now you have to wonder just how the midfielder feels, his inner turmoil surely intensified.



Being left out of the World Cup squad by Thomas Tuchel would have been a devastating blow for Foden, although City announced a new four-year contract on July 26.

Yet that came with City chiefs seemingly already knowing the direction of travel from the independent commission that was finally published last week.



In the light of what we now know, it looks like a defensive measure from a club that could face a lengthy transfer ban.

As for Foden, while City have won all seven competitive games this season, his scoring drought has continued.



His last goal in City colours came at Crystal Palace on December 14 – 34 MATCHES without finding the net.

When Tuchel came to watch him at the Manchester derby, Foden was dismissed after 23 minutes for an angry retaliation kick out which caught Bruno Fernandes amidships – even Enzo Maresca admitted the red card was correct.

It brought a three game ban, meaning Foden will be missing when City walk into a wall of vitriol at Anfield on Sunday.

But now City’s longest-serving player – as he noted in last month’s Instagram post, he is the only survivor from the squad picture ahead of the 2019-20 season – has been inadvertently caught up in the maelstrom unleashed by the commission.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Foden made his City debut – against Feyenoord in the Champions League – in the 2017-18 season, the last campaign covered by the Prem’s currently-proven allegations against the club.

As a stalwart of the club’s domination under Pep Guardiola, nobody has won more in City colours.

Yet he would only be human if he wondered what it all added up to – especially as rival fans and clubs are understandably using the verdict as evidence for their argument that City’s successes are irredeemably tainted.

Foden is not responsible for any of that.



He is the stand-out example of City’s in-house production line. Club-raised, club-trained, club loyal.

Whatever did or did not happen elsewhere in the factory, Foden was unaware the loop even existed, let alone left out of it.

His love for the club, for what the shirt and badge represents to him and the fans, is total and absolute. His commitment, too.

Yet he is caught up in the crisis, the feeling that, for a decade, City paid lip service to the financial rules while blithely and deliberately ignoring them.

That prevailing view was that City believed they could do whatever they wanted, secure in the expectation that financial muscle meant nobody would be able to stop them.



Of course, it may be that City’s arguments find favour with the appeal panel. Or, if the case goes that far, the High Court.

Although when it comes to the sources of the income, that “comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence”, the arguments do appear to have been delivered in somewhat mixed and contradictory messages.

Apparent Government-level threats will hardly serve to lessen the feeling that City’s internal email chain has brought about their own potential downfall.



Nobody can argue that the UAE investment in the area around the Etihad and elsewhere in Manchester has not been transformative.

Indeed, the huge outlay has been a true boon for the city, just as it has been for City.

But it cannot, must not, be the case that the final sentence is commuted because of the potential economic impact.

If that happens, if the Commission and the Premier League – which, as the “prosecution”, will argue for the fitting sanction – does look to have been leant on, then what will be the point of having rules and regulations in the first place?

Anybody who tells you they KNOW what is going to happen is either lying or conceited by their own sense of self-importance.



If City are relegated, which seems almost certain if the verdict sticks, it is hard to see Foden, indelibly linked to the club, pushing for an exit.

You feel he would want to be the cornerstone of any rebuild and return. Yet this must be the most difficult, conflicted and testing of times.

EFL to reject City?

Amid all the theorising about City’s fate, one issue may not have been considered.

What if the EFL declines to accept them?

Rumours abound that a number of Championship clubs are already considering contesting a relegated City’s right to come into the competition if the Prem commission verdict is upheld.



Where there to be an expulsion from the Prem – as some top flight clubs and fans are demanding – the situation could become even more complicated.

Croatia’s catastrophe

It doesn’t matter that Croatia were, as Luka Modric admitted, a “catastrophe”.

England taking them apart in Rijeka was beyond fun.

The questions about Thomas Tuchel will not be answered until he has to make the big call in a game where it is all on the line

But making England enjoyable to watch will ensure most Three Lions fans will be prepared to give Tuchel the benefit of the doubt.



Managers off the hook

The two luckiest men in the Prem are Michael Carrick and Roberto de Zerbi.

What could have been a three week pressure-cooker, cranking up the scrutiny on both of them during the international break, suddenly disappeared as everything was about Manchester City.

Yet Saturday at Old Trafford is now looming and once the two managers have had their first say on City, it will be about their own clubs.



Ever since Spurs put three past Jose Mourinho’s United in the first weeks of the 2018-19 season, with the Portuguese firing back in his post-match press conference, matches between the two have seen added importance.

Mourinho was in the other dug-out by the time Tottenham won 6-1 at United in October 2020, while 12 months later a 3-0 home defeat in N17 was celebrated as a “win” as it spelled the end for Nuno Espirito Santo, heralding the arrival of Antonio Conte and a return to the Champions League.

Spurs have had the better of it since, with a run of eight unbeaten only ended when Cristian Romero was sent off as Carrick’s United won 2-0 in March.



That, of course, included the Europa League Final in 2024 – arguably the worst quality match ever witnessed with a major trophy at stake.

Yet with United 12th and winless Spurs rock-bottom, neither manager can afford a defeat this weekend.

Carrick’s honeymoon with the United fans appears over – last season is history, he is being judged on the here and now.

And having been handed the biggest warchest in Spurs history, with total control over where the money was spent, de Zerbi is fast running out of excuses.

By 7.30pm on Saturday night, one of them is likely to be even more exposed.



Infantino the Teflon Don

Another week passes without a challenger to take on Gianni Infantino.

For all the posturing from Uefa, finding somebody willing to put their head above the parapet and contest the scheduled Fifa Presidential election in March is proving more than difficult.

Senior Uefa figures are still insisting there “must” be a contender ready to bring Infantino down.

But the deadline to find the “white knight” is now barely six weeks away.

Hardly enough time for any potential leader of the global game to develop a serious manifesto.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Meanwhile, Infantino is going around the world, picking up endorsements again.

Despite everything since the summer, he looks increasingly likely to stay in post until 2031.

Sports.title: Gauff receives racist abuse online after China Open incident
Sports.content:
Coco Gauff has had to endure online racial abuse after her latest victory at the China Open; The American star beat 16-year-old Sun Xinran in straight sets though there was an incident at a key moment when Gauff had to stop a point; Gauff explained the "unfortunate situation"

Coco Gauff reports online racial abuse after incident during her victory over Sun Xinran at China Open

Coco Gauff has progressed at the China Open (Associated Press)

Coco Gauff has said she has been racially abused on social media following an incident in her win over Sun Xinran at the China Open.

The world No 4 won 7-5 6-1 against the 16-year-old from China to progress to the last 16 in Beijing.

Gauff was serving to stay in the first set at 4-5 when Sun thought she had hit a winner, but the American had already raised her hand to stop the point as a light in the side panels around the court was flickering.

Gauff took the next three points to hold for 5-5, and then dropped just one more game in the match.

The 22-year-old tried to explain the situation on X, saying: "It was an unfortunate situation but it is out of my control.

"Xinran is incredible talent and player, I apologised for the situation at the end of the match and she completely understood."

Gauff then responded to a racist reply to her post by saying: "Hey everyone, you can dislike me or disagree about what happened without being racist.

"The amount of racist comments/dms I've received in the last few hours is insane.

"Lastly, I 'm not a cheater or a thief."

Sports.title: Mamardashvili's late penalty save denies Northern Ireland win vs Georgia
Sports.content:
Isaac Price missed a late penalty as Northern Ireland were held to a goalless draw by Georgia which nevertheless keeps them top of their Nations League group.

Liverpool goalkeeper Giorgi Mamardashvili guessed right to keep out Price's 84th-minute spot-kick after a combination of Nodar Lominadze and Saba Sazonov fouled Ruairi McConville as he sent a header against the crossbar during a goalmouth scramble.

Jamie Donley and Josh Magennis also brought saves out of Mamardashvili and Tom Atcheson felt he had should have had a first-half penalty, but Northern Ireland were held to a stalemate for the second time in a week at Windsor Park.

Georgia, still yet to score in this season's Nations League, responded to their 1-0 loss to Northern Ireland in Tbilisi 11 days ago by sacking Willy Sagnol, but Ramaz Svanadze is still awaiting his first win in charge despite Khvicha Kvaratskhelia showing flashes of his brilliance in the second half.

Northern Ireland started the night as the only side yet to concede in this season's Nations League, and Pierce Charles made big saves from Zuriko Davitashvili and Giorgi Tsitaishvili to make it four competitive clean sheets in a row for the first time since 2017.

The 21-year-old goalkeeper's seventh clean sheet in nine competitive appearances ensured Michael O'Neill's side remain top of Group B2 by a single point from Hungary.

Northern Ireland's confidence showed in their positive early intent but it took time to wear down a Georgia side who stubbornly defended their box.

McConville was first to test Mamardashvili as he met Justin Devenny's cross but his header was pushed to safety.

With the Northern Ireland fans singing 'Who are you?' at Ballon d'Or nominee Kvaratskhelia the visitors fashioned the clearest chance yet as Davitashvili wriggled free and hit a powerful strike that brought an excellent save from Pierce Charles.

Northern Ireland were soon back in the ascendancy, and when Trai Hume's long throw was allowed to bounce in the box, an improvised looping effort from Donley had Mamardashvili scrambling back.

Patrick Kelly then charged into the box but made the wrong choice in trying to find Donley as his cross was picked off, and Atcheson could not believe he was the one penalised in a clash with Sazonov but the decision was confirmed by a VAR check.

Northern Ireland struggled to replicate that fluidity after the break with some loose passing, and there was a further blow just after the hour when Ethan Galbraith, full of ideas on his return to the side after welcoming a baby boy, hobbled off.

Georgia were growing in confidence, and Pierce Charles did well to gather a deflected strike from Tsitaishvili before Kvaratskhelia blazed over.

It ended chaotically. When Shea Charles won the ball on the edge of the box it ran for Magennis who forced the save from Mamardashvili.

From the resulting corner, McConville got up but took a boot in the face Lominadze and a shove from Sazonov, with Austrian referee Sebastian Gishamer awarding the penalty after being sent to the screen.

Price, who scored his first goal in 10 internationals against Ukraine on Friday, stepped up but it was a comfortable save for the Georgia goalkeeper.

With almost the last kick of the game, Georgia appealed in vain for a penalty after Callum Marshall collided with Sazonov in the corner of the Northern Ireland box.

The impact of the new Reds boss is assessed in the latest Sky Sports Premier League podcast.

Peter Smith is joined by reporters Vinny O'Connor and Mark McAdam, and writer Dan Morgan to pick over the standout tactical ideas Iraola has brought to Liverpool so far and weigh up the impact of summer signings on the balance of the squad.

They also preview the hotly-anticipated showdown with City, which could prove to be a decisive moment at the start of Iraola's reign…

'Iraola is happy to make big decisions'

Sky Sports News' Vinny O'Connor:

"What I've seen from Andoni Iraola is that he's happy to make big decisions - and it was a big decision to leave out Jeremie Frimpong and bring in Ronald Araujo at right-back and it's worked. Liverpool needed to be more solid; they've done that

"Leaving Ryan Gravenberch out, for instance, as well. Iraola has taken that decision. When he's decided to use the youngsters - Lewis Koumas, playing him up front; when he's brought in Trey Nyoni. It seems he's given the trust to the youngsters and that's a real big plus.

"It's not all been perfect but we're gradually beginning to see Iraola's influence with the press. Teams aren't able to settle on the ball as much as they would like to against Liverpool, they're not allowing teams as many passes.

"Yes, at times they've still been caught on the break and that's an area for improvement and I think he's still trying to strive for that ideal balance in midfield.

"But with those three clean sheets in the Premier League in the last three games we're seeing a team that defends the box a lot better, and when they've got the ball, they're getting the ball forward quicker and creating chances, which bodes well for the future.

"We're seeing the signs that it's going to get that little bit more exciting and I don't think we're too far away from seeing more regular high octane football under him."

'Atletico Madrid win showed Iraola can beat big hitters'

Image: Liverpool's Alexis Mac Allister scores his side's second goal during the Champions League opening phase soccer match against Atletico Madrid

Sky Sports News' Mark McAdam:

"The key thing is they're unbeaten. When you go into a new football club, don't lose games! But that big win in the Champions League against Atletico Madrid is a massive plus because not only does that show that they can win games but they can do it against the big teams, the big hitters, those sides that are going to challenge them.

"I've been really impressed so far. There's been a transition period and the key thing that Andoni will need - and what he had at Bournemouth - was time. Time on the training pitch, time to work with the players, time to understand the players.

"It certainly feels like he's very conscious that you need to be defensively solid and you need to have more of the ball [at Liverpool].

"But I said in the summer, if I could have a season ticket to follow Liverpool around for the first six months of Andoni Iraola's term I would absolutely do it because when he is at it and at his very best there's no question it will be one of the most exciting brands of football that Liverpool fans have seen for some time.

"I know they'll go 'well, Jurgen Klopp was the manager not that long ago!' But it will hopefully be something that is very similar to that style of football."

Lift-off on Sunday?

Image: Andoni Iraola believes Liverpool still have work to do to showcase his footballing identity

Liverpool podcaster and writer Dan Morgan:

"In general, I'd say quietly impressive. He surprised me in the sense that I thought idealistically, in terms of how his Bournemouth teams played, I thought his philosophy was going to be something that he was going to be wedded to unconditionally. You play his way, it's relentless, real high-octane energy stuff.

"But he's done things that I think other Liverpool managers in the past would have done. For example, Rafa Benitez would have maybe seen the need to use a centre-back at right back just to shore up Liverpool's issues defensively, especially around set-pieces. Iraola has done that with Ronaldo Araujo. Similarly, Jurgen Klopp would have looked at someone like Lewis Koumas and said, 'I can do something with this young player, he's sticking around'.

"I think that speaks to him recognising the size of the job. He was aware that he can't go 10 games without a win in his first 10 Liverpool games - that would just bring on too much pressure and too much noise - so he's found a way to quietly get results.

"But from a Liverpool supporter, I think there is still that anticipation of, 'OK, when is the big moment going to arrive?' And there's a big opportunity on Sunday…"

Sports.title: Brundle on Bahrain GP software 'chaos' and how Sepang surface tricked teams
Sports.content:
The Bahrain GP in Malaysia was one of the crazier races I've seen in F1. Eventually, this collaboration of lateral thinking which ensured a Grand Prix took place on a great track we have missed in F1 for nine years, was a huge success.

I want to say straight away that I know from meeting numerous fans over the weekend, particularly at the airport on Monday morning, that a great many people suffered very long delays getting out of the venue and back to their bases.

Road systems became gridlocked and transit buses blocked. While the event was necessarily hurriedly assembled, this was still disappointing, and I want to add my personal appreciation to those fans in Malaysia.

At least those I spoke with said they thoroughly enjoyed the race and spectacle, many of whom would also have got as wet through as I did on the grid walk.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Intense rain delayed the start of the Bahrain GP in Malaysia

That weather cell and deluge popped up literally just as the cars headed to the grid, and as the 'easy up' shelters were positioned over the cars and wet tyres feverishly wheeled out, the standing water around the track was such that the start procedure was suspended.

When the rain eased, and with pleasing urgency, it was declared that there would be two formation laps behind the Safety Car and then a proper standing start.

'Chaos' before the start as software glitches in wet

That was all fine until we started seeing a number of cars travelling very slowly and then stopping altogether, except for the Safety Car which continued at normal pace, increasingly out by itself.

Those still running were wary of the regulations and reluctant to pass very slow cars. Many of the six Ferrari-powered cars seemed affected, some Red Bull Powertrains and a McLaren Mercedes too. Given this was the first time many of the all-new 2026 cars had run in wet conditions, there was clearly an unexpected issue.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A chaotic formation lap saw several cars come to a crawl including Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton in Malaysia

It turned out to be FIA software settings. All cars must run a standard FIA 'brain' for many essential functions to ensure parity and abide by regulations, which couldn't compute with cars travelling at such increasingly slow speeds, shutting down power delivery.

Cars were eventually spread out all over the track in two and then three tranches. Drivers at the side of the track effectively having to hit the control/alt/delete to restart their motors. It was chaos and the Safety Car was about to lap many cars which should have been diligently following it.

The only option was to abandon the whole thing and recover to the pits, at which point the Safety Car was bizarrely mid pack rather than at the front.

The next problem was to unravel the problem and regulations; would those who fully stopped and lost position, like Lewis Hamilton's Ferrari, be obliged to start from the position they arrived back in the fast lane of the pits?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen compare the starting procedure issues in Sepang during the Bahrain GP in Malaysia to the F1 Lego race.

Although it took 40 minutes all told, which actually conveniently allowed the rain cell to clear the district, a smart and fair decision was made that the restart would be in original grid order. Furthermore, the FIA quickly found the issue, rewrote some code altering key power unit operating parameters which are in place for starting procedures when the car is under 50kph, and flashed that 'patch' to all the cars, not all of which had experienced problems, such as the Aston Martins.

Anyway, it worked, even though cars would now be travelling faster behind the Safety Car on pit exit with much better track conditions, and teams and drivers by then knew what to look out for.

'Sponge-like' surface catches out Ferrari and McLaren

This track, often doused mid-race with a cloudburst, used to dry out remarkably quickly, but temperatures had been much lower on race day than during practice and qualifying. The pit lane was bone dry, and, on television pictures, so was the pit straight and many other areas. Which tyres to use for the new standing start, more than an hour and a half after the original time slot, was the next dilemma.

It looked like slick dry tyres to me, and several thought so too, like Ferrari, McLaren, Audi and Aston Martin. As soon as the cars left behind the Safety Car it was clear there was much more spray than expected, and areas such as turns three and five were still quite wet.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Lewis Hamilton drop to 15th on the opening lap as Mercedes claim the lead at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia

Some like Oscar Piastri at McLaren and Audi recognised immediately that the right tyre was the intermediate with the light water grooves. Others like Hamilton and Lando Norris decided to stick with it and hope for fast improvement. Charles Leclerc did too but contact on the first racing lap broke his front wing and he had to pit anyway, so they also fitted intermediates. Despite that long stop, in no time at all he'd caught Hamilton's sister Ferrari and passed him, such was the painfully slow pace on dry tyres.

The track surface was heavily worn in places, and the extreme weather in these parts clearly take their toll year-round. There had been no time, and no appetite either given the one-off aspect of this event, to resurface it. The nature of the asphalt, and sometimes over-60 degrees Celsius surface temperature, had been stressing the dry tyres throughout practice and qualifying with heat degradation.

Now, in a situation which George Russell described over his radio as 'weird', the track wasn't drying anything like as fast as expected. I believe that the old asphalt, with billions of tiny pockets of water in the surface, acted like a sponge.

Verstappen seizes control as Hamilton fights back

Out front it was a thrilling battle between the two Mercedes of Kimi Antonelli and Russell, and Max Verstappen's Red Bull, who were all on intermediate tyres. Max had looked the favourite to win this race for three days such was his pace.

It would be nine laps before the leading slick-tyred car of Norris was faster than the intermediate-shod cars, and by then the slick runners were over a minute behind. Importantly, Hamilton had resisted the call to change onto intermediates based on the fact that he'd taken the pain and there was no point in pitting now.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli and Max Verstappen go wheel to wheel on the restart, before Verstappen slips through to take the lead

Just at that moment Valtteri Bottas spun off his Cadillac deep into the gravel at turn 13 and there was a Safety Car deployed. It was perfect timing for the leaders as they could ditch their now overheating inters during a pit stop that would cost 18 seconds rather than 26 given the pack on track were at Safety Car speeds.

Crucially the full (not virtual) Safety Car would stay out for a good while and this allowed the slick runners to close back up and negate the huge time losses they had thus far suffered, even if they had plenty of traffic between them and their natural rivals up front who had chosen the right tyres. This was a key reset for the race.

Hamilton didn't pit and preferred track position to fresh rubber. He would impressively run his starting soft compound dry tyres for 31 laps, and it would pay dividends.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton recovered from 18th to the podium with a great drive

Championship leader Antonelli had been going along nicely in the lead, and there had been some quality overtakes between him and team-mate Russell. On dry tyres the natural speed of Verstappen, and his wily restarts, would put him into a lead which he would never be seriously challenged despite some more dramas to come.

The fast-starting Racing Bulls had been going along very nicely in the hands of Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad, who had started at the very back due to power unit penalties. Esteban Ocon had similarly been running in sixth in his Haas, and Carlos Sainz had fast-started his Williams into the top 10 too. But as the track fully dried, while it was a three-horse race out front, the usual suspects in the form of the two Ferraris and two McLarens made their way forward.

Isack Hadjar had been running in a solid fourth place in the second Red Bull, having shown decent speed again all weekend, and, given he would suffer a relative loss of power in the closing stages, he could have well have done without what happened next.

Russell engine failure 'sums up his season'

Alex Albon's Williams would grind to a halt on the exit of turn three on lap 42 of 55, albeit well parked next to a service road. The car wouldn't easily move though and so a vehicle and marshals would have to emerge from behind the barriers, meaning a full Safety Car was called again in order to control the pack to give space to recover the Williams.

Over the next couple of laps most cars would stop for fresh, albeit mostly used tyres, in order to have decent grip for the restart and closing stages. This Safety Car of course also packed the whole field back up again.

It took an age to let the three lapped runners unlap themselves, as per the flawed regulation, especially as the third of whom, Sergio Perez, was a long way behind the Safety Car even before he could unlap himself.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell retired from the Bahrain GP in Malaysia with just five laps remaining

Then two things happened. Russell's Mercedes had a power unit failure despite the Safety Car speed. It's not so unusual for something to fail when not being fully loaded, and incredibly painfully for him and his fans, he pulled over to the side of the track and retired. That image sums up his whole season of bad luck, and the pain may well continue in Singapore if he has to take fresh power unit elements.

As the pack behind him were trying to work out what was going on and if they could legitimately pass George's car under Safety Car rules, everyone slowed quite dramatically on the approach to turn one. Lando was sailing along warming his tyres, minding his own business, and in the glare of the sun failed to notice he was catching the pack at great speed.

At the back of that particular train of cars was his team-mate Oscar Piastri, and if Lando had smashed into him then it would have been a shocker for the team in terms of results in the race and spare parts and costs. He swerved left to miss Piastri, skidded down the kerb and took a long trip through the gravel losing several places in the queue, with no rights to pass them back under the Safety Car. He would end up ninth, and with Red Bull first and fifth, this leaves McLaren just 18 points ahead in the Constructors' Championship in third place.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Toto Wolff fumes after George Russell's power unit failure at the Bahrain GP in Malaysia

Verstappen made another great restart to lead and Antonelli gave the best chase he could, but the Red Bull was too fast. Behind, after a great drive, Hamilton passed Hadjar for what was third place after Russell's demise, and Leclerc in the second Ferrari did the same thing for fourth place. It was a solid and important result for team boss Fred Vasseur too, who's taken a lot of media pressure recently.

Lawson and Lindblad finished a fine seventh and 10th for Racing Bulls, and it was a welcome eighth for Fernando Alonso. His Aston Martin had been more competitive than of late, perhaps due to the layout of the track and also how the track surface affected aerodynamics, even holding off the recovering Norris on the last lap.

'A victory that has been shaping up'

It was the seventh time this year that Verstappen has been voted the fans' driver of the day, but the first time he's won a race this season and of course the impressive first victory for the all-new Red Bull-Ford power unit. It was a victory which has been shaping up for a few races now and very well deserved for the team.

Through all this, championship leader Antonelli kept his head along with speed and consistency, and by finishing ahead of his two main championship rivals in Russell and Hamilton, yet again increased his championship lead to 84 points.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Max Verstappen win the Bahrain GP in Malaysia!

It seems Qatar and Abu Dhabi will now take place as scheduled which adds another 50 points available, but if Kimi didn't show up in Singapore, Austin, or Mexico, he'd still lead the championship with four races to go.

It was a long afternoon and the race completed with just 12 minutes remaining before it would time out. In fact, it finished a full three hours and twenty minutes after the initial start time.

Let's see what challenges Singapore can throw at the teams and drivers this weekend.

Sports.title: Littler beaten in semi-finals of World Youth Championship
Sports.content:
Luke Littler lost to Cam Crabtree in the semi-finals of the World Youth Championship.

Crabtree beat Littler 6-5 and will meet Jan Schmidt in the final at Minehead.

Littler came back from 2-0 to level the game, but Crabtree ultimately overhauled him.

Littler was playing for the first time since his shock defeat to Luke Woodhouse in the opening stage of the World Grand Prix.

Crabtree raced into a 2-0 lead against 2023 World Youth Champion Littler, but the sport's premier player soon regained control with a brutal three-leg spell.

Image: Cam Crabtree upset Littler

The Warrington sensation followed up a magnificent 164 checkout with back-to-back 14-darters to move 3-2 ahead, but Crabtree was undeterred, hitting back with 92 and 100 finishes to take a 5-4 lead.

Littler responded with a terrific 117 to force a last-leg decider, although Crabtree wasn't to be denied, firing in a 16-dart hold on double six to prevail with a 97.91 average.

Littler had been flawless in the group stage at the World Youth Championship, taking three wins. He then saw off Lewis Cook, but at one point Cook, only 16 years old himself, went 3-0 ahead only for Littler to stage a comeback.

Littler then beat David Fidler 6-1 and reached the quarter-finals after defeating Archie Self 6-4.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Barry Hearn thinks Luke Littler is a natural born darts player and that the 19-year-old needs to show people boos won't put him off his game

Littler took a 6-2 victory over Harrison Leigh to win through to the final four but then came unstuck against the 23-year-old Crabtree.

This tournament is open to players aged 16-24 and offers £60,000 in prize money.

Earlier this year Littler looked like he would steamroll all before him, but his bid for a clean sweep of all major PDC titles in 2026 ended in Amsterdam where the Briton complained about being repeatedly whistled at by Dutch supporters.

A dip in form has then been compounded by unexpected defeats at the World Grand Prix and now the World Youth Championship.

Mardle: Littler's underperforming

Sky Sports commentator Wayne Mardle questioned why Littler entered the World Youth Championship. "I don't know what he wants to gain from it," he said. "It doesn't make any sense to me.

"I just don't see the value time-wise. Because time-management's everything when you're playing a lot."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the World Grand Prix match between Luke Littler and Luke Woodhouse

Littler's exit from the World Grand Prix could be cause for concern. "I'm never concerned with people losing because this is a hard industry to keep winning. The fact that he was winning all those matches on the trot in majors anyway was ridiculous," Mardle said.

"It was the way he's been losing. He's not been playing that well. This is no offence and no disrespect to Luke Woodhouse. Luke Woodhouse actually said himself that it was a scrappy game.

"It's the fact that Luke Littler didn't play well," Mardle added. "I just think he's underperforming right now, for whatever reason.

"Bearing in mind we're humans, we're not robots, we're not automatons, we do have off days as well. He's just having a couple of off days right now."

What's next?

The European Tour season continues with the Swiss Darts Trophy (October 9-11) and the Dutch Darts Championship (October 16-18) before the European Championship takes place in Dortmund, Germany from October 22-25.

Sky Sports remains the home of darts with the Grand Slam of Darts (November 14-22) and World Darts Championship (December 10-January 3) both live. Stream darts and more through NOW with no contract.

Sports.title: Woakes gives backing to ECB's Cricket For Teachers initiative
Sports.content:
Former England bowler Chris Woakes has given his backing to new ECB initiatives that plan to take cricket to more than 3,500 teachers and over 1,700 state secondary schools.

The new 'Cricket For Teachers' programme and 'Secondary Countdown Cricket' competition support the ECB's ambition to reach more than half of all state secondary schools by the end of 2028

Cricket For Teachers is a free teacher training programme designed to give PE teachers the confidence, skills and knowledge to deliver quality cricket sessions for students of all abilities.

Participating schools will receive training, resources, equipment and ongoing support to help establish a sustainable cricket culture at the school.

Image: Chris Woakes celebrates after England's 50-over World Cup win in 2019

Woakes, a two-time World Cup winner with England, capped 217 across all formats, said: "I was fortunate enough to discover my love of cricket through opportunities at school and in my local community, and I know how important those experiences can be for young people."

Woakes, who retired from international cricket in 2025, added: "These programmes will help introduce cricket to many more children who may never have picked up a bat and ball before. The more opportunities we can provide in state schools, the stronger and more inclusive the future of our game will be."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the best friend test with Stuart Broad and Chris Woakes

Alongside the ECB's new training programme, Secondary Countdown Cricket is a new mass-participation soft ball competition for students aged 11 to 16.

Funding will provide schools with training, equipment, resources and competitive playing opportunities designed to make cricket more accessible than ever before.

Image: The ECB have launched two new initiatives in schooles, 'Cricket For Teachers' and 'Secondary Countdown Cricket'

Richard Thompson, ECB chair, said: "When we launched the State School Action Plan, we made a commitment to create more opportunities for young people from every background to experience cricket. Today's launch is an important step in delivering that commitment.

"State schools educate the vast majority of young people in England and Wales, so if we are serious about making cricket the most inclusive team sport in the country, we must ensure those schools have the support they need.

"Cricket For Teachers and Secondary Countdown Cricket will help remove barriers, build confidence among teachers and give hundreds of thousands more young people the opportunity to enjoy everything our sport has to offer."

Sports.title: Medvedev defaulted for hitting spectator with ball in defeat to Djokovic
Sports.content:
Daniil Medvedev was defaulted for hitting a spectator in the face with a ball as Novak Djokovic took his impeccable record at the China Open to 33-0 and moved one win away from a first title of 2026.

Medvedev accidentally struck the fan around the left eye while trailing 7-5 5-3 and three points from defeat in Monday's punishing semi-final in Beijing, during which Djokovic saved 16 of the 18 break points he faced.

Medvedev, who will now lose all points and prize money earned from the event, hit a backhand into the stands after the ball deflected off a wall following a winner from Djokovic

The spectator was subsequently helped out of the arena and tournament organisers later announced he had been taken to hospital.

Image: Daniil Medvedev was defaulted for hitting a spectator with a ball during his China Open semi-final against Novak Djokovic

Medvedev: It was '100 per cent accident'

Medvedev said: "Terribly sorry to the spectator, first of all I'm trying to get in touch with him, if he wants it.

"Hopefully I can apologise in person. I just hope he's OK. That's the most important. I just really care about him right now.

"It was 100 per cent accident. You can see I didn't hit the ball in anger. I do a lot of bad things but usually ball abuse is not my thing.

Medvedev’s previous on-court flash points 2026 Monte-Carlo Masters: Smashed his racket on more than one occasion during 6-0 6-0 defeat to Matteo Berrettini 2025 US Open: Fined over £30,000 for becoming enraged when a photographer walked on court while opponent Benjamin Bonzi prepared to serve on match point 2025 Australian Open: Fined £54,000 after breaking a net camera by smashing it with his racket while being beaten by American teenager Learner Tien

"The ball was bouncing back so I tried to just hit it anywhere so it doesn't go out from the court When I saw the result, I felt horrible. Hopefully I can meet him and make up for it somehow."

Speaking afterwards, Djokovic, who was defaulted at the 2020 US Open for hitting a line judge with a ball, said: "It is a bit of a shock, to be honest. I am sorry for the person.

"I hope the person is not badly injured. I also feel sorry for Daniil as I know exactly how it feels to be disqualified in a big match. I'm sure he didn't want to do this intentionally."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Djokovic has his say on Medvedev's disqualification, having experienced something similar before

Djokovic: Always a battle against Medvedev

Djokovic, 39, won the China Open six times in seven years between 2009 and 2015 but had not returned prior to this campaign.

The Serb, who secured a come-from-behind quarter-final victory over world No 2 Alexander Zverev on Sunday, will meet Alex de Minaur in Tuesday's final as he looks to clinch a 102nd career title and first since the Hellenic Championship little under a year ago.

Image: Djokovic's record at the China Open is a flawless 33-0

Djokovic said: "It was a gruelling battle that I definitely didn't want to take to a third set. It was looking like that.

"It is always a big battle with Daniil, so hard to play him when he is feeling the ball in slower conditions with his big serve.

"I always believe in myself and felt I played really well in training but obviously it is different in an official match.

"My draw wasn't favourable, very tough matches from the beginning, but it makes the run to the final sweeter. Something about Beijing keeps me going."

Image: Djokovic is targeting a seventh title in Beijing

Djokovic reached the Australian Open final in January, losing to Carlos Alcaraz in four sets, but has struggled for fitness and form since and dropped out of the world's top 10, although this run in Beijing has returned him to that elite level.

The 24-time Grand Slam champion, who has played just eight tournaments this year, recently revealed an ongoing medical condition that has led to fatigue and vomiting on court, with the issue exacerbated in hot and humid conditions.

De Minaur was leading Hubert Hurkacz 6-4 3-2 in the first semi-final when his opponent pulled out through injury.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sonay Kartal's run in Beijing was ended by Elena Rybakina's conqueror Alina Charaeva in the third round

In the women's event, Britain's Sonay Kartal saw her WTA Tour comeback end in the third round with a 6-4 6-1 loss to Alina Charaeva - the player who dumped out world No 1 Elena Rybakina in the previous round.

This was Kartal's first WTA tournament since March after a stress fracture of the back and she picked up wins over Andrea Lazaro Garcia and Wang Xinyu before falling to Charaeva.

Following her loss to Charaeva, US Open champion Rybakina has now withdrawn from the upcoming Wuhan Open due to a foot injury. "I'll take some time to rest and recover," Rybakina was quoted as saying by Wuhan Open organizers.

Iga Swiatek reached the fourth round after rallying from a set and 5-2 down to beat Donna Vekic 4-6 7-6 (7-0) 6-2, while Coco Gauff also advanced to the last 16 as she brushed aside Xinran Sun 7-5 6-1.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Iga Swiatek's epic comeback earned a last-16 clash with Iva Jovic

Alcaraz wins - despite losing 16 points in a row

Over at the Japan Open, defending champion Alcaraz fought from a set down to beat fellow Spaniard Jaume Munar 5-7 6-3 6-1 and make his first final since April's Monte-Carlo Masters.

World No 3 Alcaraz led 5-3 in the first set against his compatriot but then lost 16 points in a row to ship it before the players traded breaks at the start of the second set.

The seven-time major champion eventually took control to secure a meeting with Jiri Lehecka in in Tokyo on Tuesday.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Defending Japan Open champion Carlos Alcaraz fought from a set down to beat fellow Spaniard Jaume Munar 5-7 6-3 6-1 and reach the final

Alcaraz said: "I don't know what happened in the first set. It seems that I'm struggling in every first set, but I've come back every time and I'm really happy about it."

Alcaraz's season has been disrupted by a wrist injury that caused him to miss his French Open defence as well as Wimbledon.

He returned for the final Grand Slam of the year, the US Open in New York, where he reached the quarter-finals before losing in five sets to home player Ben Shelton.

If Alcaraz takes the title in Japan for the second straight year - he beat Taylor Fritz in the 2025 final - it will be his third of the campaign, after the Australian Open and Qatar Open, and 27th of his career.
