Sports.title: Jack Catterall Pressures Teofimo Lopez Over Mandatory Fight
Sports.content:
Jack Catterall is keeping his claim on Teofimo Lopez’s next fight visible while a potential Ryan Garcia matchup attracts attention. Catterall tagged Lopez on X with an eyes emoji and a staring-eyes GIF, a brief reminder that the ordered defense remains unresolved.

The WBA ordered the welterweight champions Teofimo and Catterall to negotiate in September, giving them until October 22 to reach an agreement before possible purse bids. Catterall holds the organization’s regular title, while Teofimo holds its super championship.

Catterall has earned his shot and has little reason to wait while Teofimo pursues Ryan. Agreeing to another delay would let the champion dictate when—or whether—he gets that opportunity. His public reminder keeps pressure on Teofimo to address the ordered defense

👀 @TeofimoLopez https://t.co/I6KqhNC0AN — Jack Catterall (@jack_catt93) October 5, 2026

Ryan brings the massive gate, the circus spotlight, and the blockbuster money for Lopez. Catterall brings none of that. Fighting Catterall means defending a belt against an awkward spoiler who could derail everything for a fraction of the pay.

That leaves Teofimo stuck. Chasing a blockbuster with Ryan sounds great, but the WBA order will not simply disappear. Hunting for a bigger payday is understandable, but actually getting sanctioning body approval to ignore a mandatory challenger is an entirely different battle.

Teofimo might need to vacate his belt to chase the massive check waiting with Ryan Garcia. Taking on Jack Catterall beforehand puts the entire jackpot in jeopardy. One slip against Catterall ruins his leverage, killing the buzz for the megafight.

Pretending the order does not exist invites the WBA to strip him. The October 22 cutoff marks the end of negotiations rather than an instant title stripping, yet Lopez cannot stall forever. Catterall forced the reality into the open: defend against him or walk away from the belt to fight Ryan empty-handed.

Sports.title: Floyd Schofield Targets William Zepeda After Lucas Bahdi
Sports.content:
Floyd Schofield wants William Zepeda next if he beats Lucas Bahdi, with his father already forecasting a four-round stoppage of the Mexican pressure fighter. That is an ambitious projection before Schofield has secured his first world title.

“Zepeda is definitely who I want next. … That’s who I was going to call out and still going to call out after the fight,” Schofield told Chris Mannix. Floyd Schofield Sr. went further, arguing that Zepeda leaves too many openings and declaring: “Zepeda will get stopped in four rounds.”

Schofield faces Bahdi for the vacant WBA lightweight title this Saturday, October 10, in Chicago. A victory would give him a belt to bring into negotiations with Zepeda, making the proposed matchup more valuable than another contender callout.

Both fighters being represented by Golden Boy offers a practical reason to pursue it. The company could promote a unification involving two of its own fighters, with the winner emerging as a stronger attraction.

The competitive argument is less comfortable for Schofield than his father suggests. Zepeda’s pressure is built around making opponents work repeatedly, forcing them to defend, move, and return punches without long recovery periods. Finding openings against him is only part of the task. Schofield would also need to exploit them while managing the pace.

His knockout of Tevin Farmer showed how destructive he can be when an opponent gets caught early. It didn’t establish how he would handle Zepeda if the quick finish failed to arrive. Schofield Sr. acknowledges that facing Zepeda requires conditioning for 12 hard rounds, then assumes his son could end it in four.

There are also two immediate obstacles. Bahdi has his own chance to derail Schofield’s plans, while Zepeda has been ordered to defend against interim WBC champion Jadier Herrera. The proposed unification cannot simply be treated as available next.

Schofield naming Zepeda is a worthwhile challenge. Backing up his father’s prediction would require something considerably harder than identifying flaws on film: beating Bahdi first, then making Zepeda pay for those openings without being overwhelmed by everything coming back.

Sports.title: Oscar De La Hoya Doubts Ryan Garcia’s Zuffa Move
Sports.content:
Oscar De La Hoya doesn’t believe Ryan Garcia will join Zuffa Boxing after completing his Golden Boy contract, despite Ryan’s praise for his experience at its recent event. Keeping him, however, will require more than questioning the alternative.

“He was very complimentary, and I’m glad that it turned out great for him because it’s Ryan’s career that’s on the line. But no, I don’t think he’ll go with Zuffa. I don’t think that’s a good fit for him,” De La Hoya told The Ariel Helwani Show.

Asked to explain, Oscar attacked Dana White’s handling of boxing press conferences and questioned his authority within the operation. He didn’t identify specific contractual or financial reasons that would make Zuffa unsuitable for Ryan.

That leaves his view looking more like a promoter defending his position than evidence of where Ryan intends to sign. Ryan’s positive experience gives Zuffa something to build on if it pursues him. Oscar’s criticism doesn’t erase that impression.

Golden Boy still has one fight remaining with Ryan, and De La Hoya named Devin Haney and Teofimo Lopez as his preferred opponents. Neither matchup is finalized. Oscar indicated that arranging the next major fight comes before discussing an extension.

That remaining appearance offers Golden Boy its strongest opportunity to make a case for staying. Delivering Haney or Lopez would demonstrate that Oscar can still secure valuable fights despite the disagreements between promoter and fighter.

There is a complication: a successful final appearance could also increase Ryan’s appeal to competing promoters. Golden Boy might deliver the payday and exposure that help him negotiate a more attractive deal elsewhere.

De La Hoya says he has spoken with Ryan since the Conor Benn fight and describes their relationship as good. That should help them conduct business, but it isn’t a commitment to another contract.

Oscar can doubt a Zuffa move. His more useful task is giving Ryan a reason to choose Golden Boy again. The next opponent, the terms, and the handling of that final fight will make a stronger argument than another attack on Dana White.

Sports.title: Vergil Ortiz Jr. Nears Keith Thurman Fight
Sports.content:
Vergil Ortiz Jr. is nearing a fight with Keith Thurman, a matchup that offers a recognizable name and another payday but little explanation of where Vergil belongs among the best at 154.

Oscar De La Hoya says negotiations are being finalized, with December 12 targeted for an appearance on David Benavidez’s Arizona card. The agreement isn’t complete, but Golden Boy appears to have found its alternative to Jaron Ennis.

“There’s been rumors about Keith Thurman. So, we’re finalizing that deal there, and hopefully we can have him on the Benavidez card in December,” De La Hoya told The Ariel Helwani Show.

Thurman, 37, is coming off a stoppage loss to Sebastian Fundora. That makes him an awkward opponent for a fighter trying to establish himself at the top of the division. Vergil would be facing someone whose latest attempt to compete at championship level ended inside the distance.

The business logic is easier to understand. Thurman retains a familiar name from his welterweight championship years. That gives promoters something to advertise without needing to introduce an unfamiliar contender. His reputation can help sell the matchup even if his recent results offer much less reason to expect a competitive fight.

De La Hoya’s explanation for the stalled Ennis negotiations also helps explain the choice. He cited money, back-and-forth discussions and outside involvement without identifying those involved. Thurman appears to offer a route to getting Vergil back into the ring while that more demanding negotiation remains unresolved.

Activity has value, but the sporting reward here looks limited. If Vergil stops Thurman, Fundora has already done it. A victory would add a former champion to his record without answering the questions an Ennis fight would address.

Oscar insists the best must fight the best. Finalizing Thurman makes that promise harder to sell. Vergil gets another event and a paycheck; the opponent who could substantially strengthen his claim to being the division’s best remains somewhere beyond it.

Sports.title: Ben Whittaker Lacks Substance For Bivol, Warren Argues
Sports.content:
Ben Whittaker’s title opportunity has come before his stamina has caught up, according to Frank Warren, who told Playbook Boxing that a Dmitry Bivol fight would be a severe mismatch.

His victory over Conor Wallace leaves Matchroom with an awkward choice. Pursuing Bivol now risks exposing Whittaker before he can correct his weaknesses. Taking a demanding preparation fight risks losing the opportunity through defeat.

“He runs out of gas. He hasn’t got a great engine,” Warren said to Playbook Boxing. Asked about facing Bivol, he added: “Anyone who makes that fight should be reported to the NSPCC.” “Matchroom done a good job in promoting him. He got everybody talking about him, but you’ve got to have some substance then. And the substance at the end of the day just isn’t there.”

Wallace’s late rally supplies the strongest evidence for Warren’s criticism. Whittaker struggled when his opponent kept advancing and forced him to work while tired. Bivol’s disciplined combinations and positioning could make those demands arrive earlier, with fewer opportunities to recover.

Waiting alone will not solve that. Whittaker needs rounds that teach him to control his effort, maintain his defense, and respond when an opponent refuses to cooperate. An easy stoppage would offer little evidence that he has learned those lessons.

Warren’s suggestions of Joshua Buatsi or Willie Hutchinson come with an obvious commercial incentive: either could give Queensberry a valuable victory over a heavily promoted Matchroom fighter. They would also test whether Whittaker can withstand sustained pressure from a dangerous domestic contender.

That is the difficulty with using either as preparation. The test could become the defeat that derails the Bivol route.

Whittaker’s highlights have accelerated his popularity. His ring education needs more time. Once fatigue reduces his movement, the defensive habits behind the spectacle become harder to conceal.

Matchroom must now decide how much risk to accept while bringing his boxing up to the level his promotion already promises.

Sports.title: Sebastian Fundora Dismisses Ermal Hadribeaj’s Knockout Threat
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora sees little behind Ermal Hadribeaj’s knockout predictions, telling The Ring that his unbeaten mandatory challenger presents no threat in power or boxing ability ahead of their October 17 fight in Las Vegas.

Hadribeaj has eight knockouts in a 23-0-1 record, which makes stopping the WBC light middleweight champion an ambitious promise. His best victory, a unanimous decision over Bakary Samake in May, earned him this opportunity without showing that he possesses the punch to finish Fundora.

“Boxing-wise, IQ-wise or anything, I don’t see no threat at all,” Fundora told The Ring. “Punching power? No, there’s not really anything in my mindset that is realistic in that situation.”

Fundora’s confidence is understandable. Hadribeaj hasn’t beaten anyone with the champion’s combination of height, output, and experience. Getting past Samake in an eliminator was a useful win, but dealing with a 6-foot-6 southpaw who can maintain pressure through repeated exchanges requires considerably more.

The challenger’s unbeaten record offers no answer to how he will react when Fundora forces him to work harder than he has against previous opposition. If Hadribeaj cannot discourage him with his punches, finding enough room to box could become difficult.

Still, Fundora has already experienced the danger of giving an opponent opportunities to land. Brian Mendoza knocked him out in the seventh round in April 2023. That defeat should remain a reason to stay defensively responsible, even against someone whose record suggests modest power.

A low knockout total doesn’t prevent a challenger from landing one damaging shot. Fundora’s willingness to fight at close range can give opponents chances they would struggle to create if he consistently used his reach.

Fundora has won four straight since the Mendoza loss, most recently stopping Keith Thurman in six rounds. Hadribeaj represents another chance to build toward bigger fights, including a possible unification with Jaron Ennis.

The challenger has earned his title shot. His knockout prediction requires evidence he has yet to provide.

Sports.title: Frank Warren Questions Anthony Joshua’s Chin Against Tyson Fury
Sports.content:
Frank Warren believes Anthony Joshua’s physique will offer little protection against Tyson Fury, saying that punch resistance and stamina favor his fighter in their heavyweight showdown.

“One thing you can’t do, you can’t put muscles on chins,” Warren said to Playbook Boxing. His argument is that Fury has recovered from heavy punishment, while Joshua’s defeats against Andy Ruiz Jr. and Daniel Dubois exposed weaknesses that strength and conditioning cannot solve.

Warren pointed to the punchers who have put Fury down, particularly Deontay Wilder, and emphasized his ability to recover. He also claimed Fury has “much more stamina than AJ.”

Joshua’s muscular build has never prevented him from being hurt. The more relevant question is what happens afterward. Against Ruiz and Dubois, he struggled to regain control once the damage was done. Fury has repeatedly survived knockdowns and found a way back into fights, giving Warren a reasonable basis for that comparison.

However, those recoveries came at a cost. Fury’s ability to survive Wilder’s punches does not guarantee he can absorb Joshua’s at this stage of his career. Warren himself described both heavyweights as being in the “late autumn” of their careers, which makes their current condition more relevant than their strongest performances years ago.

Joshua also does not need to match Fury’s endurance if he can land cleanly before the fight develops into a prolonged contest. His opportunity is to punish openings without rushing his work or leaving himself exposed to the return.

Warren acknowledged that both men can punch and argued that their willingness to commit under fire could decide the outcome. That brings his criticism back to something more specific than muscles: whether Joshua can remain effective after taking a damaging shot.

Fury’s history gives Warren confidence in that situation. Joshua’s history gives him a target to attack. Neither establishes how much punishment either heavyweight can still withstand.

Sports.title: Moses Itauma Keeps Ben Davison For January Return
Sports.content:
Moses Itauma will return in January with Ben Davison still training him, Frank Warren confirmed to Playbook Boxing following a team meeting to discuss his defeat against Filip Hrgovic.

Warren identified Itauma’s pursuit of a knockout as the mistake that exhausted him. Keeping Davison means their next camp must produce a more controlled approach, with Itauma learning to win rounds without trying to finish his opponent with every punch.

“He’s staying with Ben and the team,” Warren said to Playbook Boxing. “You’ve got to judge him now on his results, which is what we’ll do.”

Warren said Itauma and his team met at the Queensberry offices on Friday, giving everyone time to review the defeat before discussing changes. He did not name a January opponent.

The promoter believes Itauma’s power would have stopped most heavyweights that night, claiming “98%” would not have survived. Hrgovic did, and that exposed the danger of building a fight around an early finish. Once the knockout failed to arrive, Itauma had spent energy he needed for the later rounds.

Warren described a fighter who needed to return to his jab, move, and take an easier round. Those are practical adjustments, but Itauma must be willing to make them while an opponent is still in front of him. Having the tools in training is different from choosing to use them under pressure.

A January victory would get Itauma moving again. The more useful evidence will be how he achieves it. Another quick stoppage could leave the questions from the Hrgovic defeat unanswered, especially if the opponent offers little resistance.

Davison’s continued involvement gives the partnership an opportunity to demonstrate that it can correct the pacing issue. Warren praised Itauma’s heart and believes he can challenge for another world title fairly soon, but that ambition depends on developing an approach that works when his power cannot settle the fight early.

Ghana News.title: FTBLRLIFE targets Ghana in expansion of global grassroots football network
Ghana News.content:
Global grassroots football platform FTBLRLIFE is targeting Ghana as part of its expansion into the African football market, with the company looking to connect the country's young players and academies to a wider global football community.

The platform, which currently has a presence in more than 130 countries, wants to create a digital ecosystem where players, coaches, academies and football businesses can connect, share their stories and discover opportunities.

Its planned entry into Ghana comes against the backdrop of a football landscape rich in young talent but where many players, particularly those outside established academies and professional structures, struggle to gain visibility.

From community pitches and school teams to privately run academies, Ghana has a large grassroots football network that continues to serve as the starting point for many of the country's professional players.

FTBLRLIFE believes technology can help bridge some of the gaps between these players and the wider football industry.

The platform allows players to build profiles showcasing their football journeys, connect with coaches and academies, follow football-related stories and gain visibility for opportunities.

Academies can also use the platform to manage their teams, organise rosters and events, share updates and showcase their players to a global audience.

For Ghana, the company believes this could provide an additional avenue for young players to be seen beyond their immediate communities.

The platform's expansion is built around what it describes as three key areas: organising the fragmented grassroots football community, increasing visibility for talent and providing support to the grassroots game.

FTBLRLIFE currently has more than 1,000 partner academies globally and says its wider programmes have impacted more than 27,000 children.

It also operates the FTBLRLIFE Foundation, which supports under-resourced football communities through its Foundation Ball programme.

The initiative provides footballs to academies in need, with QR technology on the balls creating a link between the beneficiaries, donors and the wider FTBLRLIFE community.

For a country such as Ghana, where access to basic football equipment remains a challenge for some grassroots clubs and community teams, the foundation's work could form part of the organisation's activities as it establishes itself in the market.

FTBLRLIFE founder David Clarke says the global football industry continues to overlook a significant part of the game.

“Valerie Nekesa was found playing barefoot in a village in Kenya. She just scored at a World Cup and signed with CD Tenerife. That is one story. There are millions more waiting,” he said.

The company estimates that more than 500 million players make up the global grassroots football market.

It believes many of those players remain invisible because grassroots football is often spread across disconnected academies, social media pages, messaging groups and local networks.

In Ghana, FTBLRLIFE hopes to bring some of those players and organisations onto one platform while creating links between local grassroots football and the international football community.

The move comes as Ghana continues to rely heavily on its grassroots system as a pathway for developing players for the domestic game and the Black Stars.

Several Ghanaian players who have gone on to successful careers in Europe and elsewhere began their journeys on local pitches and through youth academies.

FTBLRLIFE's Ghana strategy will therefore be closely watched by academies and young players seeking alternative routes to exposure and opportunities outside the traditional scouting system.

The platform says its ultimate goal is to give grassroots football a home and ensure that talent is not limited by geography or access to established football networks.

With Ghana now firmly in its sights, FTBLRLIFE is hoping to make the country's grassroots football community part of that global network.

Ghana News.title: Former ‘American Idol’ contestant sentenced to life without parole for wife’s murder
Ghana News.content:
An Ohio man who was found guilty of murdering his wife and staging the crime scene to make it seem as if an intruder had broken into their home and fatally shot the mother of two was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole.

Caleb Flynn, 40, a former pastor who once appeared as a contestant on "American Idol" in 2013, was found guilty of aggravated murder and multiple counts of murder, felonious assault and tampering with evidence in connection with the death of his wife, 37-year-old Ashley Flynn.

Judge Jeannine Pratt called the former pastor's actions "abhorrent" and "quite honestly impossible to fathom" while handing down the life sentence on Monday.

Caleb Flynn called 911 early on Feb. 16 to report that his wife had been shot by an intruder at their home in Tipp City, north of Dayton. He was arrested three days later. Prosecutors alleged that Caleb Flynn "executed" his wife by shooting her twice in the back of the head in bed so that he could be with his mistress and manipulated the crime scene to make it seem as if an intruder had broken in through the garage.

Pratt said that after considering the evidence in the case, there is "one clear and obvious conclusion" -- that Caleb Flynn poses the "highest risk" of harm to the public -- and admonished the "layers of deceit, manipulation and cruelty" that he has shown.

"You could have walked away. You could have separated from her and left her here on this earth to be able to be with the people that need her, who loved her, who looked forward to having her in their lives. But instead, through your greed, your selfishness, your lust, and your cruelty, you chose to take Ashley's life, and in doing so, you did far more than take the life of your wife," Pratt said. "On that fateful day in February, the person who should have been protecting their children shattered their lives."

Caleb Flynn addressed the court prior to learning his sentence, crying while reading from prepared remarks that he shakily clutched while in handcuffs and an orange jumpsuit.

He repeatedly denied killing his wife, saying, "I have unfortunately lied about a lot of things over the last couple of years. But as I stand here before God, who is my ultimate judge, I am not lying when I say I did not kill my wife."

"I will continue to fight for my innocence as long as the Lord allows me to, since I did not kill my wife," he said.

He apologised to his wife's family and asked for their forgiveness.

"I made vows to Ashley on our wedding day -- I failed those vows, and through my decisions, I have caused you guys an incredible amount of pain," he said. "Through those decisions, I'm sure you have felt betrayal, confusion, anger, and so much more."

"I take complete accountability for my words and my decisions," he said. "I am so sorry, I am so sorry, and pray that you can one day forgive me."

Caleb Flynn also addressed members of his family, including his young daughters.

"I don't know if they'll ever be able to hear this, but I want them to hear it regardless -- I love you two," he said, calling them his "greatest joy in his life."

He apologised for not being able to see them grow up and said through tears that he misses them "more than you'll ever know."

The judge said she received over a dozen victim impact statements, and several members of Ashley Flynn's family addressed the court prior to the sentence being handed down, speaking to the impact the murder of their mother has had on his daughters, Alyssa and Ava, and asking for the maximum possible sentence.

In a searing letter read on her behalf, Alyssa said, "You have already caused so much pain to your family and the world. The least you can do is tell everyone you did it and receive your outcome."

"Did you really even think about how much pain you would bring your own two daughters?" the statement continued. "By the way, Ashley Flynn was the best thing that ever happened to you. You had the best life ever, and you decided to throw it away for a girl who was half your age."

In closing, she said her family has "never been stronger", and she doesn't plan to visit him in prison.

Her sister, Ava, asked their father in a statement read on her behalf, "Mommy was the perfect person, the absolute perfect person -- what did she ever do to make you hate her so much?"

"She was my best friend. And then you chose to kill the only mother I ever had. I miss her so much -- so, so, so much. You have no idea," the statement continued, calling on him to "confess and repent" to God.

Caleb Flynn could be seen crying as the statements were read.

He faced up to life in prison without parole.

Prosecutors asked for the maximum possible sentence, arguing in a sentencing memorandum filed ahead of the hearing that he is a "dangerous individual with no regard for human life and has refused to accept accountability or show any remorse."

"It is important to note that Defendant could have lawfully left his marriage. Instead, he chose murder. He planned Ashley's murder for months. This was a planned and calculated execution," Prosecuting Attorney Paul Watkins stated.

In his memo, Watkins said Caleb Flynn's "effort to escape responsibility did not end with the staged scene or the false intruder narrative," but that his two daughters described him instructing them on what to say in their forensic interviews and that their statements "could be the difference between life and death for him."

"Thus, after taking their mother from them, Defendant attempted to use his grieving daughters to reinforce the story he had created to protect himself," Watkins stated.

The defence, meanwhile, said in its memorandum that Flynn continues to maintain his innocence and has no prior criminal history while asking for a sentence that "preserves the possibility of parole and a return to society following his rehabilitation."

The jury deliberated for nearly 2 1/2 hours before reaching a verdict on Sept. 29, finding him guilty of all charges.

During closing arguments, Miami County Assistant Prosecutor Matthew Joseph pointed to evidence including the physical scene and a side garage door he said was made to look as if an intruder had damaged it, Caleb Flynn's 911 call, text messages between the defendant and his mistress discussing the end of his marriage and digital records from the night of the shooting, which he argued "leads straight to the defendant."

"The evidence showed that being the victim would allow the defendant to keep his lucrative job working for Ashley's family business, he would benefit from Ashley's life insurance, and he could keep his position as a working worship leader with zero impact to his reputation within the church," Joseph said during closing arguments on Sept. 29 in the Miami County courtroom. "The evidence does not tell the story of an intruder."

Defence attorney Patrick Mulligan argued during his closing that the state's evidence is circumstantial, and that the only thing prosecutors proved was that Caleb Flynn was having an affair.

"Connecting a couple of meaningless dots doesn't solve the case," Mulligan told jurors.

Caleb Flynn did not testify during the trial, and the defence called no witnesses.

He denied killing his spouse in an interview with police days after the deadly shooting, according to video shown during the more than weeklong trial.

His former mistress testified for the state during the trial, reading from some of the more than 100,000 messages they exchanged over her two days of testimony.

"If I could literally kill her and not go to hell, I would do it in a heartbeat," Caleb Flynn said in one message from May 2025, Botner testified.

Following the guilty verdict, Mulligan told reporters that he expected there to be a notice of appeal filed.

When asked what appellate issues they have, he said, "There's a lack of evidence on prior calculation and design."

Watkins thanked the jury "for their dedication to justice in this case."

In a statement read by Watkins, Ashley Flynn's family said they "refuse to let the evil that ended Ashley's life have the final word in her story."

"Ashley loved Jesus with her whole heart. Her faith wasn't simply something she simply spoke about. It was how she lived," the statement said. "She loved people well, found joy beyond her circumstances, prayed boldly for her family, and wanted her life to point people to Jesus."

"Most of all, she loved being a mom," the statement continued. "She prayed over her girls, taught them to love God, and showed them what it looked like to live with faith, kindness, joy, and grace."

Ghana News.title: Education Ministry commends Ghanaian teachers on World Teachers’ Day 2026
Ghana News.content:
The Ministry of Education has commended teachers across Ghana for their dedication, professionalism and sacrifices as the country joins the international community to celebrate World Teachers’ Day 2026.

The Ministry said teachers remain at the heart of Ghana’s education system and play a critical role in shaping the minds, character and future of children.

In a press release issued on Monday, October 5, the Ministry particularly recognised teachers serving in deprived and hard-to-reach communities, where they continue to provide education despite challenging conditions.

The Ministry said the Government’s education transformation agenda is focused not only on expanding access to education but also on improving quality, learning outcomes, relevant skills and human capital development.

It stressed that teachers are essential to achieving these objectives, noting that no meaningful education reform can succeed without a strong and supported teaching workforce.

The Ministry therefore pledged to continue working with teachers, their unions and other stakeholders to strengthen the teaching profession, support professional development and address concerns affecting teachers’ welfare and working conditions.

It also called on parents, communities and Ghanaians generally to appreciate and support teachers, whose work it described as fundamental to the country’s social and economic development.

The Ministry used the occasion to express its gratitude to teachers nationwide for their continued service and the role they play in preparing future generations.

“To every teacher, we say:

Thank you for your dedication. Thank you for your sacrifice. Thank you for shaping Ghana’s future.”

Ghana News.title: NPP can reconcile with aggrieved members who want to return – Nana Akomea
Ghana News.content:
Newly elected NPP Third Vice Chairperson, Nana Akomea, says the party is willing to reconcile with aggrieved members who are prepared to return and work with the party.

He, however, says reconciliation must be a two-way process, requiring the individual's willingness to engage with the other party.

“You can’t reconcile any party, but who doesn’t want to be reconciled? The person himself or herself should want to reconcile and work with the party,” he said.

Nana Akomea was speaking on Monday about how the party could bring back members who have become disaffected.

He said the NPP would welcome not only its aggrieved members but also support from people outside the party.

“Once that is there, we even want floating voters who are not members of our party. We want NDC people to vote for us. How about members of our party?” he said.

But he stressed that those seeking reconciliation must demonstrate a willingness to engage.

“But there must be a willingness to engage. That’s the basic thing. If the willingness is not demonstrated, it becomes difficult because nobody is indispensable in a politician,” he said.

His comments come amid questions about the future of some prominent NPP figures and their relationship with the party.

On the disciplinary case involving Assin Central MP Kennedy Agyapong, Nana Akomea said he had not received an update following an extension granted to the committee handling the matter.

“Frankly, I haven’t had any update. They were given a two-week period. I was at the National Council meeting. They were given a two-week period, and I know at the next council meeting there was a report that they had asked for an extension,” he said.

He said he had not followed the matter since the extension was granted.

“So I haven’t followed it after that extension was granted to the committee. So I don’t think they have brought their report yet,” he said.

Nana Akomea said he would not express a personal view on the disciplinary matter before the committee submits its recommendations.

“That determination has been given to the disciplinary committee,” he said.

He explained that members of the National Council should allow the committee to complete its work before publicly expressing their opinions.

“Now, if members of the National Council are now going to be stating their opinions, that will prejudice the work of the committee. So let them come. Their recommendations will be made public, and then at that point we can state our opinion,” he said.

He added that the committee’s report would help determine whether there had been a willingness to engage and move forward.

“The disciplined committee will come up with it, and if the report is that there has been a willingness to engage and move on,” he said.

Ghana News.title: Tamale Child Deaths: Vehicle owner arrested as IGP deploys homicide team
Ghana News.content:
The owner of the vehicle in which the bodies of three children were found in Tamale has been arrested and transported to Accra to assist with police investigations.

The arrest follows the discovery of the bodies in the boot of a black Hyundai Tucson at Koblimahagu Zoo in the Tamale Metropolis of the Northern Region.

The Inspector-General of Police has also deployed a special investigative team to Tamale to support the Northern Regional Police Command.

The team comprises homicide investigators, crime scene experts and intelligence officers.

The three children have been identified as Dauda Abdul Aziz (3), Saani Alsharaf (5), and Dauda Fadilan (7).

According to the police, the children allegedly left home for Islamic classes at about 8am on Sunday, October 4, 2026, but failed to return.

Efforts by community members to locate them were unsuccessful until their bodies were discovered at about 5am on Monday, October 5.

The bodies were found inside the boot of a black Hyundai Tucson with registration number AS 1770-14.

Police said the vehicle was found stuck in mud on a road leading to the area.

Vehicle Owner Arrested

Preliminary inspection of the vehicle showed that the driver’s door and the rear passenger door behind the driver’s seat were open.

The other doors, including the boot, were locked, police said.

Preliminary investigations indicate that the vehicle belongs to a member of the Ghana Immigration Service.

According to the police, the owner told investigators that the vehicle had been stuck in the mud for the past five days.

“He has since been arrested and is being taken to Accra to assist the investigation,” the police said.

The vehicle has since been secured for further forensic examination.

Homicide Team Deployed

The IGP’s decision to deploy the special team is intended to strengthen the investigation into the circumstances surrounding the deaths.

The homicide investigators, crime scene experts and intelligence officers will work with the Northern Regional Police Command to establish what happened to the children.

Police have not yet disclosed the cause of death.

Bodies Held for Autopsy

Meanwhile, police have declined a request by the children’s families to release the bodies for burial in accordance with Islamic customs.

The police said an autopsy is necessary to support the investigation.

Authorities have assured the parents that the state will bear any financial costs associated with the autopsy.

Police said investigations are ongoing.

Ghana News.title: From ShattaFest to MoMo Fest: Entertainment takes centre stage in youth engagement
Ghana News.content:
Entertainment is playing an increasingly important role in how brands, artistes and organisations connect with Ghana’s growing youth population.

Recent experiences from ShattaFest and MoMo Fest have demonstrated how large entertainment programmes can attract young audiences while creating platforms for engagement and commercial activity.

ShattaFest has leveraged Shatta Wale’s strong following to bring fans together through music and live performances.

The festival provides an opportunity for fans to engage with the artiste’s brand while creating business opportunities for vendors, event organisers, hospitality providers and other players within the entertainment ecosystem.

MoMo Fest has similarly used music and entertainment to create an interactive audience experience.

The festival combines musical performances with the promotion of Mobile Money services, giving MTN Ghana an opportunity to engage customers in a relaxed and interactive environment.

The approach demonstrates how corporate brands can use entertainment to communicate with younger consumers beyond traditional advertising.

The growing popularity of such events has also increased interest in Ghana’s creative economy.

Music, event production, sponsorship, digital marketing, fashion, food, transportation and hospitality all benefit from the large audiences attracted by major entertainment programmes.

As the industry expands, stakeholders are also increasingly focusing on the quality and safety of entertainment experiences.

Organisers are expected to provide appropriate security, crowd management and other measures to ensure that audiences can enjoy events safely and responsibly.

The experiences of ShattaFest and MoMo Fest show that entertainment has become more than a leisure activity.

It is increasingly serving as a platform for youth engagement, commercial activity and the promotion of Ghana’s creative economy.

Ghana News.title: Nigerian military aircraft crashes, killing 32
Ghana News.content:
A Nigerian ​military plane flying from Benin City ‌to Lagos crashed on Monday in southwestern Ondo state, killing 25 passengers and seven crew ​members.

President Bola Tinubu, confirming that ​there were no survivors, expressed "profound sadness" and ⁠extended condolences to the families of ​those aboard.

"The Chief of Air Staff has ​briefed me, and I have directed the Nigerian Air Force to immediately commence a thorough investigation ​into the cause of the crash ​to prevent future occurrences," Tinubu said in a ‌statement.

The ⁠Air Force ATR-42 aircraft was on a routine mission from Benin City to Lagos when air traffic controllers lost contact ​with it ​at 0813 ⁠GMT on Monday, Aviation Minister Festus Keyamo said. The accident was one ​of the deadliest air disasters ​in ⁠Nigeria in recent years.

The wreckage was later located near the coastal town of Igbokoda, ⁠where ​search and rescue teams ​were deployed.

Ghana News.title: MTN encourages Ghanaians to use MoMo for saving, investing and financial planning
Ghana News.content:
MTN Ghana is encouraging customers to move beyond basic Mobile Money transactions and take advantage of the wider range of digital financial services available on the MoMo App.

The telecommunications company says the initiative forms part of efforts to deepen digital financial inclusion and help customers use technology not only to transfer money, but also to save, invest, access credit and plan for their financial future.

Speaking during MomoFest, Manager for Brands and Communication at MTN Ghana, Isaac Agyenim Boateng, said the company was repositioning MoMo from a transaction platform to a broader financial-wellness tool.

“For us as a business now, we are moving from wallet to financial well-being,” he said.

Mr Boateng noted that although many customers continue to rely on the *170# short code for basic transactions, the MoMo App provides access to a wider range of financial services.

These include savings, investments, loans and pension products, giving customers more opportunities to manage and grow their finances through their mobile devices.

Taking MoMo to customers

MTN has, over the past two weeks, intensified its engagement with customers across the Volta Region, including Ho and surrounding communities.

According to Mr Boateng, teams have been visiting communities, homes and offices to help customers download the MoMo App and understand how to use its various services.

He said the campaign was not simply about encouraging more people to download the application, but also about changing how customers use digital financial services.

The objective, he said, was to help customers move from simply sending and receiving money to using their digital wallets to build greater financial stability.

Security remains critical

Mr Boateng also urged customers to remain vigilant against fraud, assuring them that the MoMo platform has security measures in place.

He said MTN’s security systems were complemented by continuous customer education through SMS messages, social media campaigns, weekly fraud-prevention tips and educational content on its YouTube channels.

He, however, cautioned customers never to disclose their MoMo PINs or one-time passwords.

“Your PIN is your key. It is a key to your wallet,” he warned.

Cashless payments transforming businesses

Some vendors participating in the MomoFest activities also highlighted the growing importance of cashless payments to their businesses.

Vendor Abandoned Grace Oma Mefut said digital payments had reduced the risks associated with carrying large amounts of cash after making sales.

For Millicent, popularly known as MG of MG Scoreset, cashless transactions have become an important part of her online business, providing customers with a convenient way to make payments.

She said the growing adoption of digital payments was changing how businesses operate and interact with customers.

MTN Ghana says the expansion of digital financial services could make financial services more accessible while encouraging customers to move from simply using money digitally to managing their financial lives digitally.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Trump says taxpayers will no longer fund TV ads that praise him
World.content:
Move comes after ethics experts criticised three nationally broadcast ads and called for independent investigations.

Share Trump says taxpayers will no longer fund TV ads that praise him on social media

United States President Donald Trump has said he will stop using taxpayer funds for television s featuring him after widespread criticism of the campaign-style spots.

In a post on his social media site on Monday, Trump defended the s, which cost at least $1.5m in federal funds and were aired ahead of the US November midterm elections.

Trump said he considered the s to be “a positive promotion for our Great U.S.A.”, but that they would no longer be funded by taxpayers but by either him or his MAGA PAC,

MAGA Inc. is Trump’s political war chest and had amassed more than $400m by the end of July.

The announcement came as ethics experts and lawmakers from both ⁠parties have criticised the three nationally broadcast s and called for independent investigations.

The s have run during football games as recently as Sunday and during other programming.

One features Trump declaring that “America will never be a communist country”, ⁠while a chorus repeats the words “love me”. Another combines ⁠images of Mount Rushmore with footage of Trump praising a “golden age of America”.

The s end with a disclaimer saying they were paid for by the US government.

Democratic lawmakers said last month that the White House transferred $20m in Homeland Security Department funds to air ⁠the s, including one that closely resembles a 2024 Trump ⁠campaign ad, and sought independent probes.

California Attorney General Rob Bonta on Monday called ‌for an independent investigation, calling it a “staggering misuse of public funding and breach of public trust” after the calls for a probe.



Federal Communications Commission Chair Brendan Carr, a ‌Republican ‌named to his position by Trump, last week said the s were appropriate and rejected a request to investigate them.
