World.title: Moroccan journalists recount years of surveillance amid new Amnesty claim
World.content:
Rabat, Morocco – “I was surveilled not because of a specific article. I was investigating land dispossession in Morocco. I then learned I was a Pegasus target,” Omar Radi, a journalist and human rights defender, told Al Jazeera, referring to the mobile surveillance tool developed by Israeli company NSO Group.

The findings emerged in June 2020, when Amnesty International Security Lab examined his phone. Radi, now based in Germany, said he had spent two years, from 2018 to 2020, noticing signs including his phone’s battery draining quickly, its temperature rising and the network slowing down.

The physical surveillance, he said, was barely discreet.

“They came every day to get a daily report from the parking attendants in my street, the shops I used to go to, and my friends,” he said. “I would sometimes turn around and walk towards the people following me to take photographs, but they ran quickly and hid their faces.”

His case is among four detailed in a new Amnesty International report, We Start With the Verdict: Inside Morocco’s Surveillance Machine, produced with 14 media organisations and coordinated by the international network of journalists Forbidden Stories.

The other three are Fouad Abdelmoumni, a veteran activist; Abdessadak El Bouchattaoui, a human rights lawyer; and Hicham Mansouri, a journalist in exile who had been imprisoned in 2015 on charges of adultery and sexual exploitation, which Amnesty describes as trumped-up.

The report draws on interviews with a whistleblower using the pseudonym Safir, a former employee of Morocco’s General Directorate for Territorial Surveillance (DGST). Amnesty said it corroborated key parts of Safir’s testimony with independent sources, technical evidence and interviews with 10 people identified as surveillance targets, including Radi.



“The Amnesty report connected many dots as to what I was living and feeling while I was under tight surveillance,” Radi said.

“It explains the extraordinary aspect of my police interrogations and my trial, where many of my rights weren’t respected, because even the judicial police and the judges were under monitoring,” he added.

Amnesty identifies the DGST as the agency behind the deployment of Pegasus spyware in Morocco and documents what it describes as abuses of the spyware against activists and journalists between 2017 and 2021.

Morocco denies surveillance

Morocco has previously rejected Amnesty’s allegations that its authorities used Pegasus to target journalists, activists and other critics.

In statements issued in 2020 and 2022, Moroccan authorities challenged Amnesty to provide material evidence supporting its claims.

Amnesty said it wrote to Moroccan authorities four weeks before publishing its latest report and invited them to respond, but received no response.

Al Jazeera also sought comment from Moroccan officials but had not received a response at the time of publication.

Moroccan media have also challenged the latest report. Le360 cited arguments that the presence of a phone number in Pegasus targeting records does not, by itself, prove that a device was infected or establish who ordered an alleged attack.

The outlet also argued that Amnesty had not provided the conclusive technical and material evidence Moroccan authorities had demanded.

The report says Morocco’s Pegasus operations were fully active by October 2017, pointing to the case of human rights lawyer El Bouchattaoui, whose number was entered into the system in September 2017 and selected for targeting weeks before he received an infection link by text message.

Amnesty said its analysis of Pegasus records matched 103 Moroccan phone numbers to individuals identified as potential targets between September and December 2017. Of those, 65 were identifiable as civil society members, including 34 human rights defenders, 22 journalists and media workers, five lawyers and four academics.

According to Amnesty, Safir described a surveillance apparatus that combined digital and physical methods. Targeted individuals were secretly filmed and recorded in detention, offices, cars, cafes and even bedrooms, he said.

Phone shops, he added, were coopted to sell targets devices infected with spyware. Neighbours of human rights defenders, he said, were recruited as informants to file daily reports on their movements.



Safir also described the use of remote control systems (RCS) at internet cafes. Field agents would identify which cafe a target was visiting, he said, giving the DGST access to activity on machines it had already infected and allowing an operator to track calls, read messages, access photographs and record audio.

The report says similar tactics were used against activist Abdelmoumni, who was secretly filmed at home with his fiancee in 2021. Abdelmoumni said he believed the footage was captured through a hidden camera in an air-conditioning unit, based on the recording’s angle.

Safir described the episode as a “textbook case” of a DGST surveillance and cleanup operation designed to leave no trace.

Journalists describe pressure and intimidation

Taoufik Bouachrine, one of Morocco’s best-known journalists and host of the Talk on Politics podcast, was not named in Amnesty’s report but described a similar pattern.

“In Morocco, as in all Arab countries, inventive methods are used to silence journalists and deter them from investigative journalism, particularly when it concerns the unlawful exercise of power, financial corruption, and the intertwining of political authority and money,” he told Al Jazeera.

The first method, he said, is fabricating criminal cases against journalists, “often involving allegations of sexual misconduct in a conservative society that amount to a journalist’s moral execution”.

The second, he said, is a smear campaign run through armies of online trolls and operatives who target journalists and their families.

Bouachrine, 57, was arrested in 2018 on charges of rape and human trafficking and sentenced to 15 years in prison. He has denied the charges, saying his prosecution was tied to his journalism.

The United Nations Working Group on Arbitrary Detention found Bouachrine’s detention arbitrary and said he had been subjected to judicial harassment. The European Parliament adopted a resolution calling for his release, along with other journalists tried on similar charges.

He served more than six years before being released under a royal pardon. By then, Akhbar Al-Youm, the newspaper he founded, had already closed. Bouachrine said authorities had cut off its advertising revenue.

“This is another method of destroying investigative journalism,” he added, “turning off the advertising tap and leaving a newspaper to die slowly.”

World.title: Police clash with Kosovo protesters over bid to curb Hague war crimes court
World.content:
The political dispute over the court has become a factor in negotiations to hold a new presidential election.

Share Police clash with Kosovo protesters over bid to curb Hague war crimes court on social media

Police have clashed with protesters outside Kosovo’s Parliament over plans to limit the powers of a Hague-based war crimes court.

The violence broke out on Monday evening after Parliament ended its session without passing the proposed changes, which concerned the Kosovo Specialist Chambers, a court dedicated to crimes committed during the Kosovo War from 1998 to 2000.

Recommended Stories list of 2 items list 1 of 2 Serbian populist leader Vucic launches campaign for prime minister

Serbian populist leader Vucic launches campaign for prime minister list 2 of 2 What’s next for Bosnia after elections? end of list

Founded in 2015, the court is an independent part of Kosovo’s judicial system, based in The Hague and staffed internationally.

Critics, however, have accused the court’s verdicts of being overly punitive. The amendments before Parliament would limit sentences to 15 years, allow sentences to be served in Kosovo and permit appeals to the self-declared republic’s Supreme Court.

The changes passed a first reading earlier on Monday, but Parliament adjourned before a second vote could be held.

Several hundred protesters had gathered outside the Parliament building in Pristina, including supporters and veterans of the Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA), the ethnic Albanian rebel force that fought Serbian troops in the war.

Some tried to block lawmakers from leaving after the session ended. Police used tear gas and water cannons in an attempt to disperse the protesters, some of whom threw flares and firecrackers.

Naser Syla, the emergency director at a hospital in Pristina, told The Associated Press news agency that 12 people were injured, including 11 civilians.



The legislation follows the September 16 convictions of former President Hashim Thaci and three other former KLA commanders for war crimes.

Thaci was sentenced to 25 years in prison. His co-defendants received prison terms ranging from 13 to 25 years. They have all denied the charges.

The rulings prompted weeks of protests and were unanimously condemned by Kosovo’s Parliament in late September.

The question of reforming the court has also become tied to the political battle over Kosovo’s presidency.

Kosovo’s Constitutional Court has ruled that the self-declared republic has until October 6 to elect a president. If lawmakers fail to do so, Parliament will be dissolved, and Kosovo will face another early election.

The Democratic Party of Kosovo (PDK), the largest opposition party and sponsor of the bill, has hinged its support for electing a president to the successful passage of the changes.

Prime Minister Albin Kurti’s governing Vetevendosje party, or the Self-Determination Movement, wants the presidential vote to take place first.

Kurti backed allowing the bill to proceed but told Parliament on Monday that the changes had been rushed.

He has also said the appeals process should be used to challenge the controversial September convictions.

Kosovo created the Specialist Chambers under pressure from Western allies to prosecute alleged crimes by KLA members.

It was based outside Kosovo partly due to concerns about political pressure and threats to witnesses.

The court remains deeply contentious in Kosovo, where many people regard the KLA as the force that fought Serbian repression and led the self-declared republic towards declaring independence.

The 1998-99 war killed about 13,000 people, most of them ethnic Albanians, and forced about one million Kosovo Albanians from their homes.

The conflict ended after a 78-day NATO bombing campaign against Serbian forces. Kosovo declared independence from Serbia in 2008, but Belgrade does not recognise its sovereignty.

World.title: Trump officials pursue record number of cases to strip US citizenship
World.content:
Top officials have sought to expand the use of rarely invoked laws that can strip naturalised Americans of citizenship.

Share Trump officials pursue record number of cases to strip US citizenship on social media

The United States Department of Justice has filed 40 new cases seeking to strip naturalised Americans of their citizenship over alleged crimes they have committed.

In a statement on Monday, federal prosecutors said they were targeting individuals accused of “serious offenses”, including money laundering, child sexual abuse, visa fraud and tax evasion.

The statement touted the 40 cases as the largest volume of denaturalisation petitions submitted in such a short period under President Donald Trump. The petitions were filed from late August through early October.

“Today’s announcement marks the largest denaturalization effort in modern history,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche.

“Under President Trump’s leadership, the Department of Justice will continue to employ the denaturalization process to maintain our national security and protect the American people.”

The 40 citizens targeted in Monday’s announcement include people from a range of countries, including Mexico, Pakistan, China and Sierra Leone.

They are accused of concealing criminal acts and other facts about themselves as they sought to obtain citizenship. Their criminal convictions largely came after they took their oaths of citizenship.

Two people on the list are also accused of engaging in espionage on behalf of China. Committing these crimes before they became citizens, the Department of Justice alleges, meant these individuals lacked “good moral character” and should have been denied citizenship.

Expanded use of denaturalisation law

The laws to denaturalise US citizens have been used for decades, but historically, they have been reserved for serious crimes.



After World War II, for instance, the US government moved to denaturalise dozens of citizens accused of concealing involvement in the Holocaust or engaging in war crimes.

Notable cases include that of Emma Goldman, a Lithuanian-born anarchist and women’s rights activist who was jailed in 1917 for her antiwar activities, before being denaturalised and deported to the Soviet Union.

But the practice has become much less frequent since the end of the Cold War.

Top officials in the Trump administration, however, have sought to expand denaturalisation as part of a push to conduct the largest deportation operation in US history.

Under US law, prosecutors can ask courts to strip citizenship from those born outside the country if they wilfully concealed a “material fact” during their citizenship application that would have otherwise disqualified them.

But Trump’s efforts to widen denaturalisation proceedings have received pushback from human rights groups, which argue they could leave people stateless.

Critics have also warned that Trump has sought to leverage denaturalisation against specific groups he perceives to be political rivals or enemies.

Last year, for instance, the Trump administration indicated it would seek to denaturalise large numbers of Somali Americans after allegations emerged in Minnesota of daycare fraud involving the Somali diaspora.

“Send them back from where they came, Somalia, perhaps the worst, and most corrupt, country on earth,” Trump wrote at the time.

Members of Trump’s Republican Party, notably Representative Andy Ogles, have also floated the possibility of yanking citizenship from New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who was born in Uganda. Trump himself has falsely suggested Mamdani may be in the country illegally.

At one point, Trump even floated the idea of withdrawing citizenship from tech entrepreneur Elon Musk, a close ally and adviser to his second administration, after the two men had a falling-out in 2025.

Trump has also pushed to do away with birthright citizenship, which is granted to virtually all children born in the US. The few exceptions include the babies of diplomats and foreign military forces.

Birthright citizenship is protected under the US Constitution and cannot be taken away the way naturalised citizenship can.

In June, the US Supreme Court struck down Trump’s efforts to dismantle birthright citizenship, but legal battles continue after the president issued a second executive order also seeking to restrict how birthright citizenship is applied.

World.title: New York state declares measles disaster amid resurgence of disease in US
World.content:
The US had largely eliminated measles by 2000 but has seen several outbreaks amid declining vaccination rates.

Share New York state declares measles disaster amid resurgence of disease in US on social media

New York state has declared a disaster emergency over an outbreak of measles, as cases of the disease that had once been all but eliminated in the United States continue to rise.

New York Governor Kathy Hochul said on Monday that she was temporarily expanding the ability of health professionals to administer measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccines.

“No one should get seriously ill or die from a vaccine-preventable disease,” Hochul said in a statement, adding that New York has recorded 108 cases of measles this year, as of October 3. The declaration will remain in effect through November 4.

Hochul’s announcement marks the first such declaration since measles cases began to tick up in 2025. She said that seven cases were recorded in New York City and 101 elsewhere in the state.

Hochul’s declaration says 92 cases have been recorded since July 15 in a handful of rural communities with insufficient vaccination rates.

Officials in neighbouring Pennsylvania also announced that the state has surpassed 1,000 measles cases this year, the largest outbreak in the US in the last three decades. Outbreaks have also been recorded in Texas, Utah, Ohio and South Carolina.

Health experts attribute the resurgence to a decline in vaccination rates below the 95 percent rate they say is necessary to prevent outbreaks.

Critics say the decline has been spurred by an anti-vaccination movement that has surged in popularity and gained advocates inside the administration of President Donald Trump, including Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr.



The US had eliminated the domestic spread of measles by 2000, with the last outbreak of more than 1,000 cases occurring over several years in New York City in the early 1990s.

International officials from the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) are set to meet in November to determine whether the US and Mexico will retain their measles-free status, or whether the public health designations will be updated.

“PAHO reiterates the importance of maintaining high and homogeneous vaccination coverage, strengthening epidemiological surveillance, and ensuring timely outbreak response, as essential pillars to halt transmission and sustain measles elimination in the countries of the Americas,” the organisation said in a previous statement.

World.title: Trump says 'threat' led US to pull bombers from RAF Fairford
World.content:
RAF Fairford - in the Cotswolds in Gloucestershire - has been at the centre of an incident being investigated by counter-terror police.

Five men were initially arrested on suspicion of terror offences and subsequently released on bail. A sixth man, a UK-Iranian national, was also later arrested and released on bail.

Following the release of the first five men, Trump criticised the decision and US officials suggested Iran could have been involved in the incident.

Whitehall sources have not disputed that the decision from Washington to remove the bombers was in response to the incident at the airbase in Gloucestershire.

Speaking earlier on Monday, Rubio said he would not directly tie last week's incident to the decision to pull bombers from RAF Fairford.

He added: "It's not unusual to see movement of assets to different parts of the world based on exercises, redeployments, people changing out and new people coming in, new planes coming in and old planes going out."

Rubio said the US still had full confidence in the security of all its bases and that British authorities had been very co-operative since the incident.

Vance later said the bombers had been moved out of an "abundance of caution", adding Washington felt Iran was doing what it had "done for 49 years... which is engage in acts of terrorism against the US and against a lot of other people".

Days after the incident at RAF Fairford, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said there were "strong indications" that Iran had played a part in the incident but he did not provide further details, while Rubio said it had "clearly involve[d] the hands of a foreign actor" without going into further details.

Tehran has strongly denied any involvement.

In July, Iran said "any base used for aggression against Iranian territory constitutes a legitimate target for our forces".

RAF Fairford, near the village of Whelford, has been used as a forward operating location by the US air force for decades.

In recent months, the US has flown B-1 and B-52 bombers from the base for the Middle East, after the UK approved a US request to use it for defensive strikes on Iran.

The redeployment from RAF Fairford will reduce America's capacity to "quickly surge sorties against Iran, reducing the threat level somewhat", Christoph Bergs, research analyst at defence think tank the Royal United Services Institute told the Reuters news agency.

However, the use of the base had already been limited given London's stipulation that it should only be used for defensive strikes, he added.

The planes could potentially be sent to either Diego Garcia or bases in the Gulf to reduce the need for air-to-air refuelling but that would depend on capacity availability, negotiations with allies and security, Bergs added.

World.title: France braces for national day of school protests after injuries and mass arrests
World.content:
France is braced for major protests on Tuesday, after organisers called for a nationwide day of action in support of students demanding more investment in education.

It comes after a week of demonstrations, which saw students blockading hundreds of schools, at least 190 students injured, and more than 5,000 people arrested.

One student had his hand blown off during a confrontation on Monday, while another was reportedly struck in the head by a tear gas grenade last week.

France's prime minister said the government had announced measures to address their demands, but the Union Syndicale LycÃ©enne (USL), a major organiser of the protests, said the government had offered "nothing concrete".

The organisation called on people to join their mobilisation on Tuesday in the face of "this political deadlock and what we describe as unprecedented repression of the movement".

Some other organisations have also shown their support for the students, with the teachers' union SNES-FSU urging its members to join Tuesday's protest.

The radical-left La France Insoumise (LFI) party leader Jean-Luc MÃ©lenchon described the protests as the "most powerful high school and university student youth movement" since 1968 - a year of major unrest, which saw millions of workers go on strike.

The wave of demonstrations began in September in Paris and has spread across the country, with students protesting over a range of issues, including overcrowded classrooms, run-down buildings, and a lack of teachers.

The protests were started by high school students, who were later joined by university students.

World.title: Flydubai co-pilot planned to crash plane into Tel Aviv airport or building, reports say
World.content:
The co-pilot accused of trying to hijack a flydubai plane planned to crash the aircraft into Tel Aviv's Ben Gurion airport or a tower block in the Israeli city, US and Israeli reports suggest.

The Omani national was a "lone wolf" extremist, according to the reports.

The United Arab Emirates' attorney-general has said the co-pilot attempted to carry out a "terrorist act" on flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv last Wednesday.

He attacked and wounded the captain with the emergency crash axe kept in the cockpit before being overpowered by passengers. Another crew travelling on the plane was able to land it in Saudi Arabia.

Israel's prime minister has said the co-pilot underwent "Islamist radical indoctrination" and the captain, passengers and a second crew prevented "a 9/11 disaster".

World.title: Zelensky condemns 'horrific' Russian strike on boat carrying corn in Black Sea
World.content:
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky has condemned a "horrific" Russian attack on a vessel carrying corn in the Black Sea.

The ship's captain was killed in the strike involving two drones, Zelensky said, and another sailor was unaccounted for. Eleven crew members - nationals of Azerbaijan and India - have been rescued.

Romania said it had mounted a rescue mission after "a fire on the ship Royad Mammadov" outside the country's territorial waters. It said two people had died.

Russia has not commented, but its defence ministry earlier said it had struck two cargo vessels. Russia has been pounding Ukrainian infrastructure in what it says is retaliation for Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries and ships in the Black Sea.

Monday's attack by Russia targeted "a civilian vessel in neutral waters carrying corn and owned by Turkey", Volodymyr Zelensky said.

He did not give the location of the ship, but Romania's interior ministry said it had sunk about 30 nautical miles south of its port of Sfantu Gheorghe.

"At around 11:00 (09:00 GMT), Coast Guard border police officers were informed that a fire had broken out on board a commercial vessel located within Romania's exclusive economic zone," the ministry said in a statement.

"Eleven crew members have been rescued. Two deceased persons have also been identified," it added.

Ukraine's president said he had "repeatedly proposed concrete steps to de-escalate the situation and ensure security in the Black Sea" - and other countries had made "relevant proposals" too.

"But Russia consistently chooses terror and sinking civilian vessels instead of normal maritime navigation," Zelensky said.

"Pressure is needed to restore global food security," he added. "And everyone who is genuinely interested in this must help."

On Sunday, Russia's defence ministry said it would intensify its strikes across Ukraine in response to comments made by Zelensky earlier last week, in which he said Kyiv would ramp up its attacks on Russian oil refineries.

Ukraine maintains it began attacking Russian oil infrastructure because it helped the Kremlin finance the war which began with Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022.

President Vladimir Putin admitted last week Kyiv had "got some results" from its refinery attacks and Russia had lost about 1% of its GDP.

The Russian leader has also intensified his rhetoric against Western allies of Ukraine - repeating a threat of even using nuclear weapons.

Western allies have faced a surge in so-called hybrid warfare incidents blamed on Russia, particularly in Poland and the Baltics in recent months.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said last Thursday that his country was preparing for further hybrid attacks, "including serious ones", after a drone armed with explosives was found in August on the tarmac at Leipzig airport close to Ukrainian cargo planes.

The head of Germany's foreign intelligence Martin Jaeger said on Monday that "Germany is in danger of becoming embroiled in a violent conflict with Russia", which was "waging a shadow war" with the threat of attacks against targets in Germany remaining "real and imminent".

World.title: Spain PM pins hopes on housing crisis to help win snap election
World.content:
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro SÃ¡nchez's decision to call a snap election for 29 November came on the back of a parliamentary defeat.

On Friday, the raft of measures he had presented to congress aimed at improving conditions for tenants and trying to address the problem of soaring rentals was narrowly rejected, as parties on the right voted against them.

That parliamentary result confirmed that SÃ¡nchez's left-wing coalition no longer commanded a majority.

But as has so often been the case throughout SÃ¡nchez's career, the calling of the election was not a knee-jerk reaction but a carefully thought-out manouevre.

His government has been struggling in recent months.

His Socialist Party has been mired in corruption, with cases implicating former senior figures in the party, Santos CerdÃ¡n and JosÃ© Luis Ãbalos, while the former Socialist Prime Minister, JosÃ© Luis RodrÃ­guez Zapatero, is facing accusations of having benefited financially from the government's bailout of an airline. Zapatero has denied wrongdoing.

In addition, SÃ¡nchez's wife, BegoÃ±a GÃ³mez, is due to go on trial over allegations of misuse of funds and influence peddling - accusations that GÃ³mez and SÃ¡nchez vehemently deny.

Meanwhile, SÃ¡nchez's administration has struggled to manage the crisis in the Spanish exclave of Ceuta in North Africa, where more than 70,000 migrants suddenly arrived in July. Most have returned over the border to Morocco, but the city has become a political and logistical headache for the prime minister.

World.title: US 'watching closely' after plague researcher dies in Russia
World.content:
President Donald Trump says the US is looking "very strongly" at the case of a Russian lab technician who died at a plague research centre in Siberia.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington was watching closely amid concerns the incident could lead to the spread of pneumonic plague, but there was no cause for alarm.

Announcing the cause of death as "pneumonia of undetermined etiology", Irkutsk's governor said "no micro-organisms" linked to the woman's work had been found "in her biological samples".

Unconfirmed reports suggested the woman fell ill either after breaking a test tube containing the pathogen or following a field trip to a region where plague occurs naturally among wild rodents.

Asked what Washington was going to do about the risk of plague spreading from Russia, Trump said he had not spoken to the Kremlin about it.

"I hate to see them having it," he said, but added: "We'll help. Everybody who has that kind of a problem, we'll always help."

No other cases of staff from the plague institute seeking medical attention since the lab technician's death had been reported, Irkutsk governor Igor Kobzev said, quoting Russia's consumer and health watchdog, Rospotrebnadzor.

The watchdog said a biological safety team had inspected the Anti-Plague Institute of Siberia and the Far East in Irkutsk and found no emergency situation there.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov urged people not to "listen to various rumours" but "rely on Rospotrebnadzor's official statements" instead.

Russian media reported last week that nearly 200 people known to have had contact with the dead woman were under medical observation as a precaution.

Asked by a reporter for an "update on the suspected plague case in Russia", Secretary of State Marco Rubio said: "It seems that there was a worker at the lab that was infected and there's concern that that, you know, could have spread, at least internally - you've seen them do quarantine of this and that nature.

"If something like that gets out, it can quickly spread. So we're watching and monitoring it closely. I don't think it's cause for alarm, but it is cause for focus and the cause to just keep an eye on it and we're doing that."

World.title: Pentagon stops using Anthropic AI tools after blacklisting company, BBC told
World.content:
The US Department of Defence is no longer using Anthropic's AI tools, an official has told the BBC, months after it designated the company a supply chain risk on national security grounds.

The Pentagon "has ceased the use of Anthropic products", the department official said in a statement on Monday.

Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth labelled Anthropic a supply chain risk in February, and announced that the Pentagon would stop using it by late August. It is not clear why there has been a delay.

Multiple people familiar with the matter told the BBC that as recently as last week Anthopic's Claude model was still being used by the department in research, analysis and intelligence gathering as well as in military operations against Iran.

It was viewed as a critical tool for sorting through vast quantities of information, the people said. They include former US defence officials and contractors who have worked closely with the Pentagon specifically on AI.

A spokesman for Anthropic declined to comment when asked about the Pentagon's statement.

The details of the department stopping all use of Anthropic's tools have not been previously reported.

The firm had been used by the US government and military since 2024 and was the first advanced AI company to have its tools deployed in government agencies doing classified work.

But earlier this year, the Pentagon pressed it to remove its safety guardrails from Claude and give the military unfettered access to its AI products.

When Anthropic refused, citing concerns of mass surveillance and autonomous weapons, Hegseth designated the company a "national security supply-chain risk" - a law typically reserved for companies based in countries that pose a threat to the US.

Anthropic said the move was "unprecedented and unlawful" and has sued the Trump administration in an effort to overturn the designation.

World.title: Nobel Prize awarded for revealing inner workings of the brain
World.content:
US psychiatrist and neurologist Karl Deisseroth and his German colleagues Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel have been awarded this year's Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for their work in the field of optogenetics.

Their research has helped scientists learn more about the inner workings of the brain, to better understand how the human mind works.

The Nobel Committee, external praised the trio for laying the foundation of a new era in neuroscience by revealing how to switch on and off neural circuits behind "specific memories, feelings, and behaviours relevant for neurological and psychiatric disorders".

In clinical medicine, researchers are using the method to try to restore sight in people with visual impairment.

World.title: World Teachers’ Day: Abiodun employs 7,000 teachers, commits N24b to education infrastructure
World.content:
The Ogun State Government has announced the employment of over 7,000 teachers since the inception of the Prince Dapo Abiodun administration, as part of its sustained investment in strengthening teaching and learning across the state.

The government has also earmarked ₦24 billion through the State Universal Basic Education Board (SUBEB) for the provision and rehabilitation of critical education infrastructure, while over ₦51 million was presented in cash prizes to outstanding teachers, schools and administrators at the 2026 World Teachers’ Day celebration in Abeokuta.

Speaking at the celebration, held at the Cultural Centre, Kuto, Abeokuta, Governor Abiodun, represented by the Secretary to the State Government, Mr Tokunbo Talabi, said his administration recognised teachers as the foundation upon which every other profession and society was built.

“Before a doctor learns to treat patients or an engineer designs a bridge, a teacher has awakened their minds and laid the foundation they are building upon,” the Governor said.

Abiodun added that behind the achievements celebrated by society were teachers whose names might never make the headlines, but whose influence remained written in the lives they had touched.

He said his administration would continue to invest in teachers, schools and the future of every child in Ogun State, noting that the Ogun State Education Revitalisation Agenda (OGSERA) would continue to drive improvements in curriculum delivery, school management, technology, infrastructure, funding, and the welfare of teachers and learners.

The governor disclosed that the OgunTEACh programme has become a model being emulated beyond Ogun State, following the recruitment of thousands of teachers through the initiative.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He further announced the absorption of over 1,500 OgunTEACh interns into the mainstream civil service, with the beneficiaries receiving their letters of appointment at the ceremony.

Abiodun commended teachers and education administrators in Ogun State for distinguishing themselves nationally and internationally, noting that some of the state’s teachers and education administrators were in Abuja receiving national recognition as Best Teacher, Best Administrator and Best School.

He said the recognition further demonstrated the quality and commitment of teachers in the state and reaffirmed his administration’s determination to create an environment in which educators could thrive.

The Governor also presented cash awards to outstanding teachers, administrators and schools in both public and private school categories.

The first-prize winners in the Best Teacher categories received ₦2.5 million each, while the second- and third-place winners received ₦1.5 million and ₦1 million respectively.

In the public primary school category, Mr Rasaq Babatunde emerged first, Mrs Ayedun Oluwakemi second, and Mrs Ajayi Fatimo Bisola third.

In the junior public school category, Mr Soleye Olugbemi, Mrs Akande Abosede and Mrs Kuye Funmilayo emerged first, second and third respectively, while Mr Adebayo Oluwaseun, Mrs Akomolafe Beatrice and Àjọṣe Aderibigbe took the first, second and third positions respectively in the senior public school category.

In the private teachers’ category, Mrs Akanni Àyọkà of Breakthrough Academy, Akute, and Mr Kehinde Olusegun of Anglican High School, Quarry, emerged first and second respectively.

For the Best Administrators’ public category, Mr Sodipo Raymond of Muslim Primary School, Ago-Oko, Abeokuta, won first prize; Mrs Bankole Oluranti of African Church Primary School 1, Ayetoro, came second; while Mrs Olakitan Silifat of Abeokuta South Local Government Nursery/Primary School, Ijemo, Abeokuta, emerged third.

Community Nursery and Primary School, Mike II, and Christ Apostolic Grammar School, Iperu, received ₦10 million each as Best School in the primary and junior secondary school categories respectively, among other award recipients.

The event also featured the presentation of the Award of Distinguished Leadership in Technology-Driven Education and Innovation to Governor Abiodun in recognition of his administration’s efforts in advancing technology-driven education in the state.

Speaking on the theme of the celebration, “Standing with Teachers: 60 Years of Protecting the Profession, Advancing its Status and Shaping Our Future,” the Ogun State Chairman of the Nigeria Union of Teachers (NUT), Sewakanu Noah Oladipupo, described the theme as a policy-oriented call for improved recognition, status and welfare for teachers.

Oladipupo commended the Abiodun administration for recruiting over 6,000 teachers through the OgunTEACh platform, noting that there had been no recruitment of teachers for eight years before the administration came into office.

He also commended the government for approving and implementing teachers’ promotions from 2016 to 2024, adding that approval had been granted for the implementation of promotions for 2025 and 2026.

The NUT chairman particularly acknowledged the removal of the longstanding ceiling that prevented primary school teachers from progressing beyond Grade Level 16, saying the development had restored parity, hope and dignity to the primary school sector.

Speaking on behalf of the newly appointed teachers, Miss Olasoji Tobiloba expressed appreciation to Governor Abiodun for absorbing the OgunTEACh interns into the mainstream civil service.

She assured the government that the beneficiaries would reciprocate the gesture through greater diligence, commitment and dedication to duty.

The celebration brought together government officials, education administrators, teachers, union leaders, school proprietors and other stakeholders to mark the contribution of teachers to the development of Ogun State and the nation.

World.title: Military Aircraft Crash: Ondo governor orders emergency, logistics support
World.content:
Following the crash of an ATR-42 aircraft in Igbokoda, Ondo State, on Monday, the state governor, Lucky Aiyedatiwa, has directed the deployment of logistics and emergency support from the Ministry of Health and Emergency Agency to the scene.

He said the deployment was to support the ongoing search-and-rescue exercise.

This was contained in a statement by the Chief Press Secretary to Ebenezer Adeniyan.

The aircraft was flying from Benin to Lagos on a routine mission and crashed in the early hours of Monday, killing seven crew members and 25 passengers on board.

The crash occurred in a swampy area of Igbokoda, the headquarters of Ilaje LGA of Ondo State.

According to preliminary reports confirmed by the Nigerian Air Force Director of Public Relations and Information, Ehimen Ejodame, an air commodore, the aircraft, an ATR-42 with tail number NGR 931, was on a routine mission from Benin to Lagos when it crashed in a swampy area opposite the Naval Base in Igbokoda.

The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, also confirmed that 25 passengers and seven crew members were on board.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Adeniyan said Governor Aiyedatiwa received the news of the crash with deep sadness.

He said he has been in contact with the leadership of the Nigerian Air Force, the Ilaje Local Government Chairman, Maurice Oripelaye, and security agencies on the ground.

“To aid ongoing efforts, Governor Aiyedatiwa has directed the State Emergency Management Agency (SEMA), the Ministry of Health, and relevant security agencies to immediately mobilise and offer full logistical and human support to the Nigerian Air Force and other emergency response agencies in the search and rescue operations currently ongoing at the crash site,” the statement said.

“The Governor has also directed that the area be cordoned off and secured to allow for smooth and unhindered rescue operations, while urging residents of Igbokoda and adjoining communities to remain calm, cooperate with emergency responders, and refrain from spreading unverified information.”

READ ALSO: What we know about Nigerian military aircraft that fatally crashed Monday

He said the state government will continue to monitor the situation and provide updates as more information becomes available from the Nigerian Air Force.

“On behalf of the Government and good people of Ondo State, Governor Aiyedatiwa expresses his heartfelt sympathy to the Chief of Air Staff, the entire Nigerian Air Force family, and the families of all personnel and passengers on board the ill-fated aircraft. Our thoughts and prayers are with them at this difficult time,” he said.

“We pray for the safety of our gallant officers and for the success of the rescue efforts.”

World.title: Military Aircraft Crash: Tinubu declares three-day mourning, says victims to be named
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has declared a three-day national mourning for Air Force personnel who died in the crash of a military plane today.

He also directed that flags should be flown at half-mast throughout the country as a mark of respect to the officers.

President Tinubu had earlier expressed profound sadness over the crash of the Nigerian Air Force ATR-42 jet.

The accident occurred near a naval base in the Igbokoda area of Ondo State. The aircraft, carrying 25 passengers and seven crew members, was on a routine mission from Benin to Lagos when it crashed.

“This is a painful moment for our Armed Forces and for the entire nation. Our Air Force personnel put their lives on the line every day to secure Nigeria. Their sacrifice will never be forgotten,” President Tinubu declared in a condolence message to the Chief of Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Aneke, and all officers, airmen, and airwomen of the Nigerian Air Force.

“The Chief of Air Staff has briefed me, and I have directed the Nigerian Air Force to immediately commence a thorough investigation into the cause of the crash to prevent future occurrences.

“I commend the Nigerian Air Force for activating an immediate search and rescue operation following the accident.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The Air Force will release the officers’ names after contacting their families.

Bayo Onanuga

Special Adviser to the President

(Information & Strategy)

October 5, 2026

World.title: EFCC hands over N107m recovered from property fraud to Lagos victim
World.content:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has handed over N107 million recovered from a disputed land transaction to a Lagos resident who petitioned the commission after he could not take possession of the property.

In a statement on Monday, the agency’s spokesperson, Dele Oyewale, said it handed over the money in bank drafts to the petitioner through his lawyer, Babatunde Oni, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN).

The handover took place at the EFCC’s Lagos Zonal Directorate 2 office in Ikoyi, Lagos, on 30 September.

The statement revealed that the petitioner had alleged that he was defrauded in the transaction involving Adeola Ibrahim, Bolanle Bamgbose, and others.

The EFCC said the petitioner became interested in a parcel of land at Iya Oloye Crescent, off Ikorodu Road, Lagos, in October 2024 after it was introduced to him by Olalekan Kazeem and another person identified as Alfa.

The land was offered to him for N150 million.

The petitioner later engaged Bolanle Bamgbose & Associates to conduct due diligence and handle the transaction with a purported representative of the seller, identified as Monsuru, popularly known as “Area”.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

But the amount eventually paid in connection with the transaction was higher than the agreed price.

According to the EFCC, the petitioner paid N163 million to the law firm, N3 million to Kazeem, whom the commission described as an agent, and N1.575 million to a surveyor.

The payments totalled N167.575 million.

The petitioner, however, could not take possession of the land after a dispute arose over the property.

He tried to recover his money or gain possession of the land but was unsuccessful, the EFCC said.

He then petitioned the commission through Babatunde Oni SAN & Co., alleging obtaining money by false pretence, conspiracy and extortion.

The EFCC said its investigation led to the recovery of N107 million, which was returned to the petitioner on 30 September.

The recovery represents about two-thirds of the N167.575 million the petitioner allegedly paid in connection with the transaction. Based on the figures provided by the commission, N60.575 million remains unrecovered.

Recently, the agency arraigned a man over an alleged N13.6 million property fraud at the Oyo State High Court, Ibadan, Oyo State.

In July, the commission also announced the arraignment of two brothers over alleged land fraud in Port Harcourt and the arraignment of two FCDA staff members over alleged property fraud.

Speaking during the handover, the Acting Zonal Director of the Lagos Zonal Directorate 2, Bawa Kaltungo, said the commission would continue to recover funds linked to financial crimes and return them to their rightful owners where established.

The EFCC stated that the investigation into the matter is part of its work on suspected land and property fraud.

World.title: Tinubu returns to Abuja after five weeks
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu has returned to Abuja, about five weeks after he travelled abroad on a “working vacation” and about a week after he returned to the country.

The Nigerian leader arrived in Abuja on Monday evening from Lagos, where he arrived following his working vacation in the UK and France.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that Mr Tinubu left Nigeria on 30 August for an initial three-week leave, which was later extended. He returned to Lagos, Nigeria, last Tuesday, where he stayed until his return to Abuja on Monday.

World.title: NPFL: Inter Lagos hit with ₦5 million fine, three-point deduction over officials’ assault
World.content:
Inter Lagos have been hit with a series of disciplinary sanctions by the Nigeria Premier Football League (NPFL) after breaching the NPFL27 Framework & Rules during their Matchday 7 fixture against Katsina United on Sunday, 4 October.

The Lagos-based club have been sanctioned over a series of incidents surrounding the match, including “inadequate security, the harassment and assault of match officials, and the failure to control their officials and supporters after the final whistle.”

According to the disciplinary decision, “Inter Lagos failed to provide adequate and effective security at the venue, allowing unauthorised persons to gain access to restricted areas.

“The security breach subsequently led to an attack on the match officials as they made their way from the dressing room to their vehicle after the game.”

The situation reportedly escalated further as Inter Lagos failed to ensure proper conduct among their officials and supporters, resulting in the match officials being held hostage for more than an hour after the match.

The league also found that some Inter Lagos officials, alongside supporters of the club, intimidated, harassed and verbally abused the match officials in conduct deemed capable of bringing the game into disrepute.

More seriously, the club’s team manager, together with some supporters, assaulted the match officials.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The first assistant referee was injured in the face during the incident and also lost personal belongings, while his mobile telephone was damaged.

As a result of the breaches, Inter Lagos have been handed multiple financial sanctions.

The club were fined #2 million for failing to provide adequate and effective security and another #1 million for holding the match officials hostage for more than an hour.

The club was also fined an additional #2 million for assaulting the match officials. In contrast, a further #250,000 has been ordered as compensation to the affected assistant referee for the loss of his personal items, damage to his mobile phone and medical treatment for the injury sustained during the incident.

READ ALSO: NPFL summons Sporting Lagos coach Buter over refereeing criticism

Beyond the financial penalties, Inter Lagos has suffered a major sporting punishment: 3 points and 3 goals will be deducted from the club’s accrued points and goals tally for assaulting and injuring the first assistant referee.

The sanctions could therefore significantly affect Inter Lagos’ campaign as they continue their NPFL season.

The Lagos club have 48 hours from the date of notification to appeal the sanctions.

World.title: Olympic Qualifier: Oshoala, Plumptre pull out as Falcons begin preparations for Comoros clash
World.content:
Nigeria’s Super Falcons began preparations for their 2028 Olympic qualifying campaign on Monday with 14 players training in Ikenne, but several key players will miss the two-legged encounter against Comoros.

Defender Ashley Plumptre and forward Asisat Oshoala have been excused from the assignment. Meanwhile, Benfica duo Oluwatosin Demehin and Flourish Sabastine will not join the squad because of resident permit issues.

Plumptre requested to be excused after suffering a sprain and ligament injury, while Oshoala was also granted permission to miss the assignment.

The absences have forced interim head coach Augustine Eguavoen to adjust his squad, with Belarus-based former U20 forward Blessing Okpe called up to replace Oshoala.

Eguavoen has also released two players initially invited for the Olympic qualifiers to the Flamingos.

Oluwakemi Adegbuyi, the Most Valuable Player of the recently concluded WAFU-B U17 Girls Cup competition in Yamoussoukro, and Favour Nkwocha, who featured for the Falconets at the FIFA U20 Women’s World Cup in Poland, have returned to the U17 team.

The Flamingos are scheduled to leave Nigeria on Wednesday for the FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

14 players train in Ikenne

Despite the withdrawals, Eguavoen had 14 players available for Monday evening’s training session at the Remo Stars Stadium.

Goalkeeper Christiana Uzoma trained alongside defenders Farida Abdulwahab, Tumininu Adeshina, Valentina Uroko, Glory Edet, Shukurat Oladipo and Glory Ogbonna.

Oluchi Omenazu, Joy Igbokwe, Fatimoh Solaty and Suliat Abideen formed the midfield group, while forwards Shakirat Moshood, Blessing Nkor and Sandra John completed the group.

Eleven more players are expected to join the squad as preparations intensify.

Among those expected are goalkeeper Chiamaka Nnadozie, defender Michelle Alozie, midfielders Christy Ucheibe, Toni Payne and Jennifer Echegini, as well as captain Rasheedat Ajibade and forward Gift Monday.

Joy Omewa, Janet Akekoromowei and Uchenna Kanu are also expected in camp.

The arrival of the established players will give Eguavoen more options as he works to settle his team ahead of the crucial qualifying tie.

Falcons seek another Olympic appearance

Nigeria returned to the Women’s Olympic Football Tournament at Paris 2024 after a 16-year absence.

The 10-time African champions are now seeking back-to-back appearances at the Games, with Los Angeles 2028 their next target.

The Falcons will host Comoros in the first leg on Friday before the return fixture at the Remo Stars Stadium on Tuesday, 13 October.

READ ALSO: Super Falcons begin Olympic qualifier preparations with nine players in camp

The short turnaround between the two matches leaves Eguavoen with limited preparation time, making the arrival of the remaining players particularly important.

For the Falcons, the immediate objective is to secure a favourable result in the opening encounter and take control of the tie before the return leg.

The Olympic qualifying campaign also gives Nigeria a chance to respond after a disappointing 2026 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations campaign and its subsequent failure to qualify for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup.

World.title: ACAMB @ 30: Communications professionals urged to embrace innovation, AI, data
World.content:
Association of Corporate Communication and Marketing Professionals in Banks (ACAMB) has marked 30 years of shaping narratives and building trust in Nigeria’s banking industry, with regulators and industry leaders calling on communication professionals to make credibility, clarity, Innovation and ethical conduct central to the future of financial services.

The association celebrated the milestone at an anniversary gala night in Lagos on September 30, 2026, bringing together, senior officials of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), the Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria (CIBN), the Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System (NIBSS), United Bank for Africa (UBA), Optimus Bank and industry leaders alongside communication and marketing heads, from banks across the country.

Speaking at the event, President of ACAMB, Jide Sipe, said, over three decades, the association has played and continued to play a critical role in helping banks communicate with the public, manage crises and protect institutional reputation.

“For 30 years, our members have stood between the banks and the public they serve. They explain policy, manage crises and protect reputations, often under intense pressure and in real time,” Sipe said.

“We have remained consistent, from gatekeepers to strategic drivers in actualising growth, positive brand perception, aligning business values to customer needs, customer satisfaction and loyalty”

All this have to great extent catalysed the growth trajectory of the financial sector and to that, we feel a sense of pride, worthy of celebration,

He said the association would continue to strengthen the capacity of its members as the communications profession evolves, with greater focus on artificial intelligence, data and digital media, as well as mentorship for young professionals entering the industry.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Though the tools have changed since 1996, but the mandate remains same. We continue to earn trust, one credible message at a time, and we will guard it with the same discipline for the next 30 years and beyond,” he added.

While giving his address, Chairman of the occasion and 24th President of CIBN, Dele Alabi, described ACAMB’s 30-year journey as a testament to perseverance, professionalism and one that made far reaching impact the financial services industry should be proud of.

Alabi, who also commended Sipe’s leadership and recalled their years together at Ecobank Group, said ACAMB had helped strengthen communication, reputation and trust across the banking sector.

“Thirty years of shaping narratives and building trust reflects ACAMB’s critical role in strengthening communication, enhancing reputation and fostering trust across the financial services industry,” he said.

He urged communication professionals to embrace innovation without compromising ethics, in line with the CIBN’s IMPACT vision, which is built around inclusion, membership, professionalism and ethical conduct, accountability, competences & skills, and technology.

Representing the Deputy Governor of the CBN, Philip Ikeazor, the Acting Director, Corporate Communications and Investor Relations, Hakama Sidi Ali, said the banking industry was moving beyond stabilisation towards broader institutional transformation.

She challenged communication professionals to prioritise clarity over cleverness and to view customers as the ultimate test of the effectiveness and credibility of their communication.

“The credibility you carry into a crisis is built in quiet periods,” she said.

Delivering the keynote address, Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer of NIBSS, Premier Oiwoh, said the growth of digital banking had made trust even more critical, as financial services increasingly moved to mobile and digital platforms.

He noted that NIBSS had built Africa’s first mature instant payment system 15 years ago, adding that the evolution of digital banking had made trust a fundamental requirement for the continued growth of the financial system.

“Banking is all about trust. Without trust, banking cannot stand,” Oiwoh said.

Delivering a goodwill message on behalf of the Group Managing Director/CEO of UBA, Oliver Alawuba, the bank’s Group Head, Marketing and Corporate Communications, Alero Ladipo, commended ACAMB for creating a platform that brings communication professionals together across competing institutions.

“Thirty years is more than a milestone. It is evidence of relevance, resilience and the ability to evolve,” Ladipo said.

She noted that while banks compete in the market, communication professionals have a shared responsibility to strengthen confidence in the banking industry and maintain public trust in the financial system.

“Competition may separate us in the market, but there are moments when the industry must speak with a shared sense of responsibility,” she added.

Managing Director/CEO, Optimus Bank, Ademola Odeyemi, also commended ACAMB for it’s yeoman contributions over the years and shared vision, it has continued to effectively articulate on behalf of the banks, a feat that has helped the financial sector thrive collectively.

The anniversary celebration also featured networking sessions and recognition of professionals who have contributed to the growth of banking communication in Nigeria over the past three decades.

World.title: US warns foreign financial institutions not to do business with Iran
World.content:
US President Donald Trump speaks during a meeting with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun in the Oval Office of the White House in Washington, DC, on July 21, 2026. (Photo by SAUL LOEB / AFP)

The United States on Monday warned foreign financial institutions that if they conducted any business with Iran or its banking sector they could be sanctioned by Washington.

“Foreign financial institutions continuing to transact with sanctioned Iranian financial institutions could be targeted at any time without advance notification and should take immediate action to terminate such activity and relationships,” the US Treasury said in an “alert” statement.

The United States launched its war against Iran in late February, killing the country’s leadership and demanding it cease any nuclear-related activities.

The war has plunged the Middle East into violence, with Tehran’s retaliatory action targeting Washington’s Gulf allies and sending global energy and fertilizer prices skyrocketing after it virtually shut a key trading route.

Since late August, Washington has stepped up its campaign to economically isolate Tehran, warning its allies that they would be hit by secondary sanctions if they continued to conduct transactions with the country’s government.

The US Treasury has also announced a slew of new sanctions as part of that push, targeting Iran’s financial, cryptocurrency, rail, automotive and manufacturing sectors.

It has also taken action against two banks — one in the United Arab Emirates and another in Turkey — over their alleged aid to the authorities in Tehran.

In Monday’s statement, the Treasury said Iran’s government operated so-called “shadow banking” channels to circumvent US sanctions, and that foreign financial institutions should aim to identify and avoid any such activities.

AFP

World.title: Defence Minister expresses deep sorrow over crash of NAF aircraft
World.content:
By Kingsley Omonobi

Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa Rtd, has expressed deep sorrow over the tragic crash of NAF ATR 42 aircraft and the loss of officers and airmen who were involved in a routine flight mission to Lagos, describing them as personnel who exemplified the highest standards of loyalty and commitment to the defence of the country.

In a statement he personally signed, Gen Musa offered condolences to President Bola Tinubu, the leadership of the Armed Forces, and most especially, the immediate families, loved ones, and colleagues of our fallen heroes.

He said, “It is with a profound sense of grief and heavy heart that I, on behalf of the Ministry of Defence and the entire Armed Forces of Nigeria, express deep sorrow over the tragic crash of our military aircraft with tail number NAF 931 involving dedicated personnel of the Armed Forces.

“This painful incident claimed the lives of brave officers and airmen who were engaged in routine flight mission while serving our nation with courage, unyielding devotion, and selfless patriotism.

“The loss of these valiant patriots is an irreparable blow not only to the military high command and their comrades-in-arms, but to the entire Federal Republic of Nigeria.

“These fine officers and men exemplify the highest standards of military professionalism, loyalty, and commitment to the defence of our Fatherland.

“On behalf of the Ministry of Defence, I extend our heartfelt condolences to the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu, the leadership of the Armed Forces, and most especially, the immediate families, loved ones, and colleagues of our fallen heroes.

“We share in your immense grief and stand shoulder-to-shoulder with you during this tragic hour.

“Our hearts also go out to the families of the civilians on board the ill-fated aircraft, we share your grief.

“A comprehensive investigation into the circumstances surrounding this unfortunate crash has been ordered to ascertain the cause and ensure all necessary operational safety protocols are reinforced across our military aviation units.

“We pray that the Almighty God grants the souls of the departed eternal repose, and give their families, the military community, and all Nigerians the fortitude to bear this irreparable loss.”

World.title: Olise powers France to win over Belgium in Nations League
World.content:
France’s midfielder #11 Michael Olise celebrates after scoring his team’s fourth goal during the UEFA Nations League Group A1 football match between France and Belgium at the Stade de France in Saint-Denis, north of Paris, on October 5, 2026. (Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP)

Michael Olise came off the bench to inspire France to a 4-1 win over Belgium in the UEFA Nations League on Monday, handing Zinedine Zidane his first home victory since taking charge.

Use up and down arrow keys to resize the meta box pane.

Dodi Lukebakio put Belgium on course for their first competitive win over Les Bleus in 45 years when he fired the visitors in front in the first half at the Stade de France.

But France turned the match on its head in a blistering finish, scoring four times in the final 13 minutes to preserve Zidane’s unbeaten start and move closer to the quarter-finals.

Desire Doue hauled France level in the 77th minute with a low drive from the edge of the area before Olise teed up Rayan Cherki to fire them ahead four minutes later.

Olise then put the result beyond doubt with a third goal before adding another in stoppage time to cap a stunning French comeback.

France, who also beat Belgium 1-0 in Brussels last week thanks to a late Olise goal, moved three points clear of Italy at the top of Group A1, with Belgium another point back. Italy beat Turkey 3-1 in Bologna to condemn their opponents to a fourth straight loss.

Former World Cup and Ballon d’Or winner Zidane heavily rotated his team for the last match of this two-week long international window, with only Dembele keeping his place among the 10 changes.

Manchester United defender Leny Yoro and Toulouse goalkeeper Guillaume Restes made their France debuts, with Ousmane Dembele again captaining the side in the absence of the injured Kylian Mbappe.

Belgium were without the suspended duo of Kevin De Bruyne and Youri Tielemans but caught France cold when Romeo Lavia’s superb ball split open the home defence, allowing Lukebakio to race clear and tuck away a clinical finish.

Maarten Vandevoordt, making his debut in goal for Belgium, kept out efforts from Esteban Lepaul and Cherki as France pressed for an equaliser, but the dam eventually burst.

Doue gathered the ball and shot on the turn, beyond the reach of Vandevoordt, to haul France level. Cherki then turned home a cutback from Olise to give the hosts the lead as the Bayern Munich winger stole the show late on.

Olise scrambled in a third in the 88th minute and rolled in a fourth after skilful work from Doue to complete a remarkable turnaround.

AFP

World.title: Tinubu arrives Abuja after Lagos engagements
World.content:
FILE IMAGE

By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

President Bola Tinubu on Monday evening arrived in Abuja after spending a few days in Lagos following his return to Nigeria from a working vacation in Europe.

The President’s aircraft touched down at the Presidential Wing of the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, at about 7:45 p.m.

He was received on arrival by the National Security Adviser, NSA, Mallam Nuhu Ribadu; Director of Protocol at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Ibrahim Sule Dan Agundi, and some senior security officials.

Tinubu’s return to Abuja brings to an end his stay in Lagos, where he had carried out a series of official and political engagements following his return from Europe.

Recall that President Tinubu had returned to Lagos on Tuesday last week from working vacation in Europe, during which he stayed in London and Paris and held meetings with political and business interests.

Speaking briefly with journalists shortly after his arrival in Lagos, Tinubu dismissed concerns over his health and declared himself fit and ready to resume full duties.

“Ready to kick, ready to work. There’s nothing wrong. Rumour will always be emanating from politics, but the facts remain I’m here: healthy, sound and ready to go”, the President had said.

Asked about his vacation, Tinubu simply replied “I enjoyed myself”.

Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, who was among senior officials who received him in Lagos, had expressed optimism that the President would return to work with renewed energy after his time away.

While in Lagos, Tinubu participated in activities marking Nigeria’s 66th Independence Anniversary, including the national premiere of MKO, a documentary on the life and democratic struggle of the late Chief Moshood Kashimawo Olawale Abiola.

The President, accompanied by First Lady Senator Oluremi Tinubu, attended the October 1 screening at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Creative Arts in Lagos.

The documentary chronicled Abiola’s political journey, the annulment of the June 12, 1993 presidential election and the pro-democracy struggle that followed.

Tinubu also received senior government officials and political leaders during his stay in Lagos, including Vice President Kashim Shettima, who visited him at his residence on Saturday.

After the meeting, Shettima said he had remained in regular contact with the President throughout his stay abroad and described Tinubu as fully engaged with developments in the country.

The Vice President also defended the administration’s economic reforms, saying difficult decisions taken since 2023 were necessary to stabilise the economy and lay the foundation for recovery.

It is expected that Tinubu’s return to Abuja will kick-start his re-election campaigns in different parts of the country.

World.title: Ondo plane crash: No survivors yet, only wreckage, IDs – Gov Aiyedatiwa
World.content:
Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa

By Cynthia Alo

Ondo State Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa has said no survivor has been recovered from Monday’s military aircraft crash in Igbokoda, Ilaje Local Government Area of the state, with only wreckage of wings, identity cards and uniforms seen.

Aiyedatiwa said rescue teams are yet to access the main body of the aircraft because it went deep into the swamp.

The governor disclosed this on Monday night during an interview on Politics Today, a Channels Television programme.

He said the aircraft, with 32 persons on board, 25 passengers and seven crew members, was a surveillance aircraft on its way from Benin to Lagos, which lost radio signal at about 9:15 a.m.

He said information got to him at about 10:30 a.m. from the chairman of Ilaje Local Government that residents heard a sound like an air tremor before the aircraft dived into a swamp directly facing the Naval Forward Operating Base in Igbokoda.

“They saw the wreckage from the wings, some ID cards and uniforms indicating it was a military aircraft. The main body went deep into the swamp area. They haven’t been able to search the aircraft itself yet,” he said.

He said naval personnel, local emergency officials, Amotekun and residents moved into the creek with boats immediately the crash occurred, but no living soul was found.

He said the site has been cordoned off, while hospitals in Igbokoda and Okitipupa have been placed on standby with ambulances recently procured for the 18 local governments.

The governor said the Nigerian Air Force and the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau are investigating and will need to recover the black box to determine the exact cause.

Speaking on the recent elimination of Abdussamad Ohida, a top ISWAP coordinator in Ondo forest, Aiyedatiwa said the clearance operation took place about five days ago after months of top secret surveillance.

He said it was a joint operation involving the DSS, Nigerian Army, British intelligence officers and Amotekun, with no casualties recorded on the side of security forces.

The governor explained that the coordinator took over after his former superior, a Central Nigeria ISWAP leader, was arrested by the DSS in 2023, adding that intelligence was generated from that arrest and from tracking of another leader earlier eliminated by DSS.

He revealed that the criminals carry sophisticated weapons beyond AK-47, including GPMG, and had retaliated when security first launched attack.

“When we launched the first attack, they retaliated. So we had to move back, heavily arm, do serious intelligence and mapping before we re-launched,” he said.

Aiyedatiwa said the role of the UK was provision of intelligence and precision targeting equipment that Amotekun does not have, while Amotekun provided knowledge of terrain because many of its operatives are recruited local hunters.

He said Ondo’s vast forests sharing boundaries with Kogi, Edo, Ekiti and Oyo have become a corridor for criminals fleeing military operations in Kogi and Kwara axis.

According to him, what started as farmer-herder clashes years ago has graduated to terrorism, linking the group to the 2025 December 31 attack on Ipele police station and the 2022 Owo massacre.

On whether the group plans to disrupt 2027 elections, he said their agenda in totality is to kill, destroy and disrupt in any form.

World.title: Nine die in Ogun road crash
World.content:
By James Ogunnaike

No fewer than nine persons lost their lives in a fatal road traffic crash along the JBD/ORE route in Ijebu-Ode, Ogun State on Monday.

According to the statement signed by Afolabi Odunsi, Chief Route Commander and Sector Public Education Officer, FRSC Ogun State Sector Command, the crash occurred at about 4:55 p.m. at the Bethel area within the Ijebu-Ode Unit Command.

According to the FRSC, the crash involved a white Toyota Hiace commercial bus, with registration number 14B-299DT, belonging to Delta Line, and a white Sino Truck commercial vehicle, with registration number AAB162XD, belonging to Bill Gas Solution Ltd.

The nine occupants of the two vehicles were all killed in the crash.

The FRSC said the incident occurred while it was raining and the road pavement was wet.

“Preliminary investigation identified speed violation (SPV) as the probable cause of the crash,” the statement said.

The road safety agency said its rescue team arrived at the scene within two minutes of receiving the report, at about 4:58 p.m.

It added that the bodies of the victims were evacuated and deposited at the General Hospital morgue, Ijebu-Ode, while the vehicles were towed to the Ilese Police Station by the Ilese Police Motor Traffic Division.

The Sector Commander, FRSC Ogun State Command, Corps Commander Oludare Ogunjobi, urged motorists, particularly commercial vehicle operators, to exercise maximum caution while driving in the rain.

Ogunjobi advised motorists to obey speed limits, maintain safe following distances and avoid driving behaviours capable of endangering lives.

He warned that speeding on wet roads was particularly dangerous because reduced tyre grip and visibility could make it difficult for motorists to control their vehicles or stop safely.

The FRSC expressed condolences to the families of the victims and urged all road users to make safety their priority at all times.

World.title: Crash: Tinubu declares three-day mourning for Air Force personnel
World.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

President Bola Tinubu has declared a three-day national mourning for Air Force personnel who died in the crash of a military plane on Monday.

He also directed that flags should be flown at half-mast throughout the country as a mark of respect to the officers.

President Tinubu had earlier expressed profound sadness over the crash of the Nigerian Air Force ATR-42 jet.

The accident occurred near a naval base in the Igbokoda area of Ondo State.

A statement by the presidential spokesman, Mr. Bayo Onanuga, said the aircraft, carrying 25 passengers and seven crew members, was on a routine mission from Benin to Lagos when it crashed.

“This is a painful moment for our Armed Forces and for the entire nation. Our Air Force personnel put their lives on the line every day to secure Nigeria. Their sacrifice will never be forgotten,”

President Tinubu declared in a condolence message to the Chief of Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, and all officers, airmen, and airwomen of the Nigerian Air Force.

“The Chief of Air Staff has briefed me, and I have directed the Nigerian Air Force to immediately commence a thorough investigation into the cause of the crash to prevent future occurrences.

“I commend the Nigerian Air Force for activating an immediate search and rescue operation following the accident,” he said.

The Air Force will release the officers’ names after contacting their families.

World.title: Ronaldo resumes Al Nassr training after Portugal camp rift
World.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Cristiano Ronaldo has returned to Al Nassr training after leaving Portugal’s camp last week amid a dispute with head coach Jorge Jesus.

Al Nassr confirmed the forward’s return on Monday by posting pictures of Ronaldo training with his teammates, with the caption: “The GOAT. In the heart of Najd. At Al Nassr.”

Ronaldo later posted pictures on his official Instagram account, confirming his return to training, with the caption: “🟡🔵”.

The 41-year-old is now preparing for Al Nassr’s next Saudi Pro League fixture against Al Diriyah on Friday, October 9.

His return to club duty comes as efforts continue to resolve the fallout with Portugal, with the Portuguese Football Federation reportedly planning a meeting with Ronaldo in an attempt to repair the relationship between the player, Jesus and the national team.

Vanguard had earlier reported that Jesus and FPF president Pedro Proença followed Ronaldo to Copenhagen airport in an unsuccessful attempt to persuade him to remain with Portugal.

Bruno Fernandes has also played down suggestions of a split within the squad, saying there are “no divisions” in the national team and describing Ronaldo as Portugal’s “greatest symbol”.

Portugal subsequently secured their place in the Nations League quarter-finals after beating Norway 2-1.

Jesus has since left the door open for Ronaldo’s return, saying the forward can come back to the national team if he wants to.

Ronaldo is now back with Al Nassr as attention turns to his club return.

World.title: Understrength Super Eagles Battle Russia in Novgorod
World.content:
Duro Ikhazuagbe

Nigeria and Russia will play an International friendly at the Sovcombank Arena in Nizhny Novgorod this evening (5pm) with the host European nation aiming for victory against the Super Eagles without nine of the team’s starting 11 players.

The three-time AFCON winning nation was weakened by injuries and refusal by some of the European clubs to released Super Eagles players in their folds for the last game of the September-October international window.

Top star like Victor Osimhen who missed Nigeria’s two 2027 AFCON qualifiers against Madagascar and Guinea-Bissau was again left out of this Russian friendly as he’s yet to return to full fitness for Galatasaray, his Turkish Super Lig side. Ademola Lookman was excused based on representation from his Spanish side, Atletico Madrid.

Eight other players that featured for Nigeria in the 2027 AFCON qualifier against Guinea-Bissau also skipped the game here in Novgorod this evening,

However, Eagles’ Franco-Malian gaffer, Eric Chelle, appears not perturbed as the match presents him another opportunity to try out new players in different departments of the team

Meanwhile, it has been confirmed that Russia’s standout player, goalkeeper Matvey Safonov, will miss Tuesday’s encounter in Nizhny Novgorod.

Safonov left the Russian camp on Saturday to return to Paris Saint-Germain. He featured in Russia’s opening friendly against Iran on September 29, but was left out of the squad that routed Namibia 6–0 on Saturday.

With no injury reported, the goalkeeper is understood to have returned early to rest and prepare for a demanding club schedule. Safonov is currently locked in a battle with French goalkeeper Lucas Chevalier for PSG’s starting role, and any lapse could cost him his place in the lineup.

In his absence, one of Aleksandr Maksimenko, Anton Mitryushkin, or Stanislav Agkatsev is expected to start between the posts for Russia.

On 6 June last year, Russia and Nigeria played a 1-1 draw at Moscow’s Luzhniki Stadium, with the Russians going in front through an own goal by defender Semi Ajayi, before Tolu Arokodare levelled for the Super Eagles.
