World.title: Iheanacho Unfazed by Absence from Eagles, Remains Passionate Playing for Nigeria
World.content:
Marvelous David

Kelechi ‘Senior Man’ Iheanacho who is returning to the Super Eagles after over 16 months absence has restated his passion to represent Nigeria football in whatever capacity.

The Bursaspor forward in the Turkish second-tier division league, is one of the players selected by Coach Eric Chelle for the international friendly with Russia in Novgorod this evening.

Speaking with NFF TV from the Russian city yesterday, Iheanacho said despite last playing for the Super Eagles at the 2025 Unity Cup final against Jamaica in London, he remains passionate to wear the Nigerian colours at whatever level.

“I have been in the Super Eagles, even in the national team in general, for a long time, starting from the U13 to U15 to U17 and all the rest of them, the Super Eagles,” observed Iheanacho who won the Golden Ball at the 2013 FIFA U17 World Cup in UAE.

He dismissed critics who queried why he was returning to the team he last played for on May 31, 2015.

“So I have been very long here and I am not coming to the national team because of anybody or anything. It’s because of the love and passion I have for the game.

“It’s the dream of everyone to play for the Super Eagles as long as you’re Nigerian. I have been living that dream for a long time to play in the national team from a junior level up to here. Even if it’s 5-a-side Eagles are playing or I’m invited to the U15s, I’ll play because of my passion.

“I don’t care what anybody says. As long as the coach gave me a call-up, I will play, so it’s a thing of joy and I am loving it.

“I’m really happy to be here and I will enjoy it with the boys and hopefully we will have a very lovely outing “(against Russia) on Tuesday (today).”

Iheanacho left Celtic for Bursaspor after helping the Scottish side to decent performance last season.

Since his arrival in summer as a free agent, Iheanacho has had a blistering start to the 2026-27 season, registering an impressive 11 goals and two assists in nine appearances for Bursaspor

He also dismissed those relegating the Turkish league as people not informed about the quality therein.

“It’s a good league, to be fair. I don’t know how people rate the league but it is a really good league, and it’s not easy as people think.

“When you play there, you’ll know whether it’s easy or not. Obviously, my teammates will testify to that as well. I’m enjoying it and I know they are enjoying it as well. You can say it favours Nigerians but it’s a really good league,” concludes the former Manchester City and Leicester City player.

World.title: Super Falcons Open LA 2028 Olympics Qualifiers Camp with 14 Players
World.content:
A total of 14 players trained yesterday evening as Nigeria’s Super Falcons commenced preparations for Friday’s 2028 Olympics Women’s Football Tournament qualifying match against the senior women national team of Comoros.

Both teams will clash again in the return at the same Remo Stars Stadium on Tuesday evening.

Two years ago, the 10-time African champions made their return to the Women’s Olympic Football Tournament after a 16-year absence, and the Falcons are determined to again show up in Los Angeles in the summer of 2018.

Interim Head Coach, Augustine Eguavoen, has released Oluwakemi Adegbuyi (Most Valuable Player of the recently-concluded WAFU-B U17 Girls Cup competition in Yamoussoukro) and Favour Nkwocha (who featured for the Falconets at the FIFA U20 Women’s World Cup in Poland) back to the U17 women’s team, Flamingos. Defender Ashley Plumptre has pleaded to be excused due to injury (sprain and ligament), and SL Benfica of Portugal duo of defender Oluwatosin Demehin and forward Flourish Sabastine will not be coming due to resident permit pursuits.

With five-time Africa Player of the Year Asisat Oshoala also pleading to be excused, Eguavoen has had to call up Belarus-based former U20 team forward Blessing Okpe.

World.title: Roanldo’s Future Not Certain as Curtain Falls on Messi’s Argentina Career Today
World.content:
As Lionel Messi prepares to get a hero’s farewell for his successful international career, Cristiano Ronaldo’s could have ended with him running down the tunnel at the final whistle of a game he did not play.

After the World Cup, Argentina’s Messi, 39, decided to retire from international football, while Ronaldo, 41, opted to play on for Portugal.

Yet there is the possibility that Messi’s Argentina career will end up lasting a few days longer – with a home friendly with Benin Republic today in Buenos-Aires marked as his final game.

Ronaldo, furious at being made to warm up and not be brought on against Norway in the Nations League, walked out on the Portugal squad after finding out he would not start against Denmark either.

The Al-Nassr forward has scored 146 goals and won 234 caps for Portugal – both world records.

After such a high-profile falling-out with new boss Jorge Jesus, also a larger than life character who does not back down, Ronaldo is facing a big decision.

Jesus has insisted he would be welcome back if he wants to return and talks between Ronaldo, his representatives and the Portuguese FA are ongoing as they look for a solution.

While Ronaldo could not carry on playing forever, this is not how he would have expected his international career to end.

World.title: NPFL Slams Inter Lagos with N5.25m Fine for Rule Breaches
World.content:
*To be ducked three points, three goals for allowing fans attacks on match officials

Marvelous David

Inter Lagos have been charged for breaching NPFL27 Framework & Rules in the course of their Match-day 7 fixture vs Katsina United on Sunday, October 4, 2026.

The Lagos club failed to provide adequate and effective security during their home game, thereby allowing unauthorised persons to gain access to restricted areas leading to attacks on the match officials who were proceeding from the dressing room to their vehicle.

Inter Lagos also failed to ensure proper conduct of their officials and supporters, leading to the match officials being held hostage for more than an hour after the match.

Furthermore, Inter Lagos officials in company with some of their supporters intimidated, harassed and verbally abused the match officials, thereby engaging in acts capable of bringing the game to disrepute.

Inter Lagos team manager, alongside some of the club’s supporters, assaulted the match officials, resulting in the first assistant referee sustaining an injury to the face and loss of personal items including damage to his mobile telephone.

The club are fined N2 million for failing to provide adequate and effective security and another N1 million fine for holding the match officials hostage for more than an hour.

Inter Lagos have also been fined N2 million for assault on the match officials and a further N250,000 fine as compensation to the affected assistant referee for the loss of his personal items, damage to his mobile phone & treatment to the injury he sustained following the incident.

Three points and three goals shall be deducted from the accrued points and goals of Inter Lagos for assaulting and causing injury on the first assistant referee.

Inter Lagos have 48 hours from the date of notice to appeal the sanctions

Meanwhile, Sporting Lagos Coach Jeffrey Buter has been summoned by the NPFL’s Disciplinary Panel over his criticism of match officials following the club’s goalless draw with Ikorodu City.

The invitation stems primarily from remarks made after Sporting Lagos’ goalless draw with Ikorodu City in a rescheduled Lagos derby at the Mobolaji Johnson Arena, Onikan, on September 30.

In his post-match reaction, Buter questioned the standard of refereeing and suggested that officials, rather than coaches, were damaging the league’s reputation.

“They say I am bringing the league into disrepute. The referees are bringing the league into disrepute, and not me. If they are not going to fix it, the league is not going anywhere,” Buter was quoted to have said I that interview with the media.

Buter is expected to appear before the panel this week after expressing strong concerns about the standard of refereeing. The date for the hearing has not yet been fixed.

World.title: Africa Aquatics Federation Commends Dolphin Swimming League’s Impact as Season 8 Begins
World.content:
The Season 8 of the Dolphin Swimming League began on a colourful note at Grange School, Ikeja, Lagos, attracting hundreds of young swimmers, alongside a large number of parents and guardians who turned out to support the athletes at the weekend.

Recognised as Nigeria’s foremost inter-school swimming competition, the annual league is organised by Dynaspro Sports Promotion in collaboration with Advanta Interactive Limited and sanctioned by the Nigeria Aquatics Federation, the Nigeria Olympic Committee (NOC), the Nigeria School Sport Federation (NSSF), and the Lagos State Swimming Association.

What started in 2018 with just five schools has grown significantly into a thriving grassroots competition featuring 23 schools and swimming clubs. This season also welcomed participants from Abuja, highlighting the league’s expanding national reach. The competition has earned commendation from the Africa Aquatics Federation for its contribution to the rapid development of junior swimming in Nigeria.

Speaking at the opening event, Vice President of Africa Aquatics Federation, Babatunde Fatai-Williams, praised the league’s impact on youth swimming development.

According to him, the competition has provided young swimmers with consistent opportunities to train, compete, evaluate their performances and improve over time.

“I have been a strong supporter of the Dolphin Swimming League since its inception in 2018. It has made an enormous impact on junior swimming in Lagos State and Nigeria as a whole,” he said.

Fatai-Williams noted that the dominance of Lagos swimmers at national junior championships and the National Youth Games reflects the positive effects of sustained grassroots competitions. He emphasised that regular competitions are essential for athlete development, allowing swimmers to sharpen their skills through continuous participation.

The Coordinator of the Dolphin Swimming League, Oluseyi Oyebode, called for greater support from stakeholders to strengthen grassroots swimming programmes across the country.

He explained that while the league has enjoyed support from the Nigerian Olympic Committee, the Lagos State Government and the Nigeria Aquatics Federation, more collaboration is needed to sustain and expand its impact.

“Working at the grassroots level has always been challenging. Sustainability and proper structures are critical for long-term success,” Oyebode said.

World.title: STRENGTHENING FCT’S SOCIAL SERVICES AND HUMAN DEVELOPMENT
World.content:
Abuja’s development must be understood through the quality of life available to its residents. The attention now being given to healthcare, education and other essential services deserves recognition because these are the areas in which people experience government most personally. A family’s confidence in a public hospital or school says much about how effectively development is reaching ordinary citizens.

In continuing the conversation, the FCT Minister Nyesom Wike’s growing emphasis on social services is particularly significant. It connects the visible transformation of the territory with the welfare of the people who live in it. Investment acquires lasting value when the facilities provided are supported by services that residents can use with confidence.

The renewed commitment to completing Utako General Hospital deserves commendation within this wider understanding of development. Its eventual completion, equipping and staffing would expand the availability of public healthcare. Bringing an abandoned facility into use also restores the social purpose for which public resources were committed in the first place. The benefit will ultimately be measured in the care available to the communities it serves.

Affordability matters just as much as availability. An unexpected illness can place considerable pressure on a household’s finances, particularly where income is already stretched. Sustaining health insurance arrangements alongside improvements in public hospitals recognises this reality. Accessible care helps families protect their wellbeing while preserving the resources they need for education and other necessities.

Healthcare brings this relationship into clear focus. Renovating public hospitals, improving diagnostic facilities and upgrading theatres can strengthen the conditions under which medical professionals care for patients. For someone seeking treatment, the concern is whether the required service is available and accessible. Functioning equipment and properly supported health workers are therefore central to the purpose of any hospital investment.

The attention being given to public education in the FCT should also be appreciated as an investment in future opportunity. Its importance extends well beyond the school premises into the prospects of young people and the families supporting them.

The social value of development must also reach rural and satellite communities. Residents outside the city centre need access to essential services and opportunities within reasonable reach. Electricity provision can support local enterprise and improve household conditions. When it complements better access and public services, it helps more communities participate in the territory’s development.

These interventions reinforce one another. A child who enjoys good health is better placed to benefit from education. A household with access to safe water faces fewer threats to its wellbeing. A secure community gives residents greater confidence to work and invest. This relationship explains why attention to social services strengthens the value of the wider development programme.

The FCT Minister deserves commendation for giving greater attention to this human dimension of governance. The commitment to improving public hospitals and strengthening other essential services recognises that residents need dependable institutions throughout their lives. Sustaining this direction will require the same attention to service delivery that has driven the provision of physical facilities.

For me, development beyond infrastructure means that progress becomes increasingly evident in people’s daily experiences. As these interventions take effect, the promise is better care for patients, stronger opportunities for children and more dependable support for communities. That is the lasting social value Abuja’s continuing transformation should deliver.

Dr. Jumai Ahmadu, Director, Reform Coordination and Service Improvement Department, FCTA

World.title: Winnie Ntshaba reveals her first PAYCHECK! [video]
World.content:
South African actress Winnie Ntshaba opened up about her acting journey during an interview on Radio 2000’s Better Together with Sis Ntombi.

In a TikTok clip from the interview, Winnie spoke about her skincare routine, her journey to joining the stellar cast of the iconic Generations, and the amount she earned from her first paycheck.

WINNIE NTSHABA REVEALS FIRST PAYCHECK FIGURE

Reflecting on her career in this cutthroat industry, Winnie said her experience has been mostly positive, although she acknowledged that, just like any profession, it also has its downsides.



The Generations: The Legacy actress initially dreamed of becoming a doctor but changed her mind during matric and instead studied Drama at university.

Speaking about her first paycheck as an actress, Winnie revealed that she earned R2,900. She believes it was a lot of money back in 1998, as she managed to cover multiple responsibilities.

“It was a lot. I was sending some home. I was living in [the] North West. I bought furniture. It was a lot,” she said.



LANDING THE ‘GENERATIONS’ GIG

Lady luck was on Winnie’s side when she finally joined the soapie in 2005, portraying the timid Khethiwe Buthelezi after auditioning multiple times. Her character was reprised in September 2026, 21 years after she left.

Speaking about manifesting a spot on Generations before its rebrand to Generations: The Legacy, Winnie said she firmly believed in her vision, and that resilience eventually paid off.



“The passion and calling kept on speaking inside me that one day I’ll get in there. Believe you me, when I was now [sic] in Joburg, I remember my agent calling me and saying there is a role that they want you for Generations but you’re only going to get two calls. I said to her, ‘No I’m not going to take that,’ as starving as I was. I was like, ‘I’m not going to take that because I had a vision,” she said.

AGEING LIKE FINE WINE

Sis Ntombi and TikTok users marvelled at Winnie’s flawless skin, which she humbly attributed to her mother’s genes, adding that her sister’s skin is just as beautiful.

World.title: Roosevelt High School principal condemns disastrous Matric Dance
World.content:
The principal of Roosevelt High School ha publicly condemned the behaviour of learners at the recent Matric Dance. Image via Canva

The principal of Roosevelt High School in Johannesburg has published a stern open letter condemning the disastrous events that took place at the school’s recent Matric Dance.

The event – held at the upmarket Avianto Hotel – was cut short after pupils arrived under the influence of alcohol and drugs, threatened staff with firearms and left the venue in an “unacceptable condition”.

ROOSEVELT HIGH SCHOOL PRINCIPAL CONDEMNS DRUNK, DRUGGED GRADE 12 LEARNERS

In a lengthy open letter posted on the school’s official Facebook page, Roosevelt High School principal Cristèl Venter expressed her shock and disappointment at the behaviour of some learners who attended the Matric Dance at the Avianto Hotel in Muldersdrift.



Venter had initially skipped the event due to illness, but had been called in to intervene after things took a turn for the worse.

Venter revealed that learners had arrived under the influence of alcohol and drugs, and had threatened staff with firearms during their rowdy procession and reckless driving into the venue. Intoxicated learners became violently ill, vomiting all over the five-star venue.

The principal decided to cut short the Matric Dance in a bid to de-escalate the deteriorating situation, but was met with contempt and verbal abuse from parents, who angrily confronted school staff.

She shared: “In my 19 years at Roosevelt High School, I cannot recall another evening in which I apologised as many times as I did that night…to venue personnel, to staff, and to some learners who had done absolutely nothing wrong”.

The principal vowed to launch an investigation and disciplinary proceedings into the event, vowing to take action against individuals “lawfully, fairly and in accordance with due process”

“Where misconduct is established, there will be accountability.



Venter urged parents to enforce “manners, boundaries, respect for other people and understanding that actions have consequences”

She added, “The behaviour witnessed and reported last night will not become normal at Roosevelt High School. We can and must do better”.

CALLS FOR STRICT REGULATION OVER MATRIC DANCES

On the Facebook page, Roosevelt High School reposted a video by podcaster Penuel Mlostshwa, who weighed in on the school’s disastrous Matric Dance.

Mlotshwa urged South African schools and parents to regulate Matric Dance events, curbing unnecessary expenditure and financial pressure on parents.

He shared: “There is a lot of pressure on kids and their parents to buy very expensive clothing, and sadly, this now becomes a show off”

Penuel proposed that grade 12 learners enjoy a farewell event on school premises, during school hours, and wearing school uniforms.

“No fancy cars or parades”, he added.

World.title: New chapter: Durban’s Nenezane Hair Studios moves to Joburg!
World.content:
Snenhlanhla Mthembu, the owner of Nenezane Hair Studios, announced via Instagram on 1 October 2026 that her popular establishment is officially making the move to Johannesburg.

The Durban-based salon has attracted “amazing women” over the years, including celebrities such as Mawhoo, Sithelo Shozi, and Ntando Duma, who have trusted the brand for premium wig installations.

NENEZANE HAIR STUDIOS IS MOVING TO JOBURG

The salon will officially unplug its hairdryers and tongs on 25 November 2026, marking a brand-new chapter in Johannesburg from 1 December 2026.



The move to the City of Gold ushers in growth for the business, which has enjoyed a successful five-year run in Durban.

Snenhlanhla expressed her heartfelt gratitude to all her clients for their unwavering support and trust throughout the years.

“For the past 5 years since I started this journey of wig installations, you have been my rock. You supported me when I had nothing; you never left my side; you referred your sisters, your friends, your mothers to me,” she wrote.

“You trusted me with your crowns, you celebrated my wins with me, and you lifted me on my hard days. Because of you, Nenezane Hair Studios became what it is today,” she added.

FROM DURBAN TO JOBURG

For Snenhlanhla, Durban isn’t merely a place of business; it is also home. Therefore, it is not easy to simply pack up and leave, considering the invaluable connections she has forged there.

However, the move also presents an uncertain yet exciting future, one she hopes God will guide her through.



“Leaving Durban is not easy. I have built so much more than a business here. I have built a family,” she wrote.

She added, “I have met the most amazing women and will forever cherish every appointment, every laugh, every conversation we had in my chair.”

“Thank you from the bottom of my heart for your love, your loyalty, and your support. I will never take it for granted,” she continued.

“As I move to Johannesburg, I am moving to start a brand-new chapter. 1 am scared, but I am hopeful that I will go and make the most of this opportunity. I am praying that God goes before me and opens doors for me in Joburg just like He did for me here in Durban,” she added.

GOOD NEWS FOR DURBAN CLIENTS

Luckily for her beloved clients in Durban, the relocation is not the end of Snenhlanhla’s services, as they can still order wigs online, and she will take bookings whenever she is in the city.

World.title: IFP vows to tackle illegal immigration at municipal level
World.content:
Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP) mayoral candidate for the eThekwini Municipality Mkhuleko Hlengwa says municipalities do not deal directly with illegal immigration, but South Africa’s current immigration crisis requires the issue to be addressed at municipal level.

Hlengwa was speaking to party members during the IFP’s eThekwini manifesto launch at the Hollywoodbets Greyville Racecourse on Sunday, 4 October.

IFP VOWS TO DEAL WITH ILLEGAL IMMIGRATION

During his address, Hlengwa said the party plans to tackle illegal immigration to ensure that eThekwini works for Durban residents and South Africans.



He said the municipality would work with other government stakeholders to address illegal immigration, while also tackling crime, human trafficking and drugs.

“The deportation of people who are in the country illegally is not something that a municipality deals with, however, the crisis in South Africa forces municipalities to deal with it. By working hand in hand with other government stakeholders, we will make sure that whoever is here [in South Africa] is here legally. If they’re not legal, they should go.”

Hlengwa said the party’s approach would be aimed at protecting the local economy and young people from what he described as the impact of drugs and human trafficking.



“We will do this to preserve the eThekwini economy, protect the youth from drugs which are brought by foreign nationals, protect women and children from rape and human trafficking by foreign nationals. We will do this because South Africans should be put first and eThekwini residents should be put first,” Hlengwa said.

IMMIGRATION REMAINS CONTENTIOUS ISSUE

The IFP’s comments come as immigration remains a contentious issue in South Africa, with concerns about undocumented migrants and pressure on public services continuing to feature prominently in political and public debate.

Anti-illegal immigration groups, including March and March, have intensified their campaigns calling for undocumented migrants to be deported.



The Department of Home Affairs has also previously said that people should not be denied access to its services solely because they are in the country illegally, while immigration enforcement and deportation remain matters handled by national government.

Hlengwa said the IFP would work with relevant government departments to ensure that immigration laws are enforced while prioritising the interests of eThekwini residents.

World.title: Sipho Mbule reveals why he turned down Kaizer Chiefs
World.content:
Former Orlando Pirates midfielder Sipho Mbule has revealed that he turned down an opportunity to join Kaizer Chiefs after leaving Mamelodi Sundowns.

Mbule was out of contract with Sundowns last year and eventually made the move to their rivals Orlando Pirates.

The midfielder spent just one season with the Buccaneers, making 23 appearances across all competitions before leaving the club and joining Iraqi side Zakho SC.



Speaking on the Giants documentary, Mbule explained why he chose Pirates despite interest from several clubs, including Chiefs.

“Firstly, my contract with Sundowns ended. There were other teams that also wanted to sign me. Even Chiefs approached me,” Mbule said.

“The people and coaches that I spoke to, like coach Rulani, told me that the best team to join is Pirates because I think there was an opportunity for him to make a comeback [to the team].”

Mbule quickly became a fan favourite at Pirates, but his time at the club was ultimately cut short and his contract was not renewed.

His struggles at club level also affected his international career, with the midfielder losing his place in the Bafana Bafana setup and subsequently missing out on the FIFA World Cup.

Mbule was loved by Pirates fans

The “Master Chef” has since revived his career in Iraq, where he appears to have rediscovered his best form.



His resurgence at Zakho SC will come as a welcome boost for a player who was once regarded as one of the most talented midfielders in South African football.

World.title: Former PSL star pleads guilty to culpable homicide, sentencing set
World.content:
The charges against the PSL star relate to a collision on 30 October 2024. It claimed the life of nine-year-old Gomolemo Mavimbela and left two other people seriously injured.

Appearing in the Tembisa Magistrate’s Court, Mogaila admitted in his plea statement that he had negligently caused the collision. According to the National Prosecuting Authority (NPA), his vehicle veered into oncoming traffic on Andrew Mapheto Road before colliding with another vehicle.

PSL STAR SHAUNE MOGAILA ADMITS TO CAUSING FATAL CRASH

The devastating collision resulted in the death of Gomolemo Mavimbela, while her mother and 13-year-old brother were seriously injured.



NPA Communications Officer Magaboke Mohlatlole confirmed that the guilty plea resulted in a conviction on the charges of culpable homicide and failure to render assistance.

“The conviction follows a fatal collision on Andrew Mapheto Road in Tembisa on 30 October, 2024 when Mogaila’s vehicle veered into oncoming traffic and collided with another vehicle,” Mohlatlole said.

“The crash claimed the life of nine year old, Gomolemo Mavimbela, and left her mother and 13 year old brother seriously injured.



“The NPA welcomes tge conviction as an important step towards securing justice for the victims. Mogaila’s bail has been extended until his next court appearance on 17 November 2026, when he’s expected to be sentenced.”

The AfriForum Private Prosecution Unit had previously opposed proposals that could have resulted in a more lenient outcome for Mogaila. Its spokesperson, Barry Bateman, also expressed disappointment that the former PSL player did not provide a fuller account of his actions leading up to the crash.

SENTENCING SET FOR NOVEMBER

Although the PSL star has now been convicted, the case is not yet over, with sentencing scheduled for 17 November 2026. The former Sekhukhune United player remains out on R20,000 bail, which has been extended until his next appearance.



The NPA said Mogaila is expected to return to the Tembisa Magistrate’s Court on the sentencing date.

The case has brought renewed attention to the consequences of the fatal Thembisa crash, with the family of Gomolemo Mavimbela having lost a nine-year-old child while two other family members suffered serious injuries.

World.title: Why Zimbabwe is suddenly back on Trump’s radar
World.content:
President Trump to send delegation to Zimbabwe. Image via X@FonsiLoaiza

Zimbabwe is suddenly attracting renewed attention from Washington, with United States President Donald Trump expected to send a delegation to Harare for talks with President Emmerson Mnangagwa.

The potential visit follows a meeting between Mnangagwa and Republican Congressman Marlin Stutzman on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York last month.

According to Zimbabwean officials, Stutzman subsequently briefed Trump on his discussions with Mnangagwa, leading to the proposal for a congressional and business delegation to Zimbabwe.



But why is Zimbabwe back on the US radar?

Zimbabwe’s critical minerals

One major factor is Zimbabwe’s mineral wealth.

The country is seeking to position itself as an important player in the global energy transition, particularly through the extraction and local processing of minerals required for modern industries.

Zimbabwe has significant deposits of lithium, platinum-group metals, nickel and chrome, among other minerals.

Zimbabwe has increasingly pushed for investment in local processing rather than simply exporting raw minerals, creating opportunities for foreign companies seeking access to strategic mineral supplies.

This could make Zimbabwe an increasingly important economic partner as countries compete for secure critical-mineral supply chains.



Zimbabwe’s new US trade opening

Trade is another reason for the renewed engagement.

The United States has included Zimbabwe in its fiscal 2027 tariff-rate quota for raw cane sugar, giving the country an allocation of 813 metric tonnes.

The quota allows qualifying sugar imports to enter the US at a lower tariff rate than quantities outside the quota.

The move places Zimbabwe alongside other African countries, including South Africa, Mozambique and Malawi, which also have allocations under the US sugar programme.

While the allocation is relatively small, it provides Zimbabwean producers with an opportunity to access the American market.

Zimbabwe’s long-running sanctions issue

The potential thaw also comes against the background of Zimbabwe’s more than two decades of difficult relations with Washington.

The Zimbabwe Democracy and Economic Recovery Act (ZDERA), passed in 2001, has long been a major point of contention between the two countries.

A US bill proposing the repeal of ZDERA has also been introduced, although any change to the legislation would require the US legislative process to run its course.

For Zimbabwe, improved relations with Washington could therefore have implications far beyond diplomacy.

What happens next?

Zimbabwe and US officials have indicated that high-level visits, trade and investment are among the issues being discussed.

If the proposed delegation travels to Harare, attention will turn to whether the engagement produces concrete deals on minerals, agriculture, investment and trade.

For now, the developments suggest that Washington and Harare are exploring a more commercially focused relationship after years of strained ties.

World.title: When to record? Expert weighs in on how cellphone videos can become crucial evidence
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Cellphones are more than just devices used for communication and social media.

At the right moment, that phone can become a powerful tool for recording acts of crime or even misconduct.

This footage can ultimately play a crucial role in criminal or even disciplinary cases.

An example of this is the case against Lawrence Mudzinganyama.

Mudzinganyama was captured on camera allegedly threatening to shoot and kill a group of women at an upmarket Sandton restaurant.

He now faces ten charges, including fraud, intimidation and crimen injuria.

READ | Businessman accused of threatening women at Sandton restaurant granted bail

But his case is one of many.

There is also the case of eight Milnerton High School pupils who were charged with assault after a disturbing video has surfaced showing a 16-year-old Cape Town pupil being brutally assaulted.

READ| UPDATE: Eight Milnerton High pupils appear in court

For social media law expert Emma Sadlier, the ability to capture such scenes proves one's courage to document serious misconduct when it happens because, without that evidence, it may be hard to act against the perpetrator.

“We just see electronic evidence permeate the courtroom, and I think that the more that evidence exists, the more bad people end up facing the full might of the law; as a result of that evidence being taken, I say all the better,” she said.

In addressing the issue of privacy, Sadlier explained that once evidence is manifestly in the public interest, then one should not worry about the privacy rights of an individual.

She does, however, caution that there are two instances when a person's privacy is infringed.

“The first is consent, and the second is if it benefits the public. What I say is a rule of thumb, in short, when you do something illegal, when you do something against the law, against the rules, your privacy falls out the window.”

The issue becomes more sensitive when it comes to children if they are involved.

Sadlier said that in those events, it is important to be mindful of the privacy rights of children.

World.title: Number Of The Day | 100 million | 05 October 2026
World.content:
100 Million Barrels Sounds Huge. In A Global Oil Crisis, It May Not Be

One hundred million barrels of oil sounds like the kind of number that should move markets.

That is precisely what the G7 hopes will happen. Its members have agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of emergency crude oil and refined fuel reserves, with an early emphasis on diesel, as governments try to contain soaring energy costs and restore confidence to a market shaken by war, disrupted supply routes and shortages of refined products.

But the size of a government intervention tells only part of the story. What matters is the scale of the disruption it is trying to offset.

In a recent Number of the Day discussion, Gareth Edwards and Francis Herd put that imbalance into perspective. Citing International Energy Agency figures discussed during the episode, they noted that about 4.3 million barrels a day had been taken off the market. Using a conservative four-million-barrel daily figure over

seven months, the episode arrives at roughly 840 million barrels removed from supply; dramatically larger than the new 100-million-barrel intervention.

That does not make the G7 release insignificant. It helps explain why its effect may be limited.

The Problem Is Bigger Than Crude Oil

Oil markets are not simply a question of how many barrels exist underground or in strategic reserves. Consumers do not put crude oil into their cars. Crude must be transported, refined into products such as petrol and diesel, shipped to the markets that need it and delivered through functioning supply chains.

That distinction has become increasingly important during the current crisis. The G7 plan includes refined products, particularly diesel, precisely because shortages have developed further down the supply chain. European economies, for example, rely partly on imported diesel to supplement domestic refinery output, while disruption elsewhere has intensified competition for available cargoes.

The podcast captures the problem neatly through another number: global oil inventories stood at about 7.8 billion barrels in August, according to the IEA figure cited in the conversation. Yet much of that supply may be in pipelines, storage or locations from which it cannot quickly reach the places experiencing shortages.

In other words, availability is not the same as accessibility.

A market can simultaneously contain billions of barrels of oil and still experience acute shortages of the right product, in the right place, at the right time.

South Africa Cannot Escape The Global Price

For South Africans, this distinction is no academic exercise.

The Department of Mineral and Petroleum Resources confirmed that new fuel prices will take effect on 7 October. During the review period, the average Brent crude price rose from $87.89 to $101 a barrel. Government attributed the increase to geopolitical tensions, uncertainty around oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz, higher shipping costs and falling inventories.

South Africa is particularly exposed because it imports crude oil and finished petroleum products whose prices are determined internationally. The monthly domestic fuel-price calculation therefore absorbs both the international product price and movements in the rand.

That combination is now painful. Reuters reported that petrol prices are set to rise by as much as 12%, while wholesale diesel increases by about 10%.

The G7's 100-million-barrel intervention may eventually help ease some pressure. But emergency reserves cannot immediately repair damaged supply chains, remove geopolitical risk, restore refining capacity or strengthen the rand.

That is why the real significance of the number is not simply that 100 million barrels are being released.

It is that even 100 million barrels can look small when the problem is bigger than the stockpile.

References

· Number of the Day, Gareth Edwards and Francis Herd, 05 October 2026.

· South African Government, fuel-price adjustment effective 7 October 2026.

· Associated Press, G7 emergency oil and diesel release, 2 October 2026.

· The Guardian, G7 coordinated emergency reserve release, 2 October 2026.

· Reuters, South African October fuel-price increase, 5 October 2026.

World.title: SA Explained | Shadrack Sibiya: Is The Madlanga Fallout Finally Catching Up With Him? | 05 October 2026
World.content:
When A Police Crisis Becomes A Systems Test

The pressure around Shadrack Sibiya is about more than one senior officer. It tests whether South Africa can turn explosive allegations and commission findings into durable institutional reform.

The Madlanga Commission has exposed a problem that is easy to describe but far harder to fix: what happens when allegations of criminal influence reach deep enough into policing that removing individual officials may not be enough to restore trust?

Suspended Deputy National Police Commissioner Shadrack Sibiya now sits at the centre of that question. The Commission has recommended disciplinary proceedings and further investigation against him, while he faces separate criminal charges that he denies. On 5 October, SAPS confirmed that his disciplinary hearing had begun but was postponed, while Sibiya also approached the Labour Court in an attempt to halt the process.

The temptation is to treat each development as a story about one man. That would miss the bigger institutional warning.

In SA Explained, Pule Letshwiti-Jones asks whether attempts to clean up the South African Police Service risk merely “replacing one faction with another”. Silindelo Sebata responds by pointing towards the less dramatic work of institutional reform: vetting, procurement and systems that can keep functioning when powerful individuals change.

That distinction matters because commissions are exceptionally good at making hidden relationships visible. They can compel testimony, connect people and events, identify failures and recommend action. But a commission cannot permanently supervise an institution after the hearings end. Its lasting value depends on whether the organisations it examines can convert exposure into rules, controls and consequences.

For SAPS, that means the test is larger than whether any particular allegation against Sibiya is eventually proved. Criminal proceedings must follow their own evidentiary standard, disciplinary processes their own rules, and accused people retain the right to challenge the case against them. Institutional reform operates on another track. It asks why vulnerabilities existed, whether safeguards worked, who was able to bypass them and whether the same weaknesses could survive under different names and different office-bearers.

That is where public trust becomes difficult to rebuild. Trust is not restored simply because a prominent official leaves office. It returns when the public can see that misconduct is harder to conceal, complaints cannot quietly disappear, procurement decisions leave a trace, conflicts of interest are identified, and disciplinary systems do not depend on political or factional convenience.

This is also why the idea of factionalism is so corrosive. If accountability is interpreted only as one camp defeating another, every investigation becomes vulnerable to the claim that it is political retaliation. The antidote is not rhetoric. It is process strong enough to survive changes in leadership and credible enough to be applied consistently.

South Africa therefore faces a harder question than whether the Madlanga Commission can expose wrongdoing. The real question is whether the institutions receiving its findings can make the next scandal more difficult to produce.

A commission can reveal where the system failed. Reform begins only when the system is redesigned so that the same failures are less likely to happen again.

References

SA Explained episode transcript, 5 October 2026.

The Presidency, “President Cyril Ramaphosa notes recommendations and referrals of the Second Interim Report of the Madlanga Commission”.

World.title: 'Killing my son caused the death of my wife’ - Tibz' Motsoane's father
World.content:
DURBAN - Almost three years after the fatal shooting of rapper Kiernan 'AKA' Forbes and his close friend Tebello 'Tibz' Motsoane, the seven men accused of the murder are set to stand trial.

The trial, expected to begin on Tuesday, marks a significant moment for the families of the two men.

Among those who will be watching the case closely is Motsoane’s father, Sylvester Motsoane, who said having his son’s killer identified would help him begin to find closure.

READ | Seven accused in AKA murder case plead not guilty

Sylvester said the death of his son still cuts deep because right after that tragic incident he suffered another devastating blow: the death of his wife just eight months later after suffering a heart attack.

“Killing my son cost the death of my wife… I was shattered. I was a wreck. I don't know how I managed to be like this today,” he said.

The announcement of the trial date came on Monday when the seven men appeared before court.

READ |AKA and Tibz murder trial: The long road to justice

For Sylvester, the day felt heavier because this was the day his wife died.

With the matter now set for trial, he hopes that justice will take its course.
