World.title: Mayor from Colombia’s north claims De la Espriella’s armed men intimidated him
World.content:
The mayor of Sincelejo claimed Sunday that armed men intimidated him during a meeting with Colombia’s President Abelardo de la Espriella.

In a video message, Sincelejo Mayor Yahir Acuña said that armed men positioned themselves behind him while the president accused the mayor of corruption and threatened to pull municipal funds.

The accusations were partly published on the social media pages of the president, who accused Acuña of being “a person who, like you, faces 13 corruption charges, has a video in which he explains how to embezzle funds from the PAE, and, on top of that, is set to stand trial in the Supreme Court of Justice on charges of illicit enrichment.”

So let’s see what we do with Sincelejo, but I do not work under your scheme of corruption. And if you think you can continue engaging in those practices, know that someone has arrived who is going to prevent it and that I am going to concentrate on it. This money, mister mayor, I will take care of it, and to take care of it I have to keep it away from your control. President Abelardo de la Espriella

In his response, Acuña claimed that De la Espriella’s video “has been edited and digitally manipulated.”

I ask you, please, to show the full video, where you can see how disciplinary and criminal codes are being violated in Colombia, where you can see how a mayor is being intimidated with rifles in the hands of civilians. How can a mayor be constantly flanked—for the entire duration of an event—by a person armed with a rifle, with the sole purpose of intimidating him? Sincelejo Mayor Yahir Acuña

Investigative journalist Laura Ardila said on social media platform X that sources from the province confirmed Acuña’s allegations.

Sources from the department who were present say—fearing they might be named—that they left the scene terrified. They claim that Acuña was indeed surrounded by heavily armed men in civilian clothing, that the president’s office was recording the entire time, and that, based on details like these, they believe it was a scene staged in advance to go viral. Journalist Laura Ardila

The mayor subsequently pointed out that the investigations into his alleged corruption existed before the presidential campaign, during which the De la Espriella campaign may have violated electoral laws, according to Acuña.

Among other things, the mayor said that he had been approached by De la Espriella’s parents to support the far-right president’s campaign and that local print shops may have received unreported campaign funds.

Since this needs to be clarified, mister President, it would be a good idea for the oversight agencies to investigate whether any printing shops in Sincelejo incurred campaign expenses that have not yet been reported to the National Electoral Council, whether there was campaign financing, and where that campaign financing came from, Mister President. Sincelejo Mayor Yahir Acuña

The mayor also pointed out that two members of the De la Espriella administration are being investigated on corruption charges and that the president had ties to the now-defunct paramilitary organization AUC.

The president has repeatedly used corruption allegations to target political enemies.

World.title: Colombia’s top corporate lobbyist resigns over reported tensions with president
World.content:
The director of one of Colombia’s most powerful business associations, Bruce Mac Master of the ANDI, resigned amid tensions with President Abelardo de la Espriella.

In a letter to the ANDI, Mac Master said that “it is time for me to step down from my role as head of the National Association of Entrepreneurs of Colombia.”

According to the former ANDI boss, “unexpected and troubling circumstances” made working for the association “particularly complex” and ‘multiple pressures have affected its ability to act freely and carry out its functions autonomously.”

In recent weeks, unexpected and troubling circumstances have arisen that have made the Association’s operating environment particularly complex, with potential adverse effects on its members and staff. Multiple pressures have affected its ability to act freely and carry out its functions autonomously. In the face of these challenges, I have sought to act with firmness and prudence, always prioritizing institutional channels and placing the interests of the ANDI above any personal considerations, in an effort to resolve this situation. Bruce Mac Master

Mac Master’s resignation followed news suggesting that De la Espriella instructed his cabinet of boycotting the ANDI chief.

According to political news magazine La Silla Vacia, the rift between the ANDI and the government was because De la Espriella’s law firm was never allowed to join the ANDI and the association’s donations in response to the august 10 earthquake bypassed the First Lady’s newly founded and very controversial foundation.

“The General Board of Directors, its Executive Committee, and I did everything in our power to facilitate a solution and create conditions that would allow the Association to fully fulfill its role, seeking to keep channels of dialogue open and to continue contributing,” but “all of those attempts were unsuccessful.”

I deeply regret this, because I have always believed in collective intelligence and in the need for the government, the private sector, and institutions to work together—even in the face of differences—with respect, independence, and a sense of national responsibility. We tried, but we were unsuccessful. Bruce Mac Master

Mac Master said that he hoped that his resignation would restore “collaboration between the national government and the business community—as represented by the General Board of Directors, the members, and the various divisions of the Association.”

The former ANDI chief had been trying to represent the business interests of its approximately 1,600 members since 2013.

World.title: Colombia seeks to tighten checks on public protests
World.content:
Colombia’s government published a draft decree that seeks to tighten regulations on public protests.

The draft was published weeks before labor unions and social organizations plan regional anti-government protests ahead of a national strike that is set for November.

The draft seeks to update the Decree #3 of 2021, which was issued months before a national strike that was violently repressed by the police and the military.

In an attempt to prevent another bloodbath, the decree seeks to regulate authorities’ response to protests and the coordinated use of force in response to acts of vandalism and violence.

The decree regulates dialogue between the protesters and law enforcement authorities to promote the peaceful nature of protests.

The decree additionally limits the use of police intelligence against those organizing and participating in the protests.

Last but not least, the decree seeks the effective prosecution of those arrested during protests through increased surveillance and a permanent police presence.

The decree comes amid social tensions that surged after the far-right President Abelardo de la Espriella took office in August and announced counterrevolutionary measures that seek to undo reforms by his leftist predecessor, former President Gustavo Petro.

Swelling student protests have been publicly accused of being fueled by insurgencies and De la Espriella has warned that police may enter universities if they find evidence they are used to prepare acts of vandalism or terrorism.

World.title: Colombia breaks diplomatic ties with Iran
World.content:
Colombia’s Foreign Ministry said Thursday that it had broken diplomatic ties with Iran and designated the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) as a terrorist organization.

The foreign ministry made the announcements in two separate statements that were published in its website.

In the first statement, the government claimed that the decision claimed to defend “national and hemispheric security, and the fight against transnational crime.”

According to the foreign ministry, the Iranian government has “alleged ties to international terrorist groups and other narco-terrorist groups that threaten [Colombia’s] security.”

Colombia also took into account the documented human rights violations committed by the Iranian government on its territory, the verified attacks against countries not involved in the Middle East conflict, the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, and the authorities’ obstruction of the International Atomic Energy Agency’s (IAEA) efforts to verify the scope of Iran’s nuclear program. Foreign Ministry

In regards to the IRGC, the foreign ministry claimed that the Iranian armed force “poses a serious threat to international peace and security” through “covert operations beyond Iran’s borders.”

“Colombia will strengthen its control and security measures to prevent individuals associated with the IRGC from entering its territory,” said the foreign ministry in a second statement.

In his 2017 book “Watch Your Backyard,” Foreign Minister Omar Bula claimed that “Iran and Islamic extremist groups such a Hezbollah and Al Qaeda have profusely penetrated Latin America.”

As part of his foreign policy, President Abelardo de la Espriella has renewed ties with the United States, Israel and the United Arab Emirates.

In a response, the Iranian government said that the accusations of the De la Espriella government go “against the principles of mutual respect” and damage both countries’ “interests and benefits.”

“It is clear that none of the arguments put forward by the Colombian government to justify this decision are valid or logical, and that this measure was adopted solely under the influence of the Zionist regime and the United States,” said Iran’s foreign ministry.

World.title: ACSN extends lockdown of Colombia’s Caribbean coast to Friday morning
World.content:
Santa Marta-based organized crime group ACSN said Wednesday that the lockdown it has imposed on parts of Colombia’s Caribbean coast will be lifted on Friday morning.

In its first formal statement, the ACSN said that “the armed strike announced for 72 hours will end at 7:00AM on Friday 25 September 2026.”

The lockdown, which was initially called for 48 hours on Monday, has devastated the legal economy in the port city, particularly after ACSN assassins uploaded videos of them opening fire at stores that ignored the order to social media.

The online videos and half a dozen burnt buses and taxis all but cleared the streets of Santa Marta, which became a ghost town on Tuesday.

“We have never seen anything like this,” one Santa Marta resident told news program El Reporte Coronell.

President Abelardo de la Espriella announced the militarization of Santa Marta, but this was barely visible in the city’s downtown area and in the majority of Santa Marta’s neighborhoods.

“There are no police or soldiers in the streets, the people feel unprotected and are in panic,” said journalist Javier Manjarres on social media platform X.

“The current situation is a consequence of the behavior of the security forces and the decisions taken by the National Government in regards to our organization,” the organized crime group said in their statement.

The ACSN admitted that the clandestine lockdown was the result of the killing of Jose Luis Perez, a.k.a. “Cholo,” one of its commanders in the region around the Sierra Nevada mountain range just outside the city.

According to the group, security forces executed Cholo in front of his wife after his arrest.

An 18-year-old farmhand with no ties to the organization was also executed by the security, his family told media.

The lockdown has been imposed throughout the Magdalena and La Guajira provinces, a region where the group dominates organized crime and controls drug trafficking route to the Caribbean.

World.title: Colombia withdraws support for ICJ genocide case against Israel
World.content:
Colombia has withdrawn its participation in South Africa’s genocide case against Israel, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) said Tuesday.

In a statement, the court in The Hague said that Colombia’s government “decided to withdraw the Declaration of intervention that it had filed… on 5 April 2024 in the case concerning Application of the Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide in the Gaza Strip.”

The decision of the administration of President Abelardo De la Espriella is part of a wider attempt to restore ties with Israel and its main sponsor, the United States, and appease its Evangelical Christian support base.

In response to the ongoing genocide in Palestine, former President Gustavo Petro took a leading role in diplomatic efforts that sought to isolate Israel and seek justice for Israel’s victims through the world court.

In a response, the US Government put Petro on a blacklist and actively campaigned for the election of De la Espriella to prevent another leftist victory in elections earlier this year.

The new president, who took office in August, immediately restored diplomatic ties to Israel and lifted a ban on coal exports to the country in West Asia.

World.title: ACSN crime group shuts down parts of Colombia’s Caribbean coast
World.content:
Santa Marta-based crime group ACSN shut down parts of the city and the surrounding region after Colombia’s armed forces killed one of their commanders.

Jose Luis Perez, a.k.a. “Cholo,” and six of his comrades were killed during an offensive on Monday.

The son of Fredy Castillo, a.k.a. “Pinocho,” who is one of the alleged bosses of the crime group, was reportedly among those killed during the operation.

Shortly after, a pamphlet that was signed by the ACSN ordered an “armed strike” of 48 hours because of the “the fierce attacks that the government has been launching against our organization in the Sierra Nevada since this afternoon.”

Multiple buses were incinerated in the region around Santa Marta.

We hereby declare a 48-hour armed strike throughout the province of Magdalena, particularly along the Troncal del Caribe highway, in the city of Santa Marta, and in the banana-growing region. We do not want any businesses to remain open for a period of 48 hours. ACSN

According to President Abelardo de la Espriella, who traveled to the city, “they are trying to intimidate the public by promoting an armed strike.”

“I will not allow any criminal organization to subjugate citizens through threats and terror,” the president added.

Notwithstanding, multiple shop owners in Santa Marta and along the highway kept their shops closed on Tuesday, afraid to challenge the authority of the local crime bosses.

The district government closed public schools in neighborhoods where the ACSN is believed to have a strong presence. Public transport was suspended as videos of armed men opening fire on shops that failed to close voluntarily were posted on social media.

The ACSN control much of drug trafficking to the port of Santa Marta and to the coastline of the neighboring La Guajira province.

De la Espriella ended attempts to negotiate the group’s surrender and ordered a military approach after taking office in August.

World.title: Colombia’s war crimes tribunal warns ICC that De la Espriella supports “worst attack in history”
World.content:
Colombia’s war crimes tribunal JEP said that it would warn the United Nations and the International Criminal Court about plans of President Abelardo de la Espriella to cut its budget.

In a statement, JEP president Alejandro Ramelli raised the alarm warned about a pending proposal by far-right Senator Enrique Gomez (National Salvation) to reduce the tribunal’s budget by COP100 billion ($31.6 million), which received De la Espriella’s support.

A second proposal by another far-right party, the Democratic Center, sought to push all sentences against members of the security forces to military justice for revision.

According to Ramelli, the two bill proposals “prove the existence of a strategy to block the JEP’s functioning” and called on the international community to “put a stop to this effort to dismantle our financial system and calls for the essential resources needed for our operations to be guaranteed.”

These initiatives constitute a combined strategy of economic strangulation and the subjugation of the JEP to military criminal justice. It is the most serious attack we have ever faced against our independence and autonomy. JEP president Alejandro Ramelli

The president , who vowed to get rid of the JEP on campaign, said that the 2027 national budget “does not constitute any threat to any judge, it’s the Constitution at work.”

I do not have a policy of retaliation against the JEP. I have a duty to manage spending, demand results, and allocate the State’s limited resources to a justice system that serves everyone, not to a court that part of the country perceives—for reasons debated in Congress and in public opinion—as a system of privileges rather than an effective end to impunity. President Abelardo de la Espriella

Since March of 2018, the JEP has played a key role in clarifying crimes committed during the armed conflict that erupted in response to the insurgency of the now-defunct guerrilla group FARC.

Among other things, the JEP found that the guerrillas recruited more than 18,000 children and that the security forces assassinated more than 7,800 civilians to inflate their combat kills.

Hundreds of former guerrillas and former members of the armed forces are taking part in a transitional justice system that seeks to solve as many as possible of the hundreds of thousands of crimes committed during the decades-long armed conflict.

World.title: Paraguay's opposition takes Asunción from the Colorado Party and holds Ciudad del Este
World.content:
Paraguay's opposition takes Asunción from the Colorado Party and holds Ciudad del Este

5th Monday, October 2026 - 22:09 UTC Full article

In Ciudad del Este, Daniel Pereira Mujica of the opposition Yo Creo party won with 72.83%, keeping the city in the hands of the party previously led locally by Miguel Prieto

Paraguay's opposition won the mayoralty of Asunción and held that of Ciudad del Este, the country's two most populous cities, in Sunday's municipal elections, according to preliminary results from the electoral authority. The ruling Colorado Party, however, won the vast majority of districts.

With 99.92% of polling stations counted, civil engineer Soledad Núñez of the Alianza Juntos por Asunción won 47.78% of the vote to 45.98% for Colorado candidate Camilo Pérez, president of the Paraguayan Olympic Committee, a margin of 5,024 votes. Núñez was backed by the Patria Querida and Authentic Radical Liberal parties. “Asunción voted, Asunción won. Today the people who don't give up, who resist, who can't be bought, won,” she said on election night.

In Ciudad del Este, Daniel Pereira Mujica of the opposition Yo Creo party won with 72.83%, keeping the city in the hands of the party previously led locally by Miguel Prieto. Prieto has expressed interest in running for president in 2028.

The Colorado Party, to which President Santiago Peña belongs, was winning in 187 of 263 districts and 11 of 17 departmental capitals, and regained the mayoralty of Encarnación. The figures from the preliminary results transmission system must be confirmed by the official count.

After the vote, Núñez said the opposition would file a complaint with prosecutors over the publication of exit polls during election day. A consultancy posted trends for several cities on social media an hour before polls closed, without naming candidates. The Electoral Code prohibits publishing such polls until an hour after closing. “This goes against electoral participation,” said Núñez, who argued the publication may have discouraged voters. Liberal senator Celeste Amarilla called the poll “illegal” and said she would file a complaint if no one else did. The consultancy was not publicly identified and did not comment. Turnout in Asunción was 61.75%, up from 59.65% in 2021.

Municipal elections serve as a political barometer ahead of the 2028 general election.

World.title: São Paulo stocks jump 8% and the real firms after Bolsonaro's first-round win
World.content:
São Paulo stocks jump 8% and the real firms after Bolsonaro's first-round win

5th Monday, October 2026 - 17:30 UTC Full article

Bolsonaro won 47% of valid votes to Lula's 45%, and the two will face each other in the October 25 runoff

Brazilian markets rallied sharply on Monday in response to the first round of the presidential election, in which Senator Flávio Bolsonaro finished ahead of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, contrary to what polls had predicted. The São Paulo Stock Exchange's Bovespa index rose as much as 8% in early trading, above 208,000 points.

Banks led the rally. In New York, before the open, Bradesco's depositary receipts were up 15.2%, Itaú's 14.4%, Nu Holding's 12.2%, Petrobras's 10.3% and Vale's 6.4%. The real gained 1.4% against the dollar, which traded at 5.14 reais.

Bolsonaro won 47% of valid votes to Lula's 45%, and the two will face each other in the October 25 runoff. Investors see the Liberal Party senator as more likely to push through fiscal tightening that would allow high interest rates to come down; Lula avoided committing to spending cuts and expanded social programmes in the final stretch of the campaign. “The market wants change, it wants reforms, it doesn't want a large public deficit,” Pedro Galdi, an analyst at AGF Investments, told Reuters.

Not all assessments were unconditional. Bryan Harris, a partner at political risk consultancy Sabio, warned that the market would look for “clear signals” that Bolsonaro is “serious” about tackling the country's problems, and said the senator had shown little aptitude for economic policymaking.

Precedent suggests caution. Four years ago, the real gained more than 4% and the Bovespa rose 5.5% the day after Jair Bolsonaro outperformed expectations in the first round; weeks later he lost the runoff to Lula.

The Bovespa had already risen 5% in dollar terms in September as the senator's prospects improved, despite reports about his ties to Daniel Vorcaro, former owner of Banco Master, who has been arrested and charged with fraud. Flávio Bolsonaro is under investigation for alleged money laundering in that case, without formal charges, and denies any wrongdoing.

World.title: "The end of the PT era is decreed," says Flávio Bolsonaro after winning the first round
World.content:
“The end of the PT era is decreed,” says Flávio Bolsonaro after winning the first round

5th Monday, October 2026 - 17:18 UTC Full article

The senator pledged to cut the number of ministries and end presidential re-election, a measure that would require a constitutional amendment; he said one term would be enough for him

Senator Flávio Bolsonaro celebrated his first-round victory in Brazil's presidential election in Brasília with a message focused on change. “Change, the word is change. Brazil can't take any more. The end of the PT era is decreed,” he told reporters outside his campaign headquarters.

With almost 99% of votes counted, the Liberal Party candidate took 47.08% of valid votes to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's 45.10%, so the two will face each other in the October 25 runoff. Bolsonaro thanked “almost 56 million” voters and hit back at the pollsters: “The polling institutes had us behind and we grew.” The final Datafolha survey had given Lula 45% and Bolsonaro 42% of valid votes, and AtlasIntel 47% to 44.1%. In 2022, polls also underestimated Jair Bolsonaro's first-round vote.

The senator pledged to cut the number of ministries and end presidential re-election, a measure that would require a constitutional amendment; he said one term would be enough for him. He also said he would appoint at least four justices to the Supreme Federal Court, the same court that sentenced his father to 27 years in prison for attempting a coup. Those appointments depend on vacancies arising and require Senate approval.

Bolsonaro described Lula's government as a series of “records” in violence against women, taxes and business closures, campaign claims the government rejects. Lula, for his part, questioned his rival's record and linked him to the Banco Master case, in which the senator is under investigation without formal charges.

World.title: Lula bets on education and non-voters to overturn the result in the runoff
World.content:
Lula bets on education and non-voters to overturn the result in the runoff

5th Monday, October 2026 - 17:08 UTC Full article

“The result is often unexpected. You never get everything you wanted,” the president said from a hotel in São Paulo

Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has set education, research and industrial policy as the pillars of his campaign for the October 25 runoff, and urged the more than 30 million Brazilians who abstained on Sunday to vote, after finishing behind Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in the first round.

With 99.9% of votes counted, Bolsonaro took 47% of valid votes and Lula 45%. “The result is often unexpected. You never get everything you wanted,” the president said from a hotel in São Paulo. “The second round is the moment to show the true picture of today's Brazil and the Brazil we want.”

Lula pledged to maintain investment in universities, federal institutes and secondary education, and to expand the Pé-de-Meia programme, which gives students a financial incentive to reduce school dropout. “It is through education that we will change this country,” he said, linking that commitment to increasing Brazil's productive and technological capacity.

The 80-year-old president again questioned his rival's record, citing “very serious suspicions” over alleged links to organised crime and to the Banco Master case. Bolsonaro is under investigation in that case, without formal charges, and has denied any wrongdoing.

Abstention will be key. Votes for the candidates eliminated in the first round, around 8% in total, come largely from centre-right and right-wing voters, while those who do not vote are disproportionately from lower-income groups, Lula's electoral base.

World.title: Flávio Bolsonaro edges Lula in the first round; both head to an October 25 runoff
World.content:
Flávio Bolsonaro edges Lula in the first round; both head to an October 25 runoff

5th Monday, October 2026 - 10:30 UTC Full article

“Brazil wants change,” Bolsonaro said in Brasília, thanking some 56 million voters, more than his father won in the first round in 2022

Senator Flávio Bolsonaro won around 47% of valid votes in the first round of Brazil's presidential election on Sunday, ahead of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who took about 45%, according to the Superior Electoral Court's count. As neither passed half of the valid votes, the two will face each other in a runoff on October 25.

The result runs counter to the final polls. Datafolha's survey published on Saturday, based on 4,006 interviews, gave Lula 45% of valid votes and Bolsonaro 42%; Quaest had put the president five points ahead in the first round. The Liberal Party candidate led the count from start to finish.

“Brazil wants change,” Bolsonaro said in Brasília, thanking some 56 million voters, more than his father won in the first round in 2022. “The end of the PT era is hereby decreed,” he added. He did not mention former president Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year sentence under house arrest for attempting a coup and whom his son has promised to grant an amnesty if he wins.

Lula spoke shortly afterwards in São Paulo. “The result is often unexpected. I confess I was convinced I was going to win the election in the first round,” he said. “But we have the second round, and the second round is the real test. Tomorrow we start a new campaign.” The 80-year-old president criticised the Bolsonaro family's “truculent biographies” and referred to links with militias and to the Banco Master case, in which Flávio Bolsonaro is under investigation without formal charges.

The other candidates — Ronaldo Caiado, Renan Santos, Augusto Cury and Romeu Zema — won around 8% of valid votes between them. Their largely centre-right and right-wing electorate will be decisive in the runoff, along with abstention, which reached about 21% in 2022 and traditionally affects lower-income groups, Lula's electoral base, the most.

Brazilians also elected governors, the entire Chamber of Deputies, two thirds of the Senate and the state assemblies. Voting passed without major incidents, aside from power cuts at some polling stations caused by storms, which did not affect the electronic voting machines.

If he wins on October 25, Bolsonaro would add Brazil to a series of right-wing victories in the region, including those of José Antonio Kast in Chile, Abelardo de la Espriella in Colombia and Keiko Fujimori in Peru. The senator has pledged to bring the country into the Americas Shield, the Washington-backed security coalition from which Brazil is absent.

World.title: Falklands weighs curbs on Argentine visitors after flag-waving incidents
World.content:
Falklands weighs curbs on Argentine visitors after flag-waving incidents

5th Monday, October 2026 - 10:20 UTC Full article

MLA Michael Goss said the Assembly is examining what can legally be done, but insisted Argentina’s pressure is “just noise”

Amid a sharp rise in international attention on the South Atlantic and its energy resources, Falkland Islands residents have been angered by Argentine visitors seen waving Argentine flags and banners denying British sovereignty, prompting calls from members of the community to restrict such visits.

Argentine nationals can currently enter the Islands with a valid passport, proof of return travel, confirmed accommodation, health insurance and sufficient funds.

Michael Goss, a Member of the Legislative Assembly (MLA), has addressed the issue. He said he is personally not opposed to restrictions, but that the matter ultimately comes down to what can be done legally. “So we can’t turn around and directly stop people coming in at this moment in time,” he said.

However, Goss confirmed the Assembly has already begun examining options. “At this moment in time, we have been looking, at the early points of this Assembly, [at] ways and means that we could actually look to potentially put a stop to things like this, but ultimately, again, it falls down into what we can do legally. But it also comes down to administration.”

He added: “We have got to make sure that we’re not going to be seeing more and more incidents of people who are, quote unquote, ‘visiting the Falkland Islands’ to further a political agenda — it’s not acceptable.”

Goss also said: “We’re hearing a lot of noise coming from Argentina. We’ve seen sparks of this at the UN when myself and Dom were away, and ultimately we knew then that there was going to be a lot more noise coming out.”

But he insisted: “We’re not shaken by it, we’ve grown. We are strong, and we are going to continue to grow, and we are going to grow stronger from this, not weaker. So my ultimate closing statement on this is: it’s just noise, and we’re not going to let it get to us.”

Such incidents, which residents regard as attempts at intimidation, are not new to Islanders. They have recurred as President Javier Milei’s government has stepped up Argentina’s sovereignty claim, including legal action against companies exploring for oil near the Islands. In a 2013 referendum, 99.8% of Falklands voters chose to remain a British Overseas Territory.

Official guidance for visitors already exists. It reminds all tourists that many residents are still marked by the 1982 war, and it calls for prudence and asks visitors to avoid disruptive behavior.

It is complemented by a set of rules and recommendations agreed in 2019 with the Commission of Relatives of the Argentine Fallen in the South Atlantic Islands. These rules focus specifically on the Argentine Military Cemetery at Darwin, were drawn up with guidance from the International Committee of the Red Cross, and are available in English and Spanish.

World.title: US withdraws all its bombers from Britain's RAF Fairford base
World.content:
US withdraws all its bombers from Britain's RAF Fairford base

5th Monday, October 2026 - 01:35 UTC Full article

The base, in Gloucestershire, is a forward operating location for the US Air Force's Global Strike Command

The United States has withdrawn all the bombers it had deployed at RAF Fairford, in western England, a week after the incident near the base that British counter-terrorism police are investigating. Washington gave no reason for the decision.

“While operational security precluded us from confirming the movement of our assets and forces in real time, we can acknowledge now that all US bombers that were deployed to RAF Fairford have re-deployed to their home stations in the United States,” a Defense Department official said on Sunday. The aircraft were B-1B Lancer bombers, around a dozen according to CNN; six B-52s had already returned in late September.

The base, in Gloucestershire, is a forward operating location for the US Air Force's Global Strike Command. Since March, bombers had flown from there in the war against Iran, after the British government approved its use for what it called defensive strikes.

On September 27, five men were arrested near the base after reports of three suspicious vehicles, and on Thursday police arrested a sixth man, a dual British-Iranian national, in London. All six are on bail and none has been charged. Washington publicly criticised the suspects' release, which Prime Minister Andy Burnham defended, citing the strict conditions imposed.

Burnham has said there are “strong indications” that Iran played a part in the incident, without giving details. Tehran denies any involvement. The British government had not commented on the bombers' withdrawal at the time of writing.

World.title: From Group Chats to Matchday Streams: How Sports Communities Grow Online in Indonesia
World.content:
From Group Chats to Matchday Streams: How Sports Communities Grow Online in Indonesia

5th Monday, October 2026 - 00:20 UTC Full article

Indonesia's sports communities no longer depend on one venue or one broadcast. A football supporter can follow club news before breakfast, join a messaging group at lunch, watch the match at night, then debate tactics long after full time. Basketball fans do something similar around IBL clubs, while esports communities add livestreams, creator analysis, team clips, and tournament chats. APJII reported internet penetration of 81.72% in 2026, or roughly 235 million users, and DataReportal estimated 180 million social media user identities in Indonesia in October 2025. That scale gives communities room to form around a club, player, game title, city, or creator. The strongest ones grow because members have reasons to return, not because a page collects the most followers.

A Community Starts with Shared Context, Not an Algorithm

Social platforms can introduce people to a team, but belonging usually develops somewhere more specific. Supporters learn recurring jokes, player histories, rivalries, and expectations about how the team should play. Messaging groups make that knowledge portable: a fan who misses a game can still follow lineup discussion, ticket details, score updates, and post-match analysis. That accumulated context is what turns online communities in Indonesia from comment sections into durable networks.

Public feeds work for discovery, private groups are better for logistics and repeated conversation, and livestream chats capture reactions in real time.

Football Shows How Digital and Physical Support Reinforce Each Other

Indonesian football offers the clearest example because supporter identity existed long before social media. I.League reported about 1.9 million spectators across the 2025/26 top flight, while the return of away supporters in 2026/27 restored travel as a visible part of club culture. Online coordination helps organize meeting points, tickets, transport, and rules before those trips happen. Photos, chants, and travel diaries then bring the physical experience back onto the feed.

Digital discussion can send people to a stadium, and the stadium produces material that keeps the digital community active afterward. Club and league channels are strongest for confirmed information; fan pages add atmosphere, memory, and interpretation.

Basketball and Esports Build Community in Different Rhythms

The Indonesian Basketball League has been pushing the same connection from another direction. IBL said its 2026 season used digital innovation, community activity, and cross-platform distribution to bring the league closer to fans, while the regular season ran 110 games from January 10 to May 10. A home-and-away format gives local basketball communities repeated reasons to gather online and in arenas.

Esports in Indonesia works with an even more digital-native rhythm. Tournament streams produce player clips, creator breakdowns, memes, roster discussion, and patch analysis without requiring every fan to attend a venue. Garena's 2026 Free Fire roadmap, with FFWS Southeast Asia and a 24-team global final planned for November, gives communities a calendar to organize around. The conversation continues between events because balance changes and team news keep producing new material.

Adult Fans Also Meet Betting and Casino Content on the Same Screen

Real-time sports discussion makes adult betting information easier to reach, but community confidence is not evidence. A fan may see a lineup, injury update, and several strong opinions in the same chat before kickoff. Adults checking judi bola should still compare confirmed lineups, home-away form, schedule congestion, recent performance, and odds movement before interpreting a price. A goal, red card, penalty, or late team change can move live odds quickly, while bookmaker margin remains built into those prices. A preset stake helps separate analysis from the emotional speed of a supporter group. Community knowledge can add context, but it cannot remove match uncertainty.

Sports communities share phones with entertainment that has nothing to do with the event being discussed. A halftime break can send an adult user from a match thread toward several unrelated activities. Music, games, shopping, or an online casino can all be reached within seconds, but casino rounds still follow game rules, house edge, and RNG or live-dealer procedures rather than crowd mood or a football result. A winning team does not improve the probability of the next casino round. Keeping those budgets and decisions separate makes the distinction visible. One screen can host several activities without connecting their probabilities.

App installation is another place where social proof can mislead. A link shared repeatedly in a group may feel familiar even when nobody has checked the source. For some adults, a 1xBet download may sit beside score, streaming, and messaging apps, but source authenticity, requested permissions, update status, account security, and payment controls still deserve independent review. An app that handles money requires more scrutiny than one that only displays a score. The useful habit is to know what each service does and what access it requests. Popularity inside a group is not verification.

The Best Communities Filter Noise Instead of Adding to It

Growth becomes useful when a community saves members time. Strong groups surface confirmed schedules, distinguish rumor from club announcements, and know when a short clip needs more context. They also let expertise emerge naturally: one member understands tactics, another ticketing, another local travel, while a creator translates discussion into video.

Football, basketball, and esports already show different community models, yet all reward reliable information, shared identity, recurring events, and room for members to contribute. Platforms will change. A community that can move with its people is much harder to replace.

World.title: Mexico and US send troops to border in joint ‘mirror operation’ after gunfire episode
World.content:
Mexico has sent 500 Army and National Guard troops to the U.S. border in the state of Tamaulipas as part of a joint operation with the U.S. military after U.S. officials were fired upon by unknown elements from the Mexican side on Sept. 26.

Media in Mexico, citing the Pentagon, said the U.S. government announced on Saturday that it had ordered 500 soldiers to the Texas-Mexico border in response to the shooting from Tamaulipas, during which U.S. Coast Guard personnel returned fire.

🚨 Refuerzan la seguridad en la frontera de #Tamaulipas. 500 efectivos del Ejército y la Guardia Nacional fueron desplegados con apoyo de dos #helicópteros de la Fuerza Aérea. El operativo se realizará en cinco municipios fronterizos y deriva de la coordinación entre autoridades militares de #México y #EU. — Azteca Noticias (@AztecaNoticias) October 5, 2026

Later that day, the Mexican Navy said in a press release that the U.S. troop deployment was “part of the mirror operations between both countries, which demonstrate their commitment to strengthening border security, improving detection capabilities, and safeguarding their respective sovereignty.”

On Sunday, the Foreign Relations and Defense Ministries confirmed the twin troop deployments in a joint communique, describing them as part of “Concurrent Operation,” a mission featuring coordination between Mexican and U.S. military authorities with the objective of helping to prevent drug and human trafficking.

The troops patrolling in five Tamaulipas municipalities along the border include 500 Army and National Guard personnel, supported by two UH-60 helicopters from the Air Force, drones and mobile and semi-fixed anti-drone equipment.

In a late Sunday night social media post, U.S. Ambassador to Mexico Ronald Johnson referenced Operation Concurrent, saying that the U.S. Embassy “was helping to coordinate with Mexican forces that are being deployed in the border area where shots were fired against elements of the United States Coast Guard.”

Johnson added that Mexican military commanders are communicating directly with the U.S. forces as they jointly patrol their respective sides of the shared border.

The Navy is also participating via “Operation Saber,” carrying out surveillance and security operations on the northern border with operational deployments of 159 naval personnel, 11 vehicles and two drones via the Naval Sector of Matamoros, Tamaulipas.

The Navy statement said “any cooperation mechanism or exchange of information is carried out through established institutional channels, with full respect for the sovereignty, powers and jurisdiction of each country.”

With regard to last month’s shootout, the U.S. military publication Stars and Stripes (cited by the newspaper Excelsior) said “no injuries were reported … and no damage to Coast Guard assets or equipment was reported.”

An unidentified U.S. officer told Stars and Stripes that the initial shots “came from the Mexican side and Coast Guard personnel returned fire.”

With reports from Excelsior, LopezDorigacom, La Jornada and IMER Noticias

World.title: IMF now predicts Mexico’s economy will grow 1.5% this year
World.content:
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) revised its projections for Mexico’s economic growth on Friday to 1.5% in 2026 and 1.8% in 2027, following a strong second-quarter economic performance, just three months after the organization had lowered this year’s growth forecast to 1.2%.

Achieving the forecasted economic growth will depend on Mexico making a greater effort to reduce its debt through fiscal consolidation, according to the IMF, which warned that growth will likely remain constrained by external uncertainties.

The recent revision follows an official visit for an Article IV consultation mission to Mexico City in September, led by Gustavo Adler, IMF Deputy Division Chief in the Western Hemisphere Department.

Mexico recorded the second-highest quarter-over-quarter economic growth among G20 countries in the second quarter of the year, at 1.4% on a quarter-over-quarter basis between April and June, recovering from a 0.6% sequential contraction in the first quarter.

Better-than-expected figures continued to come into frame in July, with Mexico’s economy growing by 3.3% in seasonally adjusted annual terms, marking the strongest growth of any month so far in 2026.

In its October assessment, the IMF highlighted that Mexico’s disinflation process has continued and headline inflation is near target, although some underlying price pressures persist.

Mexico should focus on much-needed growth-enhancing investment by mobilizing revenues, better prioritizing spending and allowing greater private-sector involvement, according to the organization.

Meanwhile, the government should fortify its disinflation efforts by maintaining a moderately tight stance until there is clear evidence that inflation is moving durably toward the target, the IMF advised.

Achieving greater financial growth will require Mexico to close infrastructure gaps, reduce regulatory burdens and strengthen trade integration, the IMF said. Improving security, combating corruption and lowering informality could also spur growth.

Mexico’s 2027 draft budget focuses more closely on gradual fiscal consolidation than previously announced, and on an upward debt trajectory, the IMF reported.

Nevertheless, the 2027 draft budget anticipates that public debt will increase to 55% of GDP from an estimated 54% at the end of 2026, even as it doubles down on its fiscal consolidation efforts.

With reports from Reuters

World.title: After losing Morena nomination in Nuevo León, Tatiana Clouthier launches new movement of her own
World.content:
After losing the Morena party’s internal contest to become its presumptive candidate for governor of Nuevo León, Tatiana Clouthier announced the formation of a new “movement” in the northern border state.

Clouthier, a former federal economy minister who more recently headed up the federal government’s Institute for Mexicans Abroad, announced the “Todos Con Conciencia” (All With Conscience) movement in a social media post on Saturday.

“Today we had a meeting with the territory and air team,” she wrote on Facebook, referring to her campaign team.

“They reflected and shared their feelings. We concluded that we’re not going for [political] positions but rather to transform #NL [Nuevo León] and we began the #TodosConConciencia movement. Nuevo León doesn’t deserve to be surrendered. Welcome to the revolution of consciences; we’re ceasing to be inhabitants and becoming citizens,” wrote Clouthier, one of six aspirants to Morena’s gubernatorial nomination in Nuevo León.

“Our recognition of the progress with the arrival of the 4T and our support for the president,” she added.

The 4T is the “fourth transformation” political movement led by President Claudia Sheinbaum and supported by the ruling Morena party.

Clouthier’s Facebook post referred to the establishment of a civil society movement rather than a new political party ahead of the June 6, 2027, elections.

The 62-year-old Sinaloa native — daughter of 1988 presidential candidate Manuel Clouthier — is clearly disappointed that she wasn’t selected as the Morena and 4T candidate for the gubernatorial election in Nuevo León, a state currently governed by the Citizens Movement (MC) party under the leadership of Governor Samuel García.

That honor is set to go to Clara Luz Flores Carrales, a former federal deputy and ex-head of the National Public Security System. Last Monday, Flores was designated as Morena’s “state coordinator of the transformation and national sovereignty” in Nuevo León, making her the party’s presumptive gubernatorial candidate. She was Morena’s candidate at the 2021 gubernatorial election in Nuevo León, at which she attracted 14% of the vote to place fourth.

Morena ‘got it wrong,’ says Clouthier

After the meeting with her team on Saturday, Clouthier told the newspaper Reforma that Morena “got it wrong” in selecting Flores as its “coordinator” in Nuevo León. Flores and most of Morena’s other state coordinators were selected via surveys conducted by Morena.

Clouthier told Reforma that the “Todos Con Conciencia” movement “will work from a citizens’ perspective to transform Nuevo León.”

She said that “the common denominator” among the members of her team who attended Saturday’s meeting is that they feel “betrayed.”

Clouthier asserted that Flores “doesn’t represent the values for which we were invited” to participate in Morena’s selection process.

“The party got it wrong. The party didn’t rise to the occasion — neither for our president nor for the movement,” she said.

Sheinbaum: ‘It’s not a matter for the president, it’s a matter for the party’

Asked at her Monday morning press conference about the movement announced by Clouthier, Sheinbaum said it was up to “the Morena compañeras” — party president Ariadna Montiel and party official Citlalli Hernández — to speak to her.

“It’s a matter for Morena,” she said.

“What I think is that a survey is the best way to see who can be the coordinator … of any political party, because it’s what the people think. One can have a perception as a person, but the survey gives you the people’s opinion,” Sheinbaum said.

She said that she had the highest regard for both Clouthier and Flores, and acknowledged that the former wants to speak to her. Sheinbaum said she was willing to speak to Clouthier, but reiterated that Morena’s selection of candidates or coordinators is “not a matter for the president,” but rather “a matter for the party.”

She also said that “personal ambitions should not be a cause of dispute.”

“That’s why I say the best ally is the people, and the best way to know what the people think when there isn’t a direct election is a survey. That’s my opinion,” Sheinbaum said.

With reports from La Jornada and Reforma

World.title: Opinion: What about that demographic dividend?
World.content:
For decades, we’ve repeated this phrase: Mexico is a young country.

For a growing economy, we had an ideal demographic dividend — a large proportion of people of working age compared to those who depend on workers. The INEGI 2025 Intercensal Survey, published last week, should give us pause for thought. Mexico remains a young country and maintains its demographic dividend — but it is being depleted faster than we had anticipated.

Los datos de la Encuesta Intercensal el @INEGI_INFORMA dan información que nos debería llevar a una reflexión profunda sobre el cambio demográfico y sus implicaciones. Sobre eso mi columna en @El_Universal_Mx: https://t.co/njFGKqsJMN — Valeria Moy (@ValeriaMoy) September 30, 2026

The Intercensal Survey shows that in October 2025, our population stood at 130.9 million. The population in private households grew by 0.7% annually between 2020 and 2025, the slowest rate in the series dating back to 1990. In the first five-year period of the 1990s, the growth rate was 2.1% and the median age of Mexicans rose from 29 to 32 years.

The good news: we remain a young population compared to other countries. The median age in the United States is 39 years, in Germany it is 45.5 years and in Japan it is 49.8 years. The bad news: during the same five-year period (2020-2025), Germany’s median age increased by 0.6 years, Japan’s by 2.1 years and Mexico’s by 3 years. Mexico remains much younger, but it is aging faster than both countries.

Those aged 60 and older now account for 14.7% of the population, up from 12% in 2020. The most striking figure, however, is another one: the fertility rate fell from 1.9 children per woman in 2019 to 1.2 in 2024. In Mexico City, it is even lower, at 0.8. The fertility rate is equivalent to that of Japan, although we’ll have to wait and see if the trend holds. Being below the replacement rate — 2.1 children per woman — doesn’t mean the population will start to decline tomorrow, but the direction is clear and the pace is unusual. Mexico has reached this fertility level with a

fraction of the per capita income of those countries.

By the way, what did we do with that demographic dividend — that young population, ready to work and generate economic growth?

The demographic dividend is not an automatic gift; it will generate economic returns only if that population develops its talents, works in productive jobs, saves and contributes to social security. The emigration data are significant. Between October 2020 and the same month in 2025, 1.26 million people emigrated, compared to 803,000 in the previous five-year period. It does not, however, account for households that emigrated in their entirety. Seven out of ten were men, and four out of ten were between the ages of 20 and 29. The tax burden will begin to increase.

In 2025, half of all households had at least one member with non-labor income, compared to 38.5% in 2020, with transfer programs as the main source, followed by retirement benefits and pensions. The proportion of the population enrolled in public health services fell from 77.1% to 72.5%.

More older adults, more transfer payments and less formal coverage — this is a combination that public finances will struggle to withstand. What can be done? A national care system with a real budget is urgently needed. It is the most direct path to enabling more women to have paid work. We must discuss how pensions will be financed, especially in a country with low economic growth. We will also need a health care system prepared to handle chronic diseases as well as quality education.

Demographic data give us plenty of warning. And it’s already warned us.

Valeria Moy, an economist, columnist and director of the think tank Mexican Institute for Competitiveness. Follow Moy on X at @ValeriaMoy.

This article was translated, edited and republished with the permission of Valeria Moy, whose column regularly appears in the newspaper El Universal.

World.title: Tijuana and Mexicali businesses at center of latest US sanctions targeting alleged Sinaloa Cartel network
World.content:
Currency exchange businesses, gas stations and food and beverage establishments are among 25 entities in Mexico sanctioned by the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) last week for their alleged ties to the Sinaloa Cartel.

Last Tuesday, OFAC also sanctioned 21 individuals who allegedly “serve as leaders or facilitators for the Sinaloa Cartel.” Among those people are Ismael Zambada Sicairos, son of imprisoned Sinaloa Cartel kingpin Ismael “El Mayo” Zambada García, and Carlos Alberto Torres Torres, ex-husband of Baja California Governor Marina del Pilar Ávila Olmeda.

“The 21 individuals and 25 entities designated include cartel leader Ismael Zambada Sicairos (a.k.a. ‘Mayito Flaco’), members of his innermost circle, and the Tijuana-based cell leaders, money launderers, and corrupt politicians who permit the Sinaloa Cartel to operate with impunity just miles from the U.S.-Mexico border,” the U.S. Treasury Department (Treasury) said in a statement.

“… As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated or blocked persons … that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC,” Treasury said.

“In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.”

The U.S. sanctions are part of a broad crackdown on cartels by the Trump administration, which has designated the Sinaloa Cartel, the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG) and various other Mexican criminal groups as foreign terrorist organizations. U.S. prosecutors have also filed formal accusations of drug trafficking against various Mexican officials, including Sinaloa Governor Rubén Rocha Moya, who is on indefinite leave.

The sanctioned entities

The 25 sanctioned entities — almost all of which are located in Baja California — are affiliated with eight sanctioned individuals, according to the U.S. Treasury Department.

One of the sanctioned entities is a Culiacán-based hotel business, Servicios Hoteleros Gastelum, which Treasury said is owned by Hildegardo Gastelum García, described as “one of Mayito Flaco’s most trusted advisors, as well as a significant narcotics trafficker.”

Known as “Aldo,” Gastelum García “uses his illicit revenue streams to finance Los Mayos’ war against the Chapitos,” according to Treasury.

Los Mayos, a Sinaloa Cartel faction affiliated with El Mayo and Mayito Flaco, and Los Chapitos, a faction of the same cartel led by sons of imprisoned drug lord Joaquín “El Chapo” Guzmán, are engaged in a long-running dispute. The cartel infighting, frequently described as a “war,” intensified in 2024 after Zambada García was kidnapped by Joaquín Guzmán López, one of El Chapo’s sons, and forced onto a private plane that delivered both men to law enforcement authorities in the United States.

Among the other 24 sanctioned entities are the currency exchange businesses Galerias Centro Cambiario and Mia Centro Cambiario.

The former company, which is based in Tijuana and is also known as “Magic Casa de Cambio,” is owned by Ilia Elizabeth Félix Rivera, “a financial facilitator for Los Mayos,” according to Treasury.

“Félix uses her Tijuana-based money exchange … to work with complicit money exchanges in southern California to collect bulk cash narcotics proceeds from the United States, conduct mirror transactions, and transfer the funds back to Mexico, thus laundering the funds for Gordo Flubber and La Rana,” Treasury said, using the nicknames of two alleged Sinaloa Cartel operatives.

“Magic Casa de Cambio has a long history of ties to the Sinaloa Cartel; the money exchange’s previous owner and Felix’s former husband, Omar Guadalupe Ayon Diaz (Ayon), was arrested for laundering over $45 million through casas de cambio for the Sinaloa Cartel. Ayon was murdered in Tijuana in October 2023 on Gordo Flubber’s orders,” Treasury said.

Treasury said that Mia Centro Cambiario, located in the border city of Mexicali, is owned by “senior Sinaloa Cartel leader” José Ángel Rivera Zazueta. Zazueta uses the currency exchange business to “launder money for the Sinaloa Cartel, as well as a transportation company, Rivos Servicios,” Treasury said.

Rivos Servicios is also among the 25 sanctioned entities.

The other sanctioned entities include Xolo Gas de Baja California; Grupo Gasolinero Nueva Esperanza; The Woods Bar; Raes Restaurante; and Vida Orgánica Tijuana, a business that sells fresh juices and vegan products, among other goods.

Also sanctioned by OFAC for their alleged ties to the Sinaloa Cartel are businesses in sectors such as private security, entertainment and financial services.

The sanctioned individuals

The most notorious of the 21 sanctioned individuals is Zambada Sicairos, aka Mayito Flaco.

Treasury said that Zambada Sicairos, a dual Mexican and U.S. national, “has risen to fill the leadership void left by his father’s arrest and is now the undisputed head of Los Mayos.”

“Mayito Flaco was born in Anaheim, California, in 1982. Despite attempts to obfuscate his cartel bloodlines by filing a U.S. name change to Fernando Sicairos Aispuro in 2001, Mayito Flaco has remained a key figure in the Sinaloa Cartel operations for the last two decades under his father’s tutelage,” Treasury said.

“A federal grand jury in the Southern District of California (SDCA) indicted Mayito Flaco in July 2014 alongside other high-profile Sinaloa Cartel leaders on a variety of drug trafficking and money laundering charges,” Treasury said.

“While some of his family members have been brought to justice, Mayito Flaco remains a fugitive in Mexico. Today, Mayito Flaco retains command and control over Los Mayos and is responsible for directing the group’s criminal activities, including drug trafficking, murder, extortion, corruption, and kidnapping.”

Treasury said that “Mayito Flaco relies on a group of trusted individuals to provide counsel and essential support to his operations.”

Members of that group, including Gastelum Garcia, were among the 21 individuals sanctioned by OFAC last week.

Among the other sanctioned individuals are:

Brothers Jorge Luis Mendoza Uriarte (aka ‘Guero Chompas’) and Francisco Javier Mendoza Uriarte, described as “close associates” of Mayito Flaco.

Lorenzo Castillo Maldonado, who, according to Treasury, “works directly for Guero Chompas and provides protection for Mayito Flaco.”

Marco Antonio Moreno Gómez Santelices, a Tijuana-based associate of “a high-ranking Sinaloa Cartel money launderer” and the owner of “a network of security, real estate, and entertainment companies that also launder money for the Sinaloa Cartel,” according to Treasury. Moreno owns, controls or directs 10 of the 25 sanctioned entities, according to the Treasury.

Luis Alfonso Torres Torres, brother of Carlos Alberto Torres Torres, Governor Ávila’s ex-husband. Five sanctioned companies, including The Woods Bar and Raes Restaurante, are owned, controlled, or directed by Luis Torres, according to Treasury.

Pedro Ariel Mendivil García, former director of public security in Mexicali and owner of gas station operator Grupo Gasolinero Nueva Esperanza.

In its statement, the Treasury Department said that “Sinaloa Cartel-enabled narco-corruption has reached the highest levels of the Baja California state government” and alleged that “[a]t the center of this narco-corruption scheme is the ex-husband of the Governor of Baja California, Carlos Alberto Torres Torres (Carlos Torres) and his brother Luis Alfonso Torres Torres (Luis Torres).”

Treasury said that Carlos Torres, a former federal and state deputy, is “a cartel-linked political operator who has an alliance with El Ruso.”

El Ruso is Juan José Ponce Félix, alleged leader of Los Rusos, a “Sinaloa Cartel Los Mayos sub-faction” that currently dominates the Mexicali plaza, according to Treasury.

Treasury said that Carlos Torres “uses his political influence to facilitate cartel activities and protect the Sinaloa Cartel from government and law enforcement intervention in Baja California.”

“The U.S. Department of State revoked Carlos Torres’s U.S. visa in May 2025 due to his cartel affiliation and work on behalf of the Sinaloa Cartel,” Treasury said. Torres denies the allegations leveled against him.

The U.S. visa of Governor Ávila was also revoked in May 2025. Avilá, who announced her divorce from Torres in October 2025, has denied any criminal wrongdoing, but in a telephone conversation earlier this year she said she was willing to cooperate with U.S. authorities, apparently in order to avoid possible criminal charges in the United States and extradition to that country. An audio recording of the conversation was published by the newspaper El Universal in July.

According to media reports, Avilá, a Morena party governor, was one of various people who originally invested in Vida Orgánica Tijuana, which was established in late 2020.

“A Sept. 10, 2026, rectification of deeds withdrew the governor from the company, just 19 days before the announcement of the U.S. sanctions,” the news outlet Infobae reported.

In its Sept. 29 statement, Treasury said that the “former Mexicali Director of Public Security, Pedro Ariel Mendivil García (Mendivil), also has an alliance with El Ruso.”

Mendivil, who was the public security director in Mexicali between 2021 and 2024, “received bribes from El Ruso in exchange for Sinaloa Cartel control of the Mexicali municipal police to facilitate drug trafficking and carry out cartel enforcement operations,” Treasury said.

“Carlos Torres also reportedly received monthly payments from Mendivil to allow the Sinaloa Cartel to operate with relative impunity in the state. Luis Torres was responsible for taking these bribes and laundering the illicit funds through companies and political campaigns,” the Treasury Department said.

With reports from El Financiero and Infobae

World.title: Mexico and US FDA offer conflicting accounts of recent cyclospora outbreak
World.content:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) concluded its investigation of this past summer’s multistate parasite outbreak, saying its testing had positively identified the source of the outbreak as cyclospora at a farm in Guanajuato that supplied iceberg lettuce to a U.S. distributor.

With that, the FDA declared its inquiry closed, even though its probe did not conclusively determine how the contamination occurred.

In a press release, the FDA said its studies “identified several farms and a processing facility in Mexico that provided recalled lettuce distributed by Taylor Fresh Foods,” adding that there is “strong epidemiological data and traceback convergence supporting the link between this outbreak and recalled shredded iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms de México.”

While the FDA investigations were conducted in coordination with Mexican officials, Mexico’s food-safety regulator Cofepris insists there is no conclusive evidence to attribute the origin to Mexican products.

Cofepris claims tests conducted by its national reference laboratory ​on raw materials, finished products and water from ⁠the facilities in Guanajuato were negative ​for the cyclospora parasite.

It also asserts that environmental ​findings alone do not constitute conclusive evidence that agricultural products were the source of contamination.

The FDA conceded much the same in its press release, saying “[w]hile there is currently not enough evidence to conclusively determine how contamination occurred in this outbreak, the positive samples show that Cyclospora was present in the environment where lettuce was grown and processed.”

As such, Cofepris insists the available analytical data does not allow for a determination that Mexican products were the source of the outbreak.

For its part, Taylor Farms blamed the contamination on an independent grower who is no longer part of its supplier program.

The inspection of the Taylor Farms Guanajuato facility occurred in August and was the FDA’s first in more than seven years following a steep drop in international food safety inspections after the Covid pandemic.

“Our facility remains closed in central Mexico as we work with our research team to implement enhanced safety protocols from the field to the facility,” Taylor Farms said.

This latest inconclusive outcome comes after conflicting findings in July when the FDA admitted that a laboratory test had resulted in a false positive.

The outbreak, which was declared to be over on ​Sept. 11 by the U.S. Center for Disease Control and Prevention, sickened 12,883 people in 21 U.S. states, resulting in the hospitalization of 570 people. It was also linked to two deaths.

With reports from The New York Times, The Guardian, Reuters and La Jornada

World.title: Suspicious package on Mexico City Metro turns out to be churros
World.content:
A ride on the Metro and a freshly made churro are essential Mexico City experiences. An unattended box on Line 7 last week showed why the two should not necessarily be combined.

When a passenger reported an unattended cardboard box on a train traveling southbound from El Rosario toward Barranca del Muerto on Friday, Metro security personnel and officers from Mexico City’s Policía Bancaria e Industrial (PBI) sprang into action.

With the package sitting alone in a train car, the standard protocol for suspicious objects was triggered, according to media reports. Officers reportedly checked it for hazardous materials, explosive devices or other threats.

What they found was churros.

Photos circulated by the Metro system showed an open cardboard box filled with paper-wrapped pastries that appeared ready for sale. No injuries or service disruption were reported.

The train was halted at the Mixcoac station for the inspection, but there were no reports on whether passengers were evacuated from the car in question, much less the entire train.

The discovery quickly transformed a potential security alert into a social media anecdote. Commenters “mourned” the apparent vendor’s lost sales and joked that a forgotten phone would have drawn less concern than the churros did.

Metro authorities advise passengers not to open, touch, kick or move unattended packages, backpacks or boxes. Riders should instead notify security personnel via phone or a train intercom.

Line 7 links El Rosario in the northwest with Barranca del Muerto in the south, passing through the Polanco hotel zone, Chapultepec, and other busy commercial and residential areas of the capital. Before the pandemic, it averaged around 300,000 riders per day.

Churros, fried dough typically coated in cinnamon sugar and sometimes filled with cajeta, chocolate or cream, are a staple of Mexico City’s street-food scene. They are commonly sold hot at markets, fairs and sidewalk stands.

In Mexico City, one of the most well-known spots for churros is Churrería El Moro, the Mexico City-born chain founded in 1935, which has 17 locations in the capital and now three in Southern California: Costa Mesa, Los Angeles and La Habra.

With reports from López-Dóriga Digital, Infobae and Post

World.title: MND Local Los Cabos: A guide to new golf courses and renovations, 2026–2028
World.content:
Los Cabos is the top golf destination in Mexico — indeed, in all of Latin America — with 18 currently operating layouts from a who’s who of famous course designers, ranging from Jack Nicklaus and Tiger Woods to Greg Norman and Tom Fazio. And it continues to burnish its world-class bona fides, with several more high-profile courses in the works, including new designs from Woods (his third at Diamante in Cabo San Lucas) and Fazio (his second at Querencia), as well as the first local effort from four-time major champion Ernie Els, a new 11-hole short course and an expansive renovation at one of the courses that originally helped to establish Los Cabos’ reputation for world-class golf.

RENOVATIONS

One&Only Palmilla Golf Club

After Southern California real estate mogul Don Koll bought the iconic Hotel Palmilla (now One&Only Palmilla) in 1986, he launched Los Cabos as a golf destination in the early 1990s by bringing in Jack Nicklaus — the greatest champion in the game’s history and, by then, already a respected course designer — to craft layouts at Palmilla and Cabo del Sol.

Although the first local course (a modest 9-hole Fonatur layout in San José del Cabo, now Vidanta Golf) would open in 1987, Nicklaus’ attempt to create “Palm Springs by the sea” at Palmilla Golf Club became the first 18-hole test — and the first course of exceptional quality in Los Cabos — when his nine-hole Mountain and Arroyo courses opened in 1993. Another nine, dubbed Ocean, would debut in 1999, bringing the total at Palmilla to 27 holes.

The work currently underway at One&Only Palmilla Golf Club, however, is the most comprehensive in several decades — a “significant investment in the complete transformation of the golf experience at Palmilla,” according to Lloyd Walton, the club’s director of golf.

Upgrades and additions

“We are working alongside Fry/Straka Global Golf Course Design,” he said, “with the objective of respecting the character and legacy of Jack Nicklaus’ original design while comprehensively modernizing the courses, infrastructure and overall golf experience.

“The project includes the transformation of all 18 championship holes across the Mountain and Arroyo courses, including all new premium turfgrass (Tahoma 31 Bermuda grass), completely rebuilt greens to modern USGA specifications, new bunkers and tees, reshaped playing corridors, new cart paths and landscaping, together with a complete replacement of the irrigation and drainage infrastructure. Much of the existing infrastructure, including the irrigation system, dates back to the original development of the golf course more than 30 years ago.

“The Ocean course is also being completely reimagined, creating a new nine-hole Par 3 experience together with an eight-hole short course, adding a completely different dimension to the golf offering at Palmilla. Construction is now underway. During the first phase, the Mountain and Ocean courses are closed, while the Arroyo nine remains open for play. Members can play nine holes or complete the Arroyo twice for an 18-hole experience.”

As part of the extensive renovations for One&Only Palmilla Golf Club members and registered guests at the luxurious One&Only Palmilla resort, the practice facility will also be rebuilt, with target greens and dedicated short-game areas added. The current timeline is for work on the Mountain and Ocean nines, plus the revamped practice facility, to be finished by the end of 2027, with the Arroyo Course completed by the end of 2028.

NEW COURSES

El Once at Palmilla Reserve

This will be the second Par-3 “short course” in Los Cabos. But whereas Tiger Woods Oasis Short Course at Diamante, which opened in 2017, features 12 holes, El Once, as its name suggests, will have but 11.

El Once is being designed by Agustín Pizá, the Mexican course architect best known locally for his redesign of flood-damaged areas of the original Roy Dye-crafted course at the Cabo San Lucas Country Club following Tropical Storm Lidia in 2017.

A signature amenity for Reserve Club Members in upscale communities like Valley Estates, Mountain Residences and The Summit, El Once’s Par-3 pleasures will extend across 1,017 yards on 17 acres at the western end of Palmilla Reserve, with two pins on every green.

“We are reimagining golf with a one-of-a-kind experience with multiple elevated tee areas, target greens and a variety of ways to experience the more casual, social side of golf,” Pizá said. “El Once is the epitome of exciting, ever-changing challenges for every level of golfer, and Landscapes Unlimited is executing construction with trust and precision.”

The first six holes are expected to be ready for play by the end of this year, according to a recent press release.

Campo Alto at Querencia

Tom Fazio’s first course design outside the U.S., Campo Bajo at Querencia, was lauded when it opened in 2000, and its stature has only continued to grow in the years since, with Golf Digest ranking it one of the World’s 100 Greatest Golf Courses in 2016.

Fazio has returned in recent years to design another highly anticipated course at Querencia, Campo Alto, which will likewise be playable only by resident members and their guests at the private upscale community near San José del Cabo.



Notable for its elevated ridges, dramatic canyons and stunning vistas — from desert landscapes to the nearby Sea of Cortés — Campo Alto will open soon, with a grand opening event for members planned for Nov. 6.

Oleada Golf Links

Set at Oleada, an 860-acre resort and residential development on Cabo San Lucas’ Pacific Coast — between Diamante and Rancho San Lucas (home to Solmar Golf Links) in what, over the past decade, has become a hotbed of world-class golf — El’s Oleada Golf Links will offer the sort of links-style challenges (like exposure to the Pacific Coast’s windy conditions) one might expect of the two-time winner of The Open Championship.

The goal at Oleada is to “build a core golf course that harmonizes with nature,” Els has said. “We envision a compact design that drapes naturally on the land, steps lightly on nature’s toes and functions as an environmental steward of the site’s indigenous flora and fauna. With its rolling dunes, elevation changes and majestic desert-meets-ocean setting, I believe we can produce a versatile test that will rank among the best and most beautiful courses we’ve ever built.”

Preview play at Oleada Golf Links began this summer and according to Forbes, the course is expected to formally open for limited public play in November, before ultimately becoming a private course for members, albeit with access for guests at on-site resorts like Grand Hyatt Los Cabos, Golf and Spa and Conrad Los Cabos.

The Legacy Club at Diamante

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Diamante Cabo San Lucas (@diamantecabosanlucas)

The most acclaimed player of his generation, 15-time major champion Tiger Woods transitioned to a new stage of his career when his first completed course as a designer, El Cardonal, premiered at Diamante in Cabo San Lucas in 2014. El Cardonal has since become the site of the only PGA-sponsored tournament in Los Cabos, the World Wide Technology Championship, which returns Nov. 5–8.

But Woods’ impact on Diamante, also home to a superb Davis Love III layout (Dunes Course), was only just beginning. After opening the Oasis Short Course in 2017, he opened a signature restaurant (The Woods Cabo) at the Pacific Coast community in 2023, before beginning work on what may be his most ambitious project yet: The Legacy Course at The Legacy Club.

With membership capped at 250 families, and like all his designs at Diamante (but not his restaurant), private, the Legacy project has been billed by Woods’ TGR Design as “a course that transports golfers from the open desert landscape of southern Baja into a new, secluded environment of lush vegetation—truly an oasis in the desert.”

It’s expected to open by spring of 2027, per Golf Digest.

Chris Sands is a writer and editor for Mexico News Daily, and the former Cabo San Lucas local expert for the USA Today travel website 10 Best and writer of Fodor’s Los Cabos travel guidebook. He has also contributed to numerous other websites and publications, including The San Diego Union-Tribune, Marriott Bonvoy Traveler, Forbes Travel Guide, Porthole Cruise and Travel, and Cabo Living.

Copper — the daily wrap.

Key Facts The CPER copper fund rose 0.86% to US$39.86, tracking US copper futures. It is a proxy, not the spot price (RT).

tracking US copper futures. It is a proxy, not the spot price (RT). BHP asked Chile’s labour inspectorate to mediate with supervisors at Escondida, and a planned strike is on hold for five working days of talks.

Today’s Focus Copper edged higher on Monday after a planned strike at BHP’s Escondida mine in Chile was put on hold. Escondida is the world’s largest copper mine. The CPER fund, which holds copper futures and trades in New York, rose 0.86% to US$39.86. For US investors, the fund and Freeport-McMoRan are the easiest ways to follow the metal. What matters today. A five-day mediation window gives the market a short reprieve, not a settlement.

01 The session in one read

Copper firmed on Monday. The CPER fund gained 0.86% to US$39.86, and Freeport-McMoRan gained 0.78% to US$72.60.

The calming factor was labour news in Chile. BHP asked the labour inspectorate to mediate with supervisors at Escondida, and the strike was put on hold while talks run for five working days.

Southern Copper fell 0.12% to US$205.29.

Assessment — A reprieve, not a resolution MEDIUM The gains were small and came from lower strike risk, not from a change in demand. If the talks fail, the market would have to price the strike again.
