World.title: Iraq pledges $2.7 billion to stimulate economic growth
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi directed on Sunday an executive funding package and measures totaling 3.5 trillion Iraqi dinars ($2.7 billion).

The comprehensive economic program is tailor-made to increase market liquidity, finance important public projects, and help critical industries enduring economic hardship from regional oil trade disruptions.

According to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), one trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $763 million) are redirected from existing Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) initiatives to bolster housing and construction development.

Al-Zaidi ordered that at least another one trillion Iraqi dinars ($763 million) be used to enhance the liquidity of the Trade Bank of Iraq (TBI) and the Industrial Bank to finance industrial and production-related investments.

An allocation of 500 billion Iraqi dinars (approximately $382 million) is designated for the prompt settlement of longstanding governmental debts owed to private contractors and agricultural farmers.

A further investment of 500 billion Iraqi dinars (about $382 million) would bolster the national wealth fund, bringing its total balance to 1.5 trillion Iraqi dinars ($1,14 billion).

The domestic package incorporates structural measures aimed at fostering public-private partnerships, as the Iraqi government aims to strengthen its financial infrastructure following the end of the international coalition’s mission in the country.

World.title: Iraq’s Najaf receive first Iranian plane after US exemption
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Najaf International Airport in Iraq received the first Iranian flight from Tehran on Sunday, carrying over 150 passengers, marking the resumption of air travel between the two countries.

The Iraqi airport received the first flight arriving from Tehran operated by Iran’s Caspian Airlines with more than 150 passengers on board after a suspension that lasted over nine days.

The management of Najaf International Airport announced on Saturday that flights with Iran would resume on Sunday, with three evening flights scheduled, according to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

On Friday, Iraq announced that it had secured a sanctions waiver from Washington allowing Iranian airlines to operate dozens of daily flights to and from Najaf International Airport, with a similar exemption granted to Iraqi Airways.

Last week, all Iraqi airports began complying with the sanctions imposed by the United States on Iran’s entire aviation sector, causing significant disruptions at Najaf International Airport.

The Iraqi Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said in a statement on Friday that an agreement had been reached allowing Iranian airlines, except Mahan Air, to operate 40 daily flights to and from Najaf International Airport.

The agreement follows efforts to facilitate the movement of travelers and visitors entering or leaving Iraq. It also aims to support humanitarian, medical, tourism, and educational initiatives.

World.title: Iraq plans to purchase large oil tankers
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Oil has announced plans to secure funding for the purchase of new tankers—a move intended to bolster export operations and maximize revenues.

This initiative comes amid the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz and shipping disruptions in the Arabian Gulf. However, experts have raised questions regarding the project’s economic viability, cost, and timing, as well as its actual capacity to safeguard Iraqi exports during times of crisis.

Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair confirmed on Saturday that the ministry is coordinating with the government to secure the necessary funds to purchase oil tankers for the Iraqi Oil Tankers Company (IOTC), enabling the firm to carry out crude oil transport operations.

Khudair noted that the ownership of such oil tankers would bolster exports, ensure economic viability, and maximize financial returns.

The IOTC once owned 23 tankers before its fleet dwindled over the past few decades due to wars, sanctions, and the suspension of modernization efforts.

Iraq’s current fleet is limited to six small-capacity tankers used primarily for transporting petroleum products and lacks supertankers for crude oil.

The Ministry of Oil is looking to acquire modern tankers with a capacity of two million barrels to enhance Iraq’s maritime transport capabilities and facilitate the transportation of a portion of its oil shipments.

World.title: Iraq’s parliament to discuss 2027 budget with $48.8 billion deficit
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s parliament is about to start official deliberations on the 2027 federal budget, which has a significant 64 trillion Iraqi dinar ($48.8 billion) deficit.

Following the exclusion of a 2026 budget due to enormous political and economic challenges, the Iraqi Ministry of Finance has expedited the 2027 draft to meet the deadline for parliamentary submission.

The new budget’s total expenditure is projected at roughly 200 trillion Iraqi dinar (approximately $152.6 billion), matching previous record-high spending levels.

The 2027 budget represents a structural transformation by allocating 150 trillion ($114.5 billion) for traditional line items and 50 trillion Iraqi dinar ($38.2 billion) for a new World Bank-coordinated program-and-performance model to measure expenditure efficiency.

Oil valuations in the new budget are based on a cautious benchmark price of $60 to $70 per barrel.

Earlier this year, regional military tensions prompted Iran to temporarily close the Strait of Hormuz, negatively affecting Iraqi oil exports.

At peak times of the crisis, Iraq’s monthly export volumes fell by almost 80 percent, resulting in tens of billions of dollars in lost income and a major public-sector salary issue.

Despite liquidity concerns, the Iraqi government is sustaining massive fixed expenses, including plans to permanently transfer almost one million contract workers and daily wage earners to permanent public service positions.

Additionally, tensions remain over allocations for the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG). According to reports, Erbil seeks a 14 percent share of the national budget based on recent census figures.

The Parliamentary Finance Committee is holding extensive preparatory briefings to look over non-oil income files, currency value, and social safety nets before the final document goes through its first reading.

World.title: German airlines to resume direct flights to Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Transport revealed on Sunday that German airlines will resume direct flights to Baghdad International Airport, operating four weekly flights from Berlin and Dusseldorf.

The ministry said in a statement that Eurowings, a subsidiary of the Lufthansa Group, has announced that it will operate four direct weekly flights to Baghdad: two from Berlin and two from Dusseldorf.

The service, which is set to begin on December 10, 2026, reflects the growing confidence in Baghdad International Airport and the development of Iraq’s air transport sector.

The step is part of the Iraqi government’s efforts to improve compliance with international criteria that apply to the national airline and Iraqi airports, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

The development follows visits by specialized technical and operational delegations to Baghdad International Airport over the past three months to inspect the airport’s procedures and systems.

The visits ensured the airport’s compliance with international standards for security and operations, with the ultimate goal of meeting all flight operations requirements.

The decision represents a crucial advancement in enhancing the presence of European airlines within the Iraqi market.

The decision marks a big step toward increasing the operation of European airlines in the Iraqi market. It opens up new opportunities for European airlines to explore establishing more direct services to Baghdad.

German passenger airlines last flew to and from Iraq in the early 1980s. The new development signals the restoration of passenger services between the two countries. In addition, more than ten German companies have requested to operate flights to Iraq.

World.title: India tops Iraq U-17 Women 14–0 in Asian Cup qualifier
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNew.com) – The Iraqi U-17 Women’s National Football Team endured a difficult opening fixture in the AFC U-17 Women’s Asian Cup Qualifiers on Monday, October 5, 2026, falling 14–0 to India in their Group E curtain-raiser at the MP Selayang Stadium in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.

The Indian side established early attacking dominance, concluding the first half with a commanding 7–0 advantage before adding another seven unanswered goals in the second period.

The encounter was disrupted in the 64th minute—with the scoreline standing at 9–0—when match officials enforced an extended weather stoppage due to heavy thunderstorms and lightning activity around the stadium perimeter before play resumed.

Despite the setback, the young Iraqi squad is preparing for two crucial remaining group fixtures as they continue their qualifying campaign:

Matchday 2: Facing tournament hosts Malaysia on Thursday, October 8, 2026, kicking off at 4:00 PM Baghdad Time.

Matchday 3: Concluding group play against Syria on Sunday, October 11, 2026, scheduled for an early morning kickoff at 10:30 AM Baghdad Time.

The coaching staff will focus on tactical adjustments and defensive organization to regroup the squad ahead of Thursday’s match against Malaysia.

World.title: Nujaba leader defies Baghdad arrests over US flag desecration
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Akram Al-Kaabi, Secretary-General of Harakat al-Nujaba, voiced defiance against the Iraqi federal government following the arrest of several youths who desecrated the American flag during Sovereignty Day celebrations in Baghdad.

In a video published to his personal account on X (formerly Twitter), Al-Kaabi appeared walking across a U.S. flag spread on the ground, accompanied by the caption: “Your crimes are beneath our feet.”

The visual gesture followed a formal statement released by Harakat al-Nujaba on Sunday, October 4, demanding the immediate release of the detainees.

Abdul-Qadir Al-Karbalai, the movement’s military deputy, denounced the arrests in a post on X, characterizing the detention of demonstrators as a “dangerous precedent” that the group refused to tolerate.

The security crackdown originated during Sovereignty Day parades marking the full withdrawal of International Coalition forces from Iraq.

The Joint Operations Command confirmed the apprehension of individuals who trampled the American flag during a public procession in Baghdad, acting upon directives issued by Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi.

The Prime Minister ordered the formation of a formal investigative committee to probe the incident and enforce legal standards governing public parades, coming as his administration pursues a comprehensive state monopoly over arms and works to balance foreign relations following the coalition’s departure.

World.title: US dollar surges past 160,000 IQD in Baghdad and Erbil
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The U.S. dollar surged past the 160,000-dinar threshold across Iraq’s parallel currency exchanges on Monday, October 5, 2026, marking a sharp escalation in exchange volatility and setting fresh multi-month highs across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra.

The rapid upward movement widens the spread against the Central Bank of Iraq’s statutory official rate of 131,000 dinars per $100 to over 22.5 percent, reversing last week’s brief stabilization.

Daily market data showed that wholesale and retail exchange bureaus in Baghdad posted cash selling rates at 160,500 dinars per $100 against purchase bids of 159,500 dinars, registering an increase of approximately 3,000 dinars compared to Thursday’s close.

In Erbil, the commercial capital of the Kurdistan Region, parallel desks quoted selling rates at 160,150 dinars per $100, while buying bids held at 159,750 dinars. In the southern trade center of Basra, greenbacks traded slightly lower but approached the barrier, with selling figures quoted at 159,500 dinars per $100 alongside buying offers at 159,000 dinars.

The sudden rally across domestic currency trading floors comes amid renewed cash-procurement pressure from private commercial merchants and wholesale importers securing foreign exchange outside the official electronic platform.

Currency traders in Baghdad note that heightened regional market friction and temporary lulls in physical greenback distribution have driven rapid retail speculation, pushing exchange rates past psychological resistance levels despite official regulatory efforts to anchor market liquidity.

MUMBAI: Former chief of Atomic Energy Commission of India, Anil Kakodkar, who played a key role in the Pokhran nuclear weapons tests, said the main aim of the US conducting what is called a non-proliferation experiment last week was to assert its global nuclear hegemony and prevent other nations from conducting atomic tests.On Sept 30, the US conducted an experiment which will enable it to detect whether countries are carrying out low-yield nuclear explosions.Kakodkar told TOI, âThe US is attempting to get more sensitivity in terms of nuclear tests detection. There is a generic understanding that nuclear tests will not be carried out. But what if a country executes a test camouflaged?âAsked whether the motive of the test jeopardised nuclear sovereignty of countries, he said the main aim was to assert global US nuclear leadership and stop other countries from carrying out atomic weapons tests.A recent study by Federation of American Scientists says that currently India has 190 nuclear warheads and has enough military plutonium for 140 to 225 nuclear warheads.Anil Anand, considered the father of Indiaâs nuclear submarine programme, quoted US National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA) and told TOI that in the experiment researchers gathered measurements using a broad suite of advanced sensors, including accelerometers, seismometers, chemical and radiotracer samplers.He said, âTogether these measurements will improve scientistsâ understanding of the signatures produced by underground explosions and strengthen USâ ability to detect and characterise nuclear explosive events. âAccording to NNSA, it âconducted a subsurface, non-nuclear chemical high-explosive experimentâ at the Nevada National Security Site. An FB post by NNSA states, âIf foreign countries test in secret, we will know.The goal? Keeping the US one step ahead.â It further said the experiment assumes significance in the context of China supposedly having conducted a nuclear test in June 2020 secretly.âIt takes nuclear expertise to detect nuclear activities, and experiments like these ensure America remains unmatched in detection,â said Brandon Williams, NNSA administrator. âTrump Administration has made it clear that the US will lead from a position of strength. You cannot evade American innovation. With this experiment, we are sending a clear message that under this administration, America will never be outmatched. â

World.title: National Commission for Women seeks gender-neutral childcare leave, shared caregiving by parents
World.content:
Representative image

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Noting that âmotherhood should not become a career penaltyâ, National Commission for Women (NCW) has called for measures to prevent recruitment discrimination against women arising from maternity, as part of a slew of recommendations to govt on laws related to maternity and childcare.In a report â containing 37 recommendations â NCW has also called for a shift to shared caregiving by transforming existing women-centric child care legal framework into gender-neutral child care leave, available to either parent. The commission batted for extension of âgender neutralâ child care leave to private sector, mandatory paid paternity leave, expanding childcare leave eligibility to include third child through graded model, and highlighted the urgent need to make room for 5 lakh creches by 2030.It called for maternity protection to reach women beyond the formal workforce, and recommended extending maternity and childcare benefits to informal, gig and platform workers, noting that over 90% of women workers remain outside effective coverage.NCW has submitted its recommendations to the department of personnel and training (DoPT) and women and child development and labour and employment ministries, with a focus on strengthening Indiaâs maternity and childcare framework through shared parenting, universal maternity protection and family-friendly workplaces.It further recommended parity in maternity benefits for biological, adoptive and commissioning mothers, including increasing leave for adoptive and commissioning mothers from 12 weeks to 26 weeks. It also called for amending Section 60(4) of Social Security Code, 2020, in light of the Supreme Court ruling concerning adoptive mothers, while advocating for a child-centric caregiving framework rather than distinctions based solely on biological motherhood.NCW proposed dividing the existing 730-day child care leave structure equally between both working parents, with 365 days each, or allowing a common pool where both parents work in the same organisation. For children aged 0â2 years, it further proposes a 60:40 shared-care model between primary and secondary caregivers.The commission has also proposed extending child care leave to private-sector employees through a phased implementation model, beginning with large industries and subsequently covering medium and small enterprises.

World.title: Delhi Police ACP Vivek Bhagat’s additional DCP charge withheld amid harassment inquiry
World.content:
Delhi govt modifies Addl DCP charge order after ACP Vivek Bhagat opts out amid harassment inquiry

Order issued before allegations surfaced

Complaints sent to Crime Branch

NEW DELHI: The Delhi government has modified an administrative order assigning the current duty charge (CDC) of Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police (Addl DCP) to 12 Selection Grade DANIPS officers, removing Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Vivek Bhagat from the arrangement after he voluntarily sought to step aside pending an inquiry into allegations of harassment of women journalists.The government said on Monday that Bhagat had requested not to take up the additional charge until the inquiry into the allegations was completed.âVivek Bhagat, ACP, of his own volition, has requested not to avail the current duty charge assignment, till a full enquiry has been conducted in the matter of alleged harassment of women journalists and such enquiry has been satisfactorily concluded,â the Delhi government said in a post on X.âAccordingly, the order dated October 5, 2026, as aforesaid, is being modified and will be reissued with respect to assignment of current duty charge on the eleven remaining officers,â it added.The Delhi government clarified that the administrative process for assigning the additional duty charge had begun well before the allegations against Bhagat emerged.âThe proposal to confer additional duty charge to these officers was initiated on August 25, much before the present set of events.The orders were issued after due approval on October 5,â the government said.Earlier on Monday, Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu had approved the assignment of CDC of the Addl DCP post to 12 DANIPS officers serving in the Delhi Police with immediate effect. Bhagat, who is currently posted as Sub-Divisional Police Officer (SDPO) of Connaught Place, was among those named in the order,.The government also stressed that the CDC arrangement was temporary and did not amount to a regular promotion.âAs stated in the order, the assignment of current duty charge is a temporary arrangement which confers no financial benefit, and no statutory duties of the regular incumbents can be exercised by the officers to whom current duty charge has been assigned,â the statement said.A revised order assigning the current duty charge to the remaining 11 DANIPS officers will be issued, the government said.Bhagat was accused of sexually harassing a woman journalist during an October 3 protest at Jantar Mantar against alleged irregularities in the Election Commission's functioning and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Three women journalists have accused Delhi Police officers of sexual harassment during the protest.The Delhi Police received their complaints and forwarded them to the Crime Branch for further inquiry.In a statement on X on Sunday, the Delhi Police said the New Delhi district had received the complaints and transferred them to the Crime Branch for a âfair and impartial enquiryâ.Following the allegations, several independent journalists also held a protest outside Parliament Street police station, demanding registration of an FIR against the officers, according to news agency PTI.The revised Delhi government order will now cover the 11 other DANIPS officers whose current duty charge assignments were approved earlier.

World.title: Supreme Court agreed to meet, then changed mind: ONOE panel chief

had initially fixed a schedule for an "informal interaction" with members of the Parliament committee examining the bill for simultaneous elections, the panel's chairperson, P P Chaudhary, told reporters Monday, stating that the SC later found it "not appropriate" and called it off, apparently after some opposition MPs criticised the proposed meeting.

He, however, defended the proposal, saying there were precedents of parliamentary committees interacting with SC judges because of their expertise and knowledge of constitutional matters.

Sources said the idea to meet SC judges was first mooted by DMK MP P Wilson, a senior advocate, and was informally deliberated within the committee before it took this up with the SC.

The meeting was fixed for October 6 but the SC secretary general last week informed the committee of the cancellation.

"They (senior SC judges) are of the opinion that as the proposed amendment might become a subject matter of judicial review before the Supreme Court, it may not be expedient or desirable to discuss the issue on the administrative side. The proposed meeting is accordingly cancelled," the secretary general said.

Chaudhary said an email was sent to the Parliament secretariat by SC officials on September 22, stating that a meeting had been fixed on October 6 at 4.30 pm and the law ministry also sent the relevant material to the court.





"After about eight or nine days, some issues were raised publicly. Later, SC cancelled the meeting. If SC felt it was not appropriate, there was no need to pursue the matter. There was no need to create or give further publicity to the issue.

"

World.title: Lakhimpur Kheri case: UP changes public prosecutor; Supreme Court asks Allahabad High Court chief justice to decide on trial judge
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh government informed Supreme Court on Monday that it has decided to replace the public prosecutor in the 2021 case of farmers being mowed down in Lakhimpur Kheri, but said allegations against the outgoing PP by the witness were unfounded.

Former minister Ajay Mishra's son Ashish is an accused in the case.

A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also forwarded the vigilance report on the trial judge, placed before it in a sealed cover, to the Allahabad HC chief justice for appropriate decision. The witness had accused the judge of improperly withdrawing to himself cases under NDPS and SC/ST Act and acquitting the accused.

UP standing counsel Ruchira Goel said the earlier PP was a seasoned prosecutor of 16 years and had not given up key witnesses as alleged.

If doubts cast, better to replace PP: UP counsel

She said there were certain witnesses who had died and others had turned hostile, which he had given up. The bench said it understood the predicament but said whenever doubts were cast on the PP which would affect a free and fair trial, it was better to replace him.

âWe are not casting any aspersion on the professional ability of the earlier PP,â the bench said.

Appearing for Mishra, senior advocate Siddharth Dave accused the witness of attempting to prejudice the trial, the PP and the trial judge by making wild allegations and trying to coerce them to record a conviction.





âEvery now and then, the witness threatens the trial judge and the PP by stating that he will complain to SC,â he said.

The bench said the state had done a commendable job by replacing the PP but clarified, âWe are not saying anything against anyone. Our only concern is that the trial should proceed smoothly in a free and fair manner.â The bench, which is monitoring progress of the trial, was informed that 86 of 131 witnesses in the case had been examined.

World.title: Visa doesn't create absolute right to enter India, says Delhi High Court
World.content:
File photo

NEW DELHI: Delhi High Court has stressed that a foreign national does not have an inherent or legally enforceable right to seek entry into India even if granted a visa. It added the statutory framework does not treat the possession of a visa as creating an absolute and unconditional right of admission into India.Justice Amit Mahajan observed: "The statutory scheme expressly contemplates circumstances in which, notwithstanding possession of requisite travel documents, a foreigner may not be permitted to enter India on grounds, including considerations relating to national security, sovereignty and integrity of India, relations with a foreign State and public health, besides others specified by central govt.""The claim is destined to fail because there is no inherent or legally enforceable right of a foreign national to seek entry," he added. High Court's observations came while dismissing a plea by a Turkmenistan woman, seeking a direction to Centre to furnish a written speaking order giving the reasons for refusing her entry on March 25.

World.title: Only 15% going to work use public transport: NSO
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Long traffic snarls, a common feature on roads across the country, may be linked to how people commute to work. Only 15% of workers use public transport such as buses, trains, trams or auto-rickshaws, while 46% rely on two-wheelers or cars, according to the first-ever National Household Travel Survey (NHTS) by the National Statistics Office (NSO).

Two-wheelers account for 43% of workers' commute nationally and cars for 3%. In urban areas, reliance on these vehicles is higher, with 53% of workers using two-wheelers and 5.7% travelling by car.

28.3% of people reach workplace on foot: NSO

Walking is the second most common mode of work commute in the country, accounting for 28.3% of workers, 10.7% use bicycles. More than a third of rural workers (36%) walk to work, compared with just 14% in urban areas, as per the data.

The survey was conducted between July 2025 and June 2026 and included trips which are longer than 1 km. Travelling to and fro has been counted as two trips in the survey.

The survey showed a worker takes an average of 25 minutes to reach the workplace. In urban areas, the commute takes 27 minutes, compared with 23 minutes in rural areas. The morning commute remains heavily concentrated before 10 am, with nearly 95% of workers leaving home for work then.





In terms of cost, workers spend an average of Rs 785 a month on commuting, with men spending substantially more (Rs 835) than women (Rs 533). The gap widens further in rural areas, where men spend more than twice as much as women â Rs 674 against Rs 307.

Around 88% reach their institutions within 30 minutes, while the average journey takes 23 minutes. Nearly four in five students leave for school between 7 am and 10 am.

Besides meeting the railway ministryâs specific data requirements, the survey is expected to provide insights into how, when and why people travel. âInformation on travel patterns and public transport use will help identify gaps in existing transport systems, assess accessibility, optimise routes and improve service frequency and scheduling,â said NSO in a statement.

World.title: In a record, over 10,000 women clear JEE-Advanced
World.content:

JEE(A): Women accountfor 23% of registrations but 17.8% of qualifiers

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Women's success rate in JEE-Advanced reached a record high in 2026 despite fewer registrations, with over 10,000 qualifying for the first time during this period. Yet their share of IIT seat allotments barely changed, from 20.15% to 20.22%. Of the top 100 rankers, 97 were allotted seats at just three IITs - Bombay, Delhi and Madras - with Bombay alone taking 68.This time, a total 18,861 admissions were made in IITs, with 20% being female candidates. Among the top 25 rankers, 8 candidates each took admission in IIT Delhi and IIT Madras, while six toppers took admission in IIT Bombay.The Joint Implementation Committee report, prepared by IIT Roorkee, shows sharp gains for SC and ST candidates. Including candidates with disabilities in both years, their qualification rates among registered candidates rose by 9.9 and 8.3 percentage points, respectively, to 50.2% and 42.1%.SC qualifiers increased from 12,528 to 15,856, while the ST count rose from 5,017 to 6,379. Both increases were around 27%, faster than the 4.6% rise in the number of qualifiers, from 54,378 to 56,880.Of 43,112 registered women, 10,107 qualified, taking their success rate to 23.4%, against 21.7% last year.In 2025, 9,404 women qualified from 43,413 registrations. Among women who appeared in both papers, the success rate was 24.9%.Women accounted for 23% of registrations but 17.8% of qualifiers, showing that their improved success rate has yet to close the gap with male candidates.Women received 3,814 seat allotments, up from 3,664, out of 18,861 overall. Their qualifying count grew 7.5%.IITs have added seats exclusively for women to ensure they make up at least one in five new undergraduate students. Their share of allotments is only slightly above that level. The report records 3,777 allotments in seats set aside for women and 37 in seats open to all genders. Women are considered first for women-only seats within the relevant category.The small number allotted seats open to all therefore does not show how many could have secured them on rank alone.The qualifying total also includes students eligible for a one-year preparatory course before starting an IIT degree. Their number rose from 9,644 to 13,127, nearly a quarter of all qualifiers. This route is available to eligible SC and ST candidates and those with disabilities against unfilled reserved seats. Those admitted must pass the course before entering allotted degree programme.Excluding this group, SC and ST qualifiers still increased by about 17% and 19%. However, the overall number qualifying directly for degree programmes fell from 44,734 to 43,753. The report records 189 seat allotments for this course. Qualifying for either of these routes does not guarantee an IIT seat; admission also depends on rank, eligibility and available seats.

World.title: Voting begins for high-stakes bypolls in three States, one U.T. | LIVE
World.content:
Voting commenced early Tuesday (October 6, 2026) for byelections to five Assembly constituencies in West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, and Puducherry, as well as to one Lok Sabha constituency in Assam.

In West Bengal, bypolls are being held in the Nandigram and Rejinagar Assembly constituencies. In the high-profile Nandigram constituency, the election was necessitated after Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari won two seats in the State elections earlier this year and decided to vacate this one. In Rejinagar, the BJP, Congress, the AJUP, as well as the two factions of the Trinamool Congress, are contesting.

Also read | 19,000 West Bengal voters to miss bypolls as appeals remain pending in tribunals

In Tamil Nadu, the Assembly constituencies going to polls are Madurantakam (SC) in Chengalpattu district and Dharapuram (SC) in Tiruppur. The two Assembly segments were declared vacant following the resignation of Maragatham Kumaravel and P. Sathyabama. The Thattanchavady Assembly constituency in the Union Territory of Puducherry will also go to the polls

Polling for the byelection to Assam’s Nagaon Lok Sabha constituency is witnessing a triangular contest among the BJP, Congress and the AIUDF.

The counting of votes is scheduled for Friday (October 9, 2026).

World.title: U.S. envoy holds rare meeting with Sudan’s top general in push to seek end to fighting
World.content:
A U.S. envoy met over the weekend with Sudan's top general as the Trump administration pushes for diplomatic efforts to end a war that has created what many describe as the world's largest humanitarian crisis.

Massad Boulos, President Donald Trump's senior adviser for Arab and African affairs, met Saturday (October 4, 2026) with Sudanese General Abdel-Fattah Burhan at a luncheon hosted by Egyptian President Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi on the sidelines of the mid-year coordination meeting of the African Union, according to a social media post.

“These efforts aim to enable Sudan to restore its security and stability, embark on reconstruction and development, and, through an inclusive Sudanese-owned and Sudanese-led national dialogue, transition toward a civilian-led government,” Mr. Boulos wrote on X.

The rare meeting between Mr. Boulos and Mr. Burhan comes as the U.S., Egypt and other intermediaries seek to renew pressure on the warring parties in Sudan to negotiate an end to the fighting that has killed at least 59,000 people, displaced some 13 million and pushed many parts of the African nation into famine.

It also took place less than two weeks after Sudanese Foreign Minister Mohieldin Salim Ahmed Ibrahim accused the U.S. of denying a visa for Burhan to attend the high-level week of the UN General Assembly last month in New York, saying it was a betrayal of Washington's host country obligations. The State Department declined to comment at the time, citing visa privacy laws.

The war in Sudan, which has entered its fourth year, has been overshadowed over the past year by the conflicts in the West Asia.

The African country first plunged into chaos in April 2023 when a power struggle between the military and the powerful paramilitary Rapid Support Forces exploded into open fighting in the capital, Khartoum, and elsewhere in the country.

Although repeated attempts at peace talks in recent months have failed to end the war, Mr. Boulos and other Trump administration officials have said they believe there is still a chance for a regional agreement to secure an immediate humanitarian truce, including certain withdrawals and the establishment of safe humanitarian corridors.

“The United States stands ready to support all efforts leading to a comprehensive dialogue among the Sudanese political forces, leading to a preliminary road map of the future of the Sudan,” Mr. Boulos said in his post.

World.title: Trump says his super PAC will pay for taxpayer-funded ads that sparked backlash for glorifying him
World.content:
President Donald Trump said Monday (October 5, 2026) that he will stop using taxpayer funds for television s glorifying himself that sparked a major backlash, and instead tap his super PAC to cover costs going forward.

In a post on his social media site, Mr. Trump defended the ads, which cost at least $1.5 million in federal funds and have drawn intense criticism. Mr. Trump said they were “positive promotion for our Great USA.”

“This is a rather standard thing to do,” the president wrote, while blaming intense criticism for using taxpayer funds on the ads on the “Radical Left.” But the president added that he'd “decided to do the Patriotic Ads, among others, and pay for them myself, and with money I raised for MAGA, Inc."

That is Mr. Trump's political war chest, which had amassed more than $400 million by the end of July. Mr. Trump has begun to tap it to boost Republican candidates around the country ahead of midterm elections.

Mr. Trump provided no details on reimbursing taxpayers for ads that had already aired, nor on how he would go about having his political organisation pay for such future advertising.

The White House — which had fiercely defended using taxpayer money on spots meant to promote the President — said Monday (October 5, 2026) night that MAGA Inc. will pay for such ads going forward. It did not answer questions about how it or Mr. Trump might prove that his political funds were being used on such future advertising.

Mr. Trump's abrupt about-face came after leaders from both parties criticised using taxpayer funds for the ads.

Legal experts said the ads might even violate federal statutes, including a law against congressionally appropriated funds being used for “publicity or propaganda” and one limiting the partisan political activities of government employees.

The spots began airing in late September

The first ad featured clips of Mr. Trump talking about defeating communism interspersed with onscreen text promoting the “largest tax cuts in history,” “reigniting American manufacturing” and a call to “defend law and order and police.”

Later the same week, a second ad began running. It showed scenic videos of Mount Rushmore with quotes and clips from Mr. Trump's Fourth of July weekend speech there honoring the country's 250th anniversary.

A third, more recent one was virtually identical to an ad for Mr. Trump's Republican reelection campaign in 2024 and showed him walking down a hallway as his voice can be heard warning of a “final battle” against “globalists” and “warmongers.”

All ended with a message: “Paid for by the U.S. Government.”

According to AdImpact, which tracks media spending, the spots had cost at least $1.4 million by the end of September. The actual amount spent could be far more, depending on whether networks classified the ad as a political ad.

World.title: DVAC launches probe into the alleged sand mining scam during the DMK government
World.content:
The ED said in a report that the survey revealed mining beyond permissible limits. The value of the illegally mined sand was quantified at ₹4,730 crore, which the investigators alleged was the proceeds of crime

The Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) has launched an investigation into the alleged ₹4,730-crore sand mining scam which had taken place during the previous DMK government.

A detailed inquiry was ordered on the basis of a complaint filed by the Directorate of Enforcement (ED) which alleged serious irregularities in the mining of river sand across Tamil Nadu, official sources said on Monday (October 5, 2026).

Notice sent

The DVAC has sent notice to the contractors, officials, and others involved in the scam as part of the detailed inquiry which is usually conducted for establishing prima facie offence before a case is registered, the sources said.

The central agency had written to the Tamil Nadu Director-General of Police on June 13, 2024, giving evidence of the illegal sand mining and requesting registration of a First Information Report. A reminder was sent to the DGP on July 18 that year, but no action was taken.

The ED had registered a case of illegal sand mining under the provisions of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002. Investigators collected evidence by deploying advanced scientific techniques with the assistance of experts associated with a company incubated at the Indian Institute of Technology, Kanpur.

The quantum of illegal sand excavated was assessed across all 28 river-sand mining sites with the help of advanced techniques.

The ED said in a report that the survey revealed mining beyond permissible limits. The value of the illegally mined sand was quantified at ₹4,730 crore, which the investigators alleged was the proceeds of crime.

ED relies on GPS data

ED officials also relied on the GPS data provided by the company which had sold the excavators used by the contractors. The technical data — precise GPS co-ordinates, Geo Scanning, and Geo Fencing — provided by the company revealed the details of operational hours and excavation timings of the machines at precise locations.

“The ED compared the data with the GPS coordinates of the permitted quarries and the number of machines permissible under the State government rules. The findings conclusively established that the subject excavators were deployed and operated beyond the demarcated boundaries,” the agency said.

World.title: ECI fact-checks claims on Form 6 following SC observation
World.content:
Amid the political slugfest over Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant’s remarks on Form 6 used for registration of voters, the Election Commission of India (ECI) and the Press Information Bureau came out with a slew of fact-checks.

Following the reports of dissent within the commission over changes made in Form 6, the EC had in a press release on September 26, claimed that the declaration form attached with Form 6 was upheld by the apex court.

As the CJI on Monday made it clear, “any modification to Form 6 has not been approved by us. Let’s be clear,” Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi was quick to target the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) saying, “It is now established beyond doubt that Gyanesh Kumar changed Form 6 illegally and unilaterally. This is just one more proof of him abusing his position to help the BJP. He and everyone else involved in this criminal assault on our democracy will be held accountable.”

Protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar highlights

The EC was, however, quick to fact-check Mr. Gandhi in a post on X. The Commission said the Leader of Opposition’s post was misleading, asserting that the June 24, 2025 order for the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in Bihar was issued with the unanimous approval of the Commission and was upheld by the Supreme Court in its May 27, 2026 judgment. Further, the September 26, 2026 press note, categorically stated that the declaration attached to Form 6 for the SIR had been upheld by the Supreme Court.

The press note of September 26 itself came into focus when Ashutosh Ranka of the Cockroach Janta Party in a post on X claimed that it was no more available on the EC website.

The PIB fact-checked him saying: “The press release dated 26th September 2026 is available in the public domain and has not been taken down by the Election Commission of India.”

World.title: Morning Digest: Voting in high-stakes bypoll in three States, one U.T. today; ECI fact-checks claims on Form 6 following SC observation, and more
World.content:
Voting in high-stakes bypoll in three States, one U.T. today

Voting will take place today (October 6, 2026) for byelections to five Assembly constituencies in West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, and Puducherry, as well as to one Lok Sabha constituency in Assam. The counting of votes is scheduled for Friday (October 9, 2026). Follow live updates here

Jeffrey Archer, U.K. author and politician, dies aged 86

Jeffrey Archer, the best-selling ​British novelist and former politician ‌who was jailed for lying ​in a high-profile ⁠libel case, has died aged 86, his publisher HarperCollins said on ‌Monday (October 5, 2026). Mr. Archer sold over 300 million copies worldwide ‌and was known for pacy ‌thrillers ⁠like his 1976 debut Not ⁠a Penny More, Not a Penny Less and Kane & Abel, with his ​final novel ‌Adam and Eve due to be published this month.

India-U.S. trade deal talks have plateaued; further demands, concessions will be very difficult: FinMin

Negotiations for the India-U.S. trade deal have reached a “plateau”, where it will now be “very difficult” to add to the list of demands and concessions that have been agreed to, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said. Speaking at the Munich Security Conference, Ms. Sitharaman said that India’s imports of Russian oil did not feature as a condition during the negotiations for its free trade agreement (FTA) with the European Union, which is set to be signed in December this year.

ECI fact-checks claims on Form 6 following SC observation

Amid the political slugfest over Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant’s remarks on Form 6 used for registration of voters, the Election Commission of India (ECI) and the Press Information Bureau came out with a slew of fact-checks. Following the reports of dissent within the commission over changes made in Form 6, the EC had in a press release on September 26, claimed that the declaration form attached with Form 6 was upheld by the apex court.

Sheikh Hasina’s activities in India ‘principal challenge’ in planning Bangladesh PM’s visit: Humaiyun Kobir

The “principal challenge” in planning a visit of Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to India are the activities of deposed premier Sheikh Hasina and her team who are based in India, said State Minister for Foreign Affairs of Bangladesh Humaiyun Kobir. Responding to questions from The Hindu on the sidelines of the ongoing Bay of Bengal Conversation organised by Dhaka’s Centre for Governance Studies (CGS), Mr. Kobir emphasised the importance of “strategic autonomy” for Bangladesh and said India has to appreciate the “challenges of a newly elected government” in Bangladesh. He further argued that activities of the exiled leaders of the Awami League will not help India.

SC asks Centre to furnish details on relocation of Central Secretariat Library under Central Vista project

The Supreme Court sought a detailed affidavit from the Union government on the proposed relocation of the 135-year-old Central Secretariat Library in Delhi, which houses over 8.5 lakh books, as part of the Central Vista redevelopment project. The court sought details of the space earmarked for the library, along with its layout plans. The court’s suo motu intervention comes amid reports that the library, currently housed in the Shastri Bhawan complex, was directed on September 17 to vacate the premises by September 30 as part of the redevelopment project.

CEC Gyanesh Kumar has lost public trust and must be removed, say former bureaucrats, activists

A group of senior retired bureaucrats, civil society activists, and academics accused Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of six instances of “proved misbehaviour” and sought his removal, but could not submit their “notice of impeachment” to him in person, as heavy barricading and police deployment prevented the delegation from reaching the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) office. They subsequently emailed their “chargesheet” to the CEC.

SIR: No inquiry yet into bulk Form-7 submissions targeting minority voters

Amid a row where multiple cases have emerged where Form-7, used to file objections and seek deletion of names from the electoral rolls, have been filled in bulk, mostly targeting Muslim and minority communities, Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) V. Anbu Kumar said that “in none of the cases has an inquiry been initiated by the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO)”. Directions have been given to all EROs to take action as per law against those who knowingly make false statements or declarations in writing while filling forms such as Form-7, preceded by an inquiry under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, following an over-five-hour-long protest by Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on October 1.

Set up 24-hour monitoring cells to prevent sexual offences, Supreme Court tells Delhi Police

Underlining the need to take preventive measures against sexual offences, the Supreme Court asked the Delhi Police to set up 24-hour monitoring cells for continuous surveillance of vulnerable areas. The court also asked the police to strengthen patrolling, particularly around educational institutions and public spaces. A Bench of Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran observed that the mere installation of CCTV cameras in public spaces would serve little purpose without continuous monitoring to detect suspicious activity and enable a swift police response.

India, Switzerland identify areas of cooperation in defence, nuclear energy: PM

India and Switzerland have identified new opportunities for cooperation in areas of defence and nuclear energy, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said, following a bilateral meeting with Swiss President Guy Parmelin. Agreements signed by the two sides included one to extend visa durations and student permits. Mr. Parmelin is in India for a three-day visit to commemorate the first anniversary of the Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA) between India and the four-country European Free Trade Association (EFTA), which came into force on October 1, 2025.

BJP says Supreme Court notice to EC, Centre shows independence of institutions

The Supreme Court’s decision to issue notices to the government and the Election Commission (EC) while hearing a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) petition demonstrated a functioning democratic process, negating the Opposition’s charge of an “atmosphere of fear” in the country, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) said. The Supreme Court issued notices seeking responses within a week on a plea challenging the decisions allegedly taken by the EC without the approval of two Election Commissioners.

This is going to be an age of flux, confident we will rise to challenges: Jaishankar

This is going to be an age of flux for the world, with conflicts and tariff volatility making it turbulent, External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar said, underlining that responding to the challenges emerging out of the “choppy waters” is the task at hand. “I'm very confident that we will rise to the challenges,” Mr. Jaishankar said during an interactive session at the 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave in New Delhi.

Most of rural agricultural workers landed in non-productive, informal urban jobs in 25 years: study

A study on productivity gap in farm and non-farm sectors, published in the Journal of Development Economics and authored jointly by economists Rajeer Jat and Bharat Ramaswami, has found that that the labourers from agriculture sector, who shifted to cities, were pushed towards non-productive sectors such as transport and restaurants making no substantial changes either in the economy or in their lives. It said that between 63% and 75% of non-farm workers are in informal employment-dominated industries that are not more productive than agriculture.

Congress claims tribal students headed for Mumbai protest detained; condemns action

The Maharashtra Congress alleged that police early stopped several tribal students who had come to Mumbai to stage a protest at Azad Maidan demanding the resignation of the tribal development minister and detained them. The students’ voices could not be silenced through threats, the Opposition party said, asserting that it would stand with tribal students in the “fight for their legitimate rights”.

Mamata serves legal notice on hospital, Health Department over disclosure of her medical records

Former West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee’s lawyers served a legal notice on the SSKM Hospital, the Bangur Institute of Neurosciences, and the State Health Department over the alleged disclosure of her medical records from 2021 without her consent. The development comes two days after Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, during a press conference, made her medical report public. Mr. Adhikari claimed that Ms. Banerjee had faked her injury.

Sanjay Dutt clarifies after his ‘no peace in India’ remark turns into a row

Hindi film actor Sanjay Dutt has issued a clarification after his remarks that ‘he doesn’t feel peace in India anymore’, made at actor Shekhar Suman’s talk show, sparked a controversy. The clarification by the actor comes two days after his episode was aired on Shekhar Tonite Youtube channel, which drew widespread backlash from social media users. Taking to X, the actor wrote, “I would like to clarify that it was never my intention to hurt, offend, or disrespect the sentiments of any individual, community, or institution”. He stated that his remarks were made as part of a scripted conversation intended to be light-hearted and humorous.

Tejashwi Yadav alleges electoral fraud in Bihar, says CEC acting at BJP’s behest

INDIA bloc leader and Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) national working president Tejashwi Yadav shared details of the action plan against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged illegalities in the special intensive revision (SIR) exercise. On October 7, Bihar leaders of the INDIA bloc will launch an Aakrosh March against the CEC, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah at the block level. On October 8, they will hold a sit-in protest in all districts, followed by a demonstration at the Lok Bhavan in Patna — led by the Leader of the Opposition Mr. Yadav.

Trump cites Indian election that didn’t happen to call U.S. electoral process ‘corrupt’

In an apparent faux pas, U.S. President Donald Trump mentioned India in a social media post to claim that the electoral process in the U.S. was “corrupt”, when there were no elections in India, and the post clearly appeared to be about the presidential election in Brazil. The message was later corrected. In a Truth Social post, Trump claimed that “125 million people voted in India’s Presidential elections and the results came out shortly after the vote closed”.

U.S. accuses California woman of spying for China, surveilling Taiwan leader’s son

U.S. ⁠authorities arrested a California woman and accused her of spying on a son of Taiwan's President at the behest ‌of Chinese officials, the FBI said. The FBI arrested Wanying Zhang, also known as Heather, at Los ‌Angeles International Airport before her ‌planned departure ⁠to China, the agency said in a ⁠statement. Authorities charged Zhang, 34, of Irvine, California, with acting as an unregistered foreign agent.

OpenAI's Sam Altman says AI benefits warrant accepting some risks

OpenAI Chief Executive Sam Altman said the benefits of artificial intelligence justify accepting some risks and argued the technology ​should remain broadly accessible to the public. “We believe that the world ‌should accept some bad things happening for the benefits of ​this technology and people having the agency,” Altman ⁠said in an interview with Politico’s technology-focused newsletter Decoded.

World.title: Delhi Govt withholds current duty charge of Additional DCP given to officer accused of sexually harassing journalist
World.content:
The current duty charge (CDC) of the post of Additional Deputy Commissioner of police to Assistant Commissioner (ACP) Vivek Bhagat — accused of sexually harassing a woman journalist during a protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar in New Delhi — has been withheld, the Delhi government said late on Monday (October 5, 2026).

A Delhi government order earlier in the day assigned CDC of additional DCP to 12 DANIPS officers including Mr. Bhagat.

Later, the Delhi government, clarified that the October 5 order assigning current duty charge of Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police to 12 DANIPS officers was based on a proposal initiated on August 25, well before the present allegations.

Government of NCT of Delhi order dated October 5, 2026, wherein current duty charge of the post of Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police has been assigned to 12 officers of DANIPS is being modified in respect of Shri Vivek Bhagat, ACP. The proposal to confer additional duty charge to these officers was initiated on August 25, much before the present set of events. The orders were issued after due approval on October 5, 2026. As stated in the order, the assignment of current duty charge is a temporary arrangement which confers no financial benefit, and no statutory duties of the regular incumbents can be exercised by the officers to whom current duty charge has been assigned. However, Shri Vivek Bhagat, ACP, of his own volition, has requested not to avail the current duty charge assignment, till a full enquiry has been conducted in the matter of alleged harassment of women journalists and such enquiry has been satisfactorily concluded. Accordingly, the order dated October 5, 2026, as aforesaid is being modified and will be reissued with respect to assignment of current duty charge on the eleven remaining officers. — Delhi Government (@DelhiGovDigital) October 5, 2026

The order stated that the assignment was a temporary arrangement carrying no financial benefit and did not confer the statutory powers of a regular incumbent. As per Delhi government, ACP Vivek Bhagat subsequently requested that he not be given the current duty charge until a full enquiry into the allegations of harassment of women journalists was completed.

The order is being modified accordingly, with the charge to be assigned to the remaining 11 officers.

Earlier in the day, ACP Bhagat — accused of sexually harassing a woman journalist during the October 3 protest at Jantar Mantar — was assigned the rank of additional DCP, drawing sharp reaction from various quarters.

Three women journalists accused Delhi Police officers of sexual harassment during the October 3 protest against alleged irregularities in the Election Commission's functioning and Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

The Delhi Police has received the complaints and forwarded them to Crime Branch for further inquiry.

(With PTI Inputs)

World.title: Saudi-backed Yemeni forces expel the Houthis from several areas around key strait, officials say
World.content:
Forces of the Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen have recaptured several key areas around Bab el-Mandeb Strait from Iran-backed Houthi rebels, Yemeni officials said Monday.

The officials said forces allied with the internationally recognised government have retaken the crucial town of Dhubab just north of the strait. They also captured the towns of Bab and Hadeid, said the officials, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak to reporters. Witnesses said they saw government tanks and forces entering the towns.

The government push came as part of a major offensive launched early Monday (October 5, 2026) under air cover by a Saudi military coalition.

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters that it was expected that the Saudi-backed government in Yemen would hit back at the rebels to reclaim territory. Asked if the Saudi-led coalition coordinated the action with the United States, Rubio said that Saudi Arabia and the US have a defence agreement but wouldn't offer more details.

The Yemeni government was ousted from some of its territory by a Houthi campaign and the Saudis have come under attack, and “they have a right to defend themselves,” Mr. Rubio said.

The U.S. has provided support to Saudi Arabia in its ongoing campaign against the Houthis, according to a regional official and a U.S. official who spoke on condition of anonymity because they weren't authorised to speak to reporters. U.S. support included intelligence sharing, target identification and planning for the offensive, said the officials.

The U.S. had supported the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis early in the Yemen war, before quitting the coalition in recent years.

The U.S. Embassy in the Saudi capital of Riyahd warned U.S. citizens on social media to be vigilant about possible drone or missile attacks.

The offensive came just after the rebels said they had captured more territory in the southwestern part of Yemen, taking a key town in a blow to the Saudi-backed forces as they advanced toward a strategic provincial capital in the region.

The Saudi-led coalition spokesman, Maj. Gen. Turki al-Malki, said 100 fighter jets were providing support to the forces of Yemen's internationally recognized government fighting against the Houthis. He said the coalition has secured “air protection” of the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait and destroyed hundreds of Houthi targets as part of the ongoing campaign.

World.title: Pakistan, Turkiye, Saudi Arabia agree to rapid force deployment in the kingdom under Makkah pact
World.content:
Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye have agreed to deploy military forces and capabilities rapidly in the kingdom, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Monday following an emergency meeting of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in Riyadh.

The three countries held an emergency meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC) of the Makkah Defence Alliance to address the security developments and threats facing Saudi Arabia, the FO statement said.

“The committee decided to move immediately to the practical implementation of the collective defence commitments and to take the necessary measures to provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment in the kingdom, in accordance with the approved arrangements and the national legislation of the parties, thereby enhancing readiness, military integration, and the collective capacity to confront and counter threats,” it added.

While the statement did not specifically name any threat, the development comes against the backdrop of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia in the Yemen conflict.

In the Riyadh meeting, the three members of the Makkah Defence Alliance condemned “in the strongest terms” the attempted targeting of Makkah and Madina, as well as the continuing attacks targeting cities and civilian and economic facilities in Saudi Arabia, reaffirming their “unequivocal rejection of any attack or threat against the kingdom’s security and territorial integrity”, the statement said.

For their part, Pakistan and Turkiye commended the “vigilance and readiness of the Saudi armed forces, as well as the professionalism and high level of competence they have demonstrated in countering the threats and attacks facing the kingdom and in safeguarding its security and territorial integrity”, the FO said.

The SPDC reviewed the outcomes of the political and military consultations preceding the meeting and approved the recommendations submitted to it, affirming that the Makkah pact embodied a firm commitment to collective defence and a unified position in confronting threats, it said.

Moreover, the three countries affirmed that the security of each member of the alliance was an “integral part of the collective security of the three countries, and that translating the Makkah Agreement for Joint Defence into practical measures demonstrates the credibility of the commitment to collective defence, strengthens the effectiveness of deterrence, and reaffirms the unity and determination of our three countries to defend their security, sovereignty, and territorial integrity, in accordance with the provisions of the agreement”.

Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, who was part of Pakistan’s delegation in the meeting, joined Geo News programme ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Saath’ via telephone and said Saudi Arabia had made “gains and recovered some areas” in Yemen in the ongoing fighting with the Houthis.

When asked about a possible operational role by Pakistan and Turkiye, the defence minister replied that both nations had a “presence in theatre”, but only Saudi troops were involved in combat operations.

“Whatever assistance they require is being provided. But right now, the Turkish and Pakistani armies are playing a supportive role,” he said, noting that Pakistan was involved in reconnaissance.

The defence minister said the meeting was primarily focused on formalising the Makkah alliance’s operational structure.

“The organisational structure of the alliance was formalised during today’s meeting,” he said.

As part of the institutional development of the Makkah alliance, the SPDC decided to appoint Pakistan’s Lieutenant General (Retd) Nauman Mahmood as the first secretary general of the alliance for a three-year term, the FO statement said.

“The parties welcomed him, wished him every success in the discharge of his duties, and expressed their confidence in his contribution to advancing the alliance and achieving its objectives,” it added.

In an earlier statement on social media platform X, the FO said Pakistan’s delegation to the meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC) included Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and Asif.

“The meeting will also be attended by the respective ministers of foreign affairs, ministers of defence, as well as chiefs of general staff of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and the Republic of Türkiye,” the FO added.

The Makkah defence pact , signed on Aug 7, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empower its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

The SPDC meeting under it has been held as Yemen’s Saudi-led coalition government launched a major military campaign on Sunday to recapture territory held by the Houthis.

Fighting between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis showed no signs of abating over the weekend, with the Houthis saying the kingdom had launched dozens of strikes on Yemen’s capital Sanaa, after which they attacked an Aramco facility with ballistic missiles and drones south of Riyadh.

The foes have traded strikes since the Houthis seized all of Yemen’s Red Sea coast and took control of the Bab al-Mandeb strait in a lightning offensive.

On Sept 25, the military chiefs of Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia met in Riyadh for urgently convened talks under the pact in light of the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

On Sept 18, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry had expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia, saying Pakistan will go to “any extent” to defend the Gulf state, adding that Islamabad’s commitment to the kingdom’s security is “unconditional”.

World.title: IMF talks likely to clear way for $1.2bn disbursement
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Pakis­tan’s ongoing talks with a visiting staff mission of the International Monet­ary Fund (IMF) are set to conclude on a positive note later this week, paving the way for the disbursement of about $1.2 billion under two concurrent progra­mmes — the $7bn Exten­ded Fund Facility (EFF) and the $1.4bn Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF).

Informed sources said the two sides were now finalising the Memor­andum of Econ­omic and Fiscal Policies (MEFP) after covering the substantive parameters of the biannual review.

Following the completion of the draft exchanges, the staff mission, led by Ms Iva Petrova, is expected to conclude its visit in the next couple of days, official sources said. There were no new demands from the Fund, except for makeup adjustments to bridge past slippages. The revenue target remains unchanged, with a greater focus on achieving the half-yearly target following robust collection in the first quarter, which exceeded the target.

The development comes as the authorities struggle to finalise the liquefied natural gas (LNG) import plan for the upcoming three winter months — December to February — amid a challenging supply situation stemming from the US-Iran conflict.

The gas companies and the petroleum division had sought at least 22 import cargoes for the three-month period, but the task force on energy, led by Lt Gen Zafar Iqbal, has promised no more than 10-12 cargoes of around 100 million cubic feet each on a best-effort basis, using all diplomatic and logistical channels.

The plan will be presented to the prime minister for approval, given the involvement of around $100m per spot cargo and the requirement for consent from the Ministry of Finance and the State Bank of Pakistan.

The matter has assumed greater importance because the LNG import plan will affect the current account targets agreed upon by the Ministry of Finance and the IMF. Sources, however, indicated that actual LNG imports may not exceed seven to eight cargoes over the three winter months, given prevailing market conditions, which would bring the outcome closer to the Ministry of Finance’s desired level.

The two sides have agreed to expedite groundwork for targeted subsidies in the gas sector through the social protection programme to contain gas-sector circular debt and move BISP-based subsidies for the poorest consumers in the power sector into the implementation phase, starting January next year following the introduction of the revised base tariff.

The distribution companies have already filed tariff petitions during the course of the talks to demonstrate their preparedness to the IMF team, the sources said.

The government has assured the Fund of plans to reduce cross-subsidies from the industrial sector and contain gas-sector debt, which has now reached Rs3.6 trillion and continues to rise. This includes principal payables of around Rs1.8 trillion and almost an equivalent amount in accrued interest and late-payment surcharges.

The gas companies have reported that the introduction of a protected category for domestic consumers, involving gas prices of Rs200-350 per mmBtu, has aggravated the pricing gap and, consequently, increased circular debt. Only four of the 12 consumer slabs covered the cost of gas supply during the winter months, while the remaining eight remained below breakeven rates for around eight months despite the imposition of substantial fixed charges.

Although these measures are not being defined as prior actions, the authorities may have to take a few steps between the conclusion of the ongoing IMF talks and the scheduling of the Fund’s Executive Board meeting to ensure smooth processing of Pakistan’s case for the disbursement of $1.2bn and seek waivers for a couple of unavoidable slippages that had already occurred against the end-June 2026 targets.

An IMF structural benchmark committed by the government requires a major policy reform by end-January 2027 to replace the budgeted tariff-differential subsidy and cross-subsidy system with a targeted, budgeted subsidy framework for low-income consumers through BISP.

The World Bank is assisting the government in linking power consumers to the National Socio-Economic Registry. The government has undertaken to complete the technical linkage, along with validity checks, by end-November to determine eligibility criteria.

The IMF is now also pushing for greater transparency in the Inland Freight Equalisation Margin (IFEM), which facilitates uniform petroleum pricing across the country.

Published in Dawn, October 6th, 2026

World.title: After breakdown of talks with govt, PTI says reconciliation not possible without including Imran
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: PTI leaders on Monday declared that reconciliation between their party and the government was not possible without including incarcerated party founder Imran Khan in the dialogue process.

Narrating the opposition’s stance on why the talks with the government failed over the weekend, PTI’s secretary general, Salman Akram Raja, presented his party’s demand that Imran be included in any future political dialogue.

“Only [Imran] has the capability to bridge the gulf that has developed between the state and the nation,” Raja said during the press conference held at Khyber Pakhtunkhwa House in Islamabad.

“Imran Khan is very important for us and we had every right to seek his opinion, but it was not allowed,” Raja said.

The PTI leader said that another reason for the failure of the talks was that the government was not willing to pursue a collective strategy against terrorism. Raja told the media that the PTI had entered into the negotiations with sincerity and was serious about addressing the issues.

“Even on the second day, we were hoping that another round of talks would streamline things,” he said.

Describing the reasons for talks failing, Raja said: “We were being pushed to support the government over every action being taken regarding terrorism in KP.”

He added that the PTI had demanded that the government respect the recommendations and opinions of a jirga held by the KP Assembly, in which political parties and stakeholders had participated.

The jirga had recommended solutions to the problem, the opposition delegation had told the government, according to Raja.

The delegation had also asked the government to consider the opinions of tribal leaders, Raja said.

He said the PTI had suggested the agreement should mention that a collective decision would be made regarding terrorism, but the government had said it would not put it down on paper.

“We were told that a unanimous strategy against terrorism would not be developed and it would not be included in the agreement,” he said. Raja said that the government had deliberately complicated the situation.

“It is a fact that the current issues can only be addressed by Imran Khan.

“We had demanded that Imran Khan and his opinion should be included in all issues, which is why we demanded a meeting of party leaders with him,” Raja said.

The two rounds of talks between the government and the opposition held on Friday and Saturday did not yield positive results, with counterterrorism policies and access to Imran emerging as two major sticking points.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, who was part of the process, on Sunday singled out KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi for the failure of talks, saying that he changed the agreement.

Separately, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said the PTI representatives came for talks but were unwilling to abandon their “double standards and hypocrisy”.

For its part, the PTI said it wanted immediate access to party founder Imran for consultations, and even agreed to forgo other demands for this. However, the government declined to make access to Imran part of the proposed agreement, the opposition party claimed.

Addressing the failed talks, Minister for Kashmir Affairs and Gilgit-Baltistan Amir Muqam said on Monday that the government’s delegation had suggested that both sides “be on the same page” about terrorism.

Following the failed talks, the PTI went ahead with its protest march on Sunday despite warnings from the federal government.

KP Assembly speaker to summon security committee meeting

Against this backdrop, KP Assembly Speaker Babar Swati said he was going to summon another meeting of a special committee on security, which was constituted after a peace jirga in the assembly in November last year.

“I am again summoning a meeting of the special committee. I wish for the relevant authorities and institutions to sit together on this important matter,” he posted on X.

He emphasised that it was important to consider this process initiated by the KP Assembly before the Centre held the former responsible for the law and order situation in the province.

Swati recalled that political parties had issued a joint statement after the Nov peace jirga, in light of which the assembly had constituted a special committee on security. The committee, he said, was briefed by the provincial police chief, the Counterterrorism Department, the KP home additional chief secretary, the Home Department, the KP chief secretary and other relevant provincial institutions.

“We also informed the leadership in the Centre about this process and sent letters to the prime minister, the Senate chairman, the National Assembly speaker and the interior minister, informing them that the assembly was moving towards [formulating] comprehensive parliamentary recommendations,” he said.

Swati said just one important official, the Peshawar corps commander, was left to brief the committee.

“I had spoken to the Peshawar corps commander and he had assured me of his participation. However, the meeting has yet to take place,” he added.

“I am again summoning a meeting of the special committee. I wish for the relevant authorities and institutions to sit together on this important matter.

“Whatever we have heard, seen, and whatever facts have come before the committee — they will present their stance; the relevant institutions will present theirs,” Swati said.

Following that, he continued, the committee would formulate its recommendations, which would be presented before the assembly.

“After the assembly’s approval, the recommendations will be forwarded to the provincial and federal governments so that responsibility, policy and practical measures are clearly [stated].”

The speaker said the people of KP wanted peace and called for the relevant parties to play their respective roles in moving towards a collective solution.

“We have to find a way while collectively implementing the National Action Plan, clarifying the responsibilities of relevant institutions,” he added.

Later, it emerged that Swati had sent a letter to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, urging the implementation of the joint declaration issued by the assembly’s peace jirga in 2025.

In the letter, a copy of which is available with Dawn, Swati noted that a special committee on security had been constituted in the province to prepare a comprehensive report on the security situation after “due consultation with all relevant stakeholders”. This committee actively sought engagement with the KP governor, the provincial government, political leadership, elected representatives, the Armed Forces, and other relevant security institutions regarding the law and order situation in the province.

A peace jirga was held on Nov 12 last year in continuation of this process, Swati added, which was attended by over 30 leading members of political parties, elected representatives and other stakeholders.

“After detailed deliberations, the jirga adopted a joint declaration reflecting the collective concerns and aspirations of the people of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, particularly with regard to terrorism, security, and the restoration of lasting peace,” the letter stated, adding that this declaration had already been shared with the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) for consideration.

Swati’s letter further noted that the committee also received detailed briefings from provincial government departments and institutions about “the prevailing security situation, the nature of threats confronting the province, and the measures being undertaken to address them”.

It clarified that the committee’s objective in seeking such insight was not to interfere in the operational responsibilities of security agencies, but rather to keep elected representatives fully informed on matters that affected their constituents.

“The special committee has prepared a report on the security situation in the light of these briefings,” Swati said, noting that this was intended to be forwarded to the federal government for inclusion in the National Action Plan as well as to the KP government as part of effective counter-terrorism measures.
